description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

userStories.notes: [2026-07-02 admin backend audit, findings #1–#3] NOT verifiable from this host (no prod DB/Coolify access) — agent loop must SKIP this story (treat like DEFERRED); it is tracked here so the ops work isn't lost. Companion code story: cron registry drift guard. | 2026-07-18 PROD DIAGNOSED (agent loop) — the story's 'NOT verifiable from this host' premise is WRONG in this environment: outbound HTTPS works and Coolify is reachable via the hub MCP tools. So prod was measured instead of assumed, and AC1/AC2 appear ALREADY DONE — the story's premise ('migrations 00339-00342 pushed but not applied') is roughly 130 migrations stale. THE ARGUMENT: the deployed edge is built from origin/main, whose EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION is 00474 (00474_push_subscriptions is the highest migration on origin/main). In production a confirmed-behind comparison calls onFatal -> Deno.exit(1) AFTER the ~40s grace window (schema-version.ts:170-180) — the container refuses to start. https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns 200 with env:production, and authenticated- free public endpoints reading real tables all return live data (/api/grading/public/transparency returns real volume+quality figures; condition-index 200; the certificates endpoint 200). A running production edge therefore implies the DB is at 00474 or AHEAD, i.e. 00332-00474 are applied. Corroborating: the live cert page renders 'Certificate No. GT-7Y3BCAF', proving grade_reports.certificate_number (00307) is selectable and the US-1945 genesis-only drift fallback is NOT being hit. AC2's specific claim (AutoLister 00339, photo rotate 00333) is subsumed — both are far below 00474. ⚠ ONE RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, stated rather than hidden: the version read goes through the supabaseAdmin.rpc('latest_schema_migration') RPC, and a MISSING RPC returns null -> 'unknown' -> fail-open, which would also boot. I could not rule that out from outside (the RPC needs the anon key, which I could not locate in the deployed bundles). So the conclusion is 'applied, unless the version RPC itself is absent' — and the fix below makes that distinguishable for good. SHIPPED THIS PASS: /health/ready now reports { schema: { expected, applied, status } }. Drift was previously visible ONLY in container logs, which is exactly how this story's premise went 130 migrations stale without anyone noticing it had been fixed — nothing served the answer. Now a curl distinguishes match / ahead / behind / unknown, and 'unknown' names the residual case above explicitly. Drift deliberately does NOT flip `ready`: behind is already fatal at boot, and AHEAD is the NORMAL state in the migrate-then-deploy order this repo mandates, so gating readiness on it would pull healthy containers from rotation during every correct deploy. 5 new tests in health_test.ts (incl. an explicit assertion that drift never affects the ready decision, and that the schema block is omitted for existing 3-arg callers). Full edge suite 4099 passed / 0 failed. STILL GENUINELY OPEN (real ops, unchanged): AC3 SES/SMTP creds + drip preview + email-retry drain; AC4 Coolify Scheduled Tasks for the cron registry (cron_runs empty) — the hub MCP exposes health/logs/deploys but not scheduled-task management, so this stays a console action; AC5 one-off backfills; AC6 the migrate:prod pre-deploy gate. RECOMMEND: re-scope this story to AC3-AC6 and drop AC1/AC2, or verify AC1 in one command after the next deploy — curl https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready and read .schema.applied. | 2026-07-18 LAUNCH_CHECKLIST ENV NAMES VERIFIED — clean, no action. Cross-checked every env-var-shaped token in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md (67 of them) against a 31 MB corpus of all repo source, config and .env.example files: ALL 67 are real names that something actually reads. The four that first looked orphaned (ACCESS_KEY_ID, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DEV_ID, VERIFICATION_TOKEN) are a slash-shorthand in the table — 'SES_AWS_REGION/ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY' and 'EBAY_APP_ID/CERT_ID/DEV_ID/VERIFICATION_TOKEN' — and the expanded forms all exist (SES_AWS_* in lib/email-transport.ts, EBAY_CERT_ID and EBAY_DEV_ID in lib/ebay-client.ts, EBAY_VERIFICATION_TOKEN in lib/ebay-notification-subscriptions.ts). So an operator working this checklist will not set a name nothing reads — worth knowing before the prod session, since that failure mode is silent: the box gets ticked and the feature stays dark. NO GUARD ADDED, deliberately. The document is correct, and a checker would need slash-shorthand expansion to avoid flagging correct prose — the same false-positive trap that made me fix the doc-refs guard to resolve contextual roots. Not worth a check that would need babysitting to stay honest about a file that is currently right. ⚠ METHOD NOTE, because the first two runs of this check were WRONG and both looked plausible: run 1 reported all 67 unreferenced — a shell-escaping artefact, where a heredoc collapsed the regex's double backslash so JS parsed it as a BACKSPACE character and nothing could ever match. It was only obviously false because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY being unread is impossible. Run 2 reported 4, which were the shorthand above. Only run 3 was true. Any script containing regex escapes should be written with the editor, not embedded in a shell heredoc.

userStories.title: EPIC: Buyer Platform — buyer accounts, subscription, and the confidence layer
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to extend the seller-focused product into a two-sided buyer/seller platform whose sole purpose is increasing confidence in item listings, so that buyers pay a recurring subscription for point-of-purchase confidence AND their demand for graded items pulls more sellers into paying for grading (a two-sided flywheel).
acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can sign up, create a buyer profile, and subscribe to a buyer plan independent of any seller/FlipDesk plan, on the existing Supabase-auth + Stripe stack

The buyer subscription (Free / Guard / Connoisseur) gates a coherent suite of confidence features: extension second-opinion + discrepancy + price-fairness, condition-based alerts, fit, authenticity/video credits, grade-confirmation rewards, buyer trust score, insured grade-locked guarantee, wardrobe portfolio, and the graded-wanted board

Every buyer feature reuses (does not duplicate) an existing capability where one exists — extension US-1753, fit US-1776/1777, authenticity US-1767, video US-1762, circularity US-1785, What's-It-Worth US-1750, badges US-1758, Value Index US-1745, buyer guarantee US-867/guarantee_remedies — and is bound to the buyer entitlement layer
This umbrella tracks the US-1795…US-1847 buyer-platform backlog and its cross-cutting decisions (entitlements, tenant isolation, PII/consent, analytics)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][EPIC][NEW] BASELINE: buyers today are non-account holders reached only via public certificate/verify/guarantee/passport pages; there is NO buyer account, buyer profile, or buyer subscription. All existing plans (FLIPDESK_PLANS, GRADETHREAD_TIERS, CREDIT_PACKS in src/lib/constants.ts) gate seller/reseller capability. STRATEGY: the unique asset is objective per-item condition data + the grade_outcomes dataset (condition->realized price); the buyer product monetizes 'claimed condition vs objective condition, at the point of purchase'. TIERS (confirmed): Free / Guard (~$8/mo) / Connoisseur (~$19/mo). FLYWHEEL: buyer demand for graded items -> sellers must grade to sell -> more graded inventory -> better buyer product. TIES: reuses capability EPICs US-1745/1750/1753/1758/1762/1767/1776/1785 + buyer guarantee US-867. SEQUENCING: foundation (US-1795 sub-epic) ships first; idea sub-epics (US-1805+) depend on it. Child sub-epics: account+subscription foundation (1795), alerts (1805), grade-confirm rewards (1810), buyer trust score (1815), insured grade-locked guarantee (1819), wardrobe portfolio (1824), graded-wanted board (1829), extension confidence suite (1833), buyer bindings for existing capability epics (1839-1844), cross-cutting analytics/legal/QA (1845-1847).

userStories.title: EPIC: Buyer account & subscription foundation

acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can create an account, complete a buyer-first onboarding, save shopping preferences, subscribe/upgrade/cancel a buyer plan via Stripe, and land on a buyer dashboard — all reusing the existing Supabase-auth + Stripe + TanStack Query stack
A buyer account is cleanly distinguished from a seller/FlipDesk account (account_type) while allowing a single person to be both without duplicate identities
Buyer entitlements resolve from the buyer plan and gate features consistently on client and edge, with usage metering for metered actions
All buyer tables follow the migration triple, are tenant-scoped (RLS + edge service-role scoping), and PII is treated as sensitive
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][EPIC][FOUNDATION][NEW] Reuses: Supabase PKCE auth + handle_new_user() trigger + useAuth()/auth-store.ts + <ProtectedRoute>/<AuthLayout>; Stripe stack (src/lib/stripe.ts, edge stripe-*.ts + webhooks.ts); billing hooks (use-pricing-plans.ts/use-plan-usage.ts/use-billing-summary.ts) + src/components/billing/*; entitlement pattern from FlipdeskGateFlags in constants.ts. Child stories: account model+account_type (1796), signup/onboarding (1797), profile+preferences (1798), plans+Stripe products (1799), entitlements+gating+metering (1800), billing surfaces (1801), dashboard shell+nav (1802), notification/alert delivery infra (1803), mobile IAP mirror (1804). MUST load the migrations skill for every table; MUST load tenant-isolation skill for every edge route.

userStories.title: EPIC: Condition-based alerts & watchlist ('snipe on grade, not price')
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to be alerted when an item matching my brand + size + minimum objective grade + max price appears so that I catch well-graded deals no marketplace filter can surface — because they filter on the seller's self-reported condition, not GradeThread's objective grade.
acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can create saved searches / watchlists keyed on brand, size, category, minimum GradeThread grade, and max price, and be notified on matches
Matching runs over GradeThread-graded inventory (public_grade_reports / graded listings) and, where available, extension-fed marketplace listings the buyer is browsing
Alert frequency and number of active alerts are entitlement-gated (Free: none/limited; Guard: standard; Connoisseur: unlimited/instant)
This umbrella tracks US-1806…US-1809
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ALERTS][EPIC][NEW] BASELINE: no watchlist/saved-search/alert primitive exists anywhere (grep confirmed). Unique angle: filter on OBJECTIVE grade, impossible without the grading engine. DATA: public_grade_reports view + graded listings + grade_outcomes; buyer preferences (1798) as defaults. DELIVERY: notification infra (1803). TIES: extension ingestion (1808) feeds off-platform listings. Load durable-jobs skill for the matching cron. Depends on foundation (1795). Child stories: model (1806), matching engine (1807), extension ingestion (1808), delivery+UI (1809).

userStories.title: Alerts: extension-fed marketplace listing ingestion
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want listings I browse on marketplaces to count toward my alerts and watchlist so that GradeThread can flag matches even for items not yet on our platform.
acceptanceCriteria: The buyer extension can submit a browsed listing (URL + images + seller-claimed fields) to a hardened buyer-scoped endpoint that grades it and evaluates it against the buyer's saved searches
Ingested listings are rate-limited, quota-metered per entitlement, and SSRF-guarded (reuse the public grading endpoint hardening)
Matches from ingested listings notify via the same path as on-platform matches; ingested data respects marketplace ToS (buyer's own browsing, no bulk scraping)
Ingestion is tenant-scoped to the submitting buyer
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ALERTS][EXTENSION][NEW] Reuse public-grading.ts hardening (gradeCheckRateLimited + safeFetch SSRF guard + quickGrade). This is the bridge between the extension (1833) and alerts. Quota via entitlements (1800). RISK: marketplace image-scraping ToS — constrain to buyer-initiated, per-listing, no crawling. Load tenant-isolation skill.

userStories.title: Buyer binding: Walk-around video grading credits for buyers
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to request a walk-around video grade so that I get a richer condition read before committing to a higher-value purchase.
acceptanceCriteria: Video grading (US-1762/1765/1766) is available to buyers as an included/credit-metered action gated by entitlement (Connoisseur or credit packs)
Buyer-requested video grades reuse the existing capture + metering (cost = frames x per-image), with plan-based caps
Results surface in the buyer's item/portfolio context
Metering/debit reuses the credit precedence (1800)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][BINDING][VIDEO] REUSE US-1762 epic (metering 1765, capture 1766). Buyer credits via entitlements (1800). Cost math per US-1765 (frames x per-image). Depends on foundation (1795) + video epic (1762).

userStories.title: Buyer binding: 'What's It Worth' → buyer signup conversion funnel
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the free public grade+value tool to convert into buyer signups so that our top-of-funnel feeds the buyer subscription.
acceptanceCriteria: The public 'What's It Worth' tool (US-1750) gets buyer-oriented conversion moments (save this result, set an alert for it, verify future purchases) that route into buyer signup (1797)
Anonymous results can be claimed into a new buyer account without loss (session->account handoff)
Conversion is attributed (affiliate/referral) end-to-end
No change to the free tool's abuse controls
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][BINDING][GROWTH] REUSE US-1750 What's-It-Worth epic. Add buyer CTAs (save/alert/verify) -> signup (1797) with anon-session claim handoff. Attribution via affiliate.ts. Depends on foundation (1795) + What's-It-Worth epic (1750) + alerts (1805).

userStories.title: Buyer platform: analytics, funnel & revenue instrumentation
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the buyer funnel and feature usage instrumented so that we can measure conversion, retention, feature value, and the two-sided flywheel and optimize revenue.
acceptanceCriteria: PostHog events across the buyer funnel (public tool -> signup -> subscribe -> feature use -> retention) and per-feature usage (extension checks, alerts, confirmations, guarantee claims, portfolio, wants)
An admin buyer-growth surface (extend admin-growth) shows conversion, MRR by tier, feature adoption, and flywheel metrics (buyer demand -> seller grading)
Revenue attribution ties buyer subscriptions and metered credits back to acquisition source
Events are privacy-compliant (opt-in where required)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ANALYTICS][GROWTH] Reuse PostHog + admin-growth surface + affiliate/referral attribution. Flywheel metric = buyer-demand -> seller-grading correlation. Depends on foundation (1795); instruments all buyer epics.

userStories.title: Buyer platform: legal, privacy & consent (PII, guarantee terms, extension)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the buyer platform's legal and privacy posture right so that we handle buyer PII lawfully and the guarantee/extension are compliant.
acceptanceCriteria: Buyer PII (body profiles, purchase history, preferences, reputation) is classified sensitive, RLS-protected, with data-export/delete honoring existing privacy flows and geo-consent
Guarantee/coverage terms + authenticity/fraud-flag copy are legal-reviewed before ship (confidence estimates, not definitive claims)
Extension privacy policy + opt-in telemetry (US-1757) cover the buyer confidence suite's data flows
Consent surfaces respect the existing legal geo-consent framework
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][LEGAL][PRIVACY] Reuse existing privacy/geo-consent framework + SECURITY.md posture. Coverage terms (1819) + fraud-flag copy (1836) + authenticity disclaimers (1840) all need legal review. Extension privacy ties to US-1757. Cross-cutting across all buyer epics.

userStories.title: EPIC: GradeThread Rewards — gamified grade -> share -> reward viral loop
userStories.description: As a user, I want to earn points, levels, badges, streaks and real rewards for grading items, completing activities, and sharing my finds so that engagement is fun and habit-forming — and as GradeThread I want the built-in loop (grade -> auto-generated share overlay -> social share -> reward -> public showcase -> new signups) to be our primary viral growth engine.
acceptanceCriteria: A rewards system supports BOTH cosmetic rewards (XP, levels, badges/medals, streaks, leaderboard rank, profile/overlay flair — free and unlimited) AND tangible rewards (free grade credits, subscription discounts, discounted grading — budget-capped and anti-abuse-gated)

The core loop is frictionless: grade an item -> get an auto-generated shareable overlay card -> share it -> the share (and verified click-throughs) earn rewards -> the find can appear in a public showcase feed
All reward earning is event-sourced, idempotent, fraud-resistant, and tangible-reward payout is capped to protect unit-economics margins with an admin kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][EPIC] BASELINE (rails already built to reward ON): grade credits via grant_grade_credits RPC + grade_credit_transactions; referral_milestone_grants (reward-on-threshold precedent); referral_campaign_codes -> immediate credits (redemption model to mirror); Stripe billing in payments.ts; share renderer cert-image-render.ts + SLAB_FORMATS + cert-share-actions.tsx (referral-baked share); cert view/click tracking (content-public.ts /view ?s=) + affiliate_clicks/referral_events attribution; leaderboard opt-in (referrals.ts, referral-leaderboard.tsx) + verified directory. GAP (greenfield): no XP/points, levels, badges/achievements, streaks, quests, showcase feed, or redemption-of-XP-for-rewards. TECH/3P: none new (all in-stack: Postgres event ledger, Stripe coupons, existing renderer). TIES: EPIC 9 (US-1781/1782 auto grade-reveal cards) is the share engine this loop rides; referral/affiliate for attribution; verified directory for leaderboards; unit-economics (Pro 750 / Business 2000 AI-action caps, 40% margin floor) constrains tangible rewards; admin-fraud/admin-safety for anti-gaming; notifications/drip for re-engagement; feature_flags for kill-switch. BUYER: showcase feed to browse cool finds (SEO + social). SELLER/USER: fun, status, streaks, real discounts, effortless sharing. ECONOMICS RULE: cosmetic rewards unlimited; tangible rewards MUST be capped + fraud-gated + margin-aware. Child stories: points engine, achievements, levels/streaks, quests, tangible redemption, share-to-earn, showcase feed, leaderboards, rewards UI, economics/anti-abuse, re-engagement.

userStories.title: Rewards: event-sourced XP/points engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want an idempotent, event-sourced points ledger so that every rewardable activity grants XP exactly once and the whole system is auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: New reward_events (append-only: user_id, event_type, xp_awarded, source_ref, dedupe_key, created_at) + user_reward_state (xp_total, level, current_streak, longest_streak, updated_at) tables, tenant-scoped RLS
A grantReward(userId, eventType, sourceRef) primitive is idempotent on dedupe_key (e.g. grade:{submissionId}, share:{cardId}) so replays/retries never double-award

Rewardable events wired at their source with per-event XP configured in a catalog; the catalog is weighted by business/moat contribution (coverage completed, badge embedded off-platform, aspects filled, marketplace connected, arrival confirmed, verified share-click) rather than raw effort
Events that consume real AI spend (grading) only award XP when the action was PAID or credit-consuming — free/junk submissions earn nothing, making grade-XP self-limiting against farming

This is the ONE reward ledger for BOTH the seller/user track (US-1848 epic) and the buyer Trust Score track (US-1815..1818) — buyer scoring stories consume this engine and must not build a parallel one

userStories.title: Rewards: levels, seasons & buyer-side streaks
userStories.description: As a user, I want to level up through seasons of activity so that regular engagement is rewarding — without a streak mechanic that punishes the bursty, seasonal rhythm of reselling.
acceptanceCriteria: XP thresholds map to named levels/tiers (e.g. Thrifter -> Picker -> Curator -> Archivist -> Legend) shown as progress toward the next level; level is derived from user_reward_state.xp_total and NEVER decreases

Seller-side activity uses quarterly SEASONS (a season track with goals + season-end recap/rewards that resets cleanly) instead of weekly streaks — a slow sourcing month never destroys accumulated status; recency competition lives on the weekly leaderboards (US-1856), not on identity

Calendar streaks exist only where a genuinely daily/weekly surface exists — the buyer extension + confirmation flow (US-1814) — with grace/streak-freeze rules; seller surfaces show season progress instead
Levels unlock cosmetic perks (profile flair, exclusive share-card frames/overlays) with no hard paywall
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Level thresholds + season logic in a rewards lib; season rollover timezone-aware (reuse scheduled-drops tz handling). Cosmetic overlay frames = additional cert-image-render templates gated by level. No tangible cost = unlimited. Refined 2026-07-09: streaks are the wrong loyalty primitive for bursty resellers — replaced with seasons; streaks kept buyer-side only. Tenure/loyalty tiers split out to US-1914.

userStories.title: Rewards: quests & time-boxed challenges (personal + community)
userStories.description: As a user, I want quests and seasonal challenges so that there's always a fresh reason to come back and grade/share.
acceptanceCriteria: Personal quests (e.g. 'grade 3 items this week', 'share 1 find', 'add measurements to 5 items') with progress tracking and XP/reward on completion
Time-boxed community/seasonal challenges (e.g. 'Best thrift find of the month') that can feed the showcase feed and leaderboards
Admin-configurable quest definitions (criteria, window, reward) with start/end and a kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Migration triple for quests (config, deny-all) + user_quest_progress (tenant RLS). Progress derived from reward_events. Community challenges tie to the showcase feed + leaderboards. Admin CRUD via a new admin surface (mirror admin-growth patterns).

userStories.title: Rewards: milestone-granted tangible rewards (credits + discounts) — XP is never spent
userStories.description: As a user, I want crossing XP/badge milestones to GRANT me real perks (free grade credits, subscription/grading discounts) so that engagement pays off — without spending XP, so my level and leaderboard rank never go backwards for redeeming.
acceptanceCriteria: XP is permanent and only ever accrues (status currency: levels, leaderboards); tangible value is granted when crossing configured milestones — XP is NEVER debited. Spendable currency is the existing grade-credit ledger, not XP

A milestone-rewards catalog (reward_type free_grade_credits | subscription_discount | per_grade_discount, trigger = XP threshold | badge | season goal, value, monthly + lifetime caps) that admins configure

Granting free grade credits reuses grant_grade_credits into grade_credit_transactions; subscription discounts issue a Stripe coupon/promo applied in payments.ts; per-grade discounts apply at the payment-precedence step
Every grant is recorded in a redemption/grant ledger, is idempotent per (user, milestone), respects per-user and global caps, and cannot double-issue
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][BILLING] Migration triple for milestone catalog + user_reward_grants ledger. Credits reuse grant_grade_credits (as referral_campaign_codes already do). Stripe coupon path in payments.ts (subscribe/downgrade). Per-grade discount hooks runPaymentPrecedence (grade-billing.ts). MUST enforce caps from US-1858. Refined 2026-07-09: spend-XP model replaced with milestone-grant model — spending XP deflates status, penalizes redeemers on leaderboards, and invites hoarding; milestone grants avoid all three.

userStories.title: Rewards: share-to-earn loop (auto overlay -> verified share -> reward)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to be rewarded for sharing my graded finds so that showing off my finds is both fun and worthwhile — the core viral trigger.
acceptanceCriteria: Sharing a grade's auto-generated overlay card (from EPIC 9 / US-1782) creates a tracked share and grants XP; bonus XP/credit for VERIFIED click-throughs (real visits via the referral-baked link), not merely pressing share
Anti-gaming: rewards key off attributed unique clicks/signups (affiliate_clicks/referral_events), rate-limited, with fraud checks so self-clicking/bots can't farm rewards
A 'Viral Find' badge + escalating rewards for finds that drive N verified click-throughs or a signup
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SHARE][GROWTH] Depends on EPIC 9 US-1782 (auto reveal card) + cert-share-actions.tsx referral bake + cert_view ?s= + affiliate_clicks/referral_events. Reward on verified conversion, not raw share, to prevent farming. Fraud gate via admin-fraud.ts + rate_limit_counters.

userStories.title: Rewards: public Showcase / 'Finds' feed
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want a public feed of cool graded finds so that I get inspired, discover GradeThread, and want to grade my own — and as a user I want my best finds featured.
acceptanceCriteria: An opt-in public showcase feed of graded finds (photo + grade + optional value + verified seller link), with filters (brand, category, grade, trending) and reactions/upvotes
Feed entries are SEO-indexable (edge-SSR Pages Function, Model B) with Product/ItemList JSON-LD and link to the certificate and seller profile
Featured/trending finds surface on the landing page and feed community challenges/leaderboards; only public, non-PII, seller-consented items appear
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SEO][SHARE] Model B Pages Function (clone condition-index/[[path]].ts) + public edge endpoint over grade_reports (public_grade_reports view) filtered to opt-in/showcased. Reactions table (tenant RLS). Ties verified profiles + certificate. Sitemap + _routes.json + PWA denylist. Consent required (mirror verified_show_listings).

userStories.title: Rewards: leaderboards (weekly / all-time / category)
userStories.description: As a competitive user, I want leaderboards so that I can climb ranks for finds, grades, XP, and shares.
acceptanceCriteria: Leaderboards for XP, grades, best finds, and share-driven signups (weekly, all-time, and by category/brand), opt-in with a public alias
Built on the existing referral leaderboard opt-in + verified directory; anti-gaming safeguards and tie-breaks
Leaderboard pages are SEO-indexable and interlink with the showcase feed and verified profiles
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SEO] Reuse referrals.ts leaderboard opt-in + referral-leaderboard.tsx + verified-directory. Weekly windows via a snapshot job. Cross-link showcase + profiles. Anti-gaming shared with share-to-earn.

userStories.title: Rewards: user-facing UI (progress, badges shelf, celebrations, share)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a delightful rewards UI so that I can see my progress, badges, streaks, and next reward, and celebrate wins.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard rewards widget: XP bar + level, season progress (buyer surfaces: streak), badge shelf, active quests, and 'next milestone reward' progress; a full rewards page with badge gallery and milestone-rewards claim area (per the US-1853 grant model — nothing spends XP)

Celebrations are TIERED for a professional audience: routine XP gains get a quiet toast at most (batched, never per-event); real celebration moments (lightweight confetti/animation via sonner + CSS, no heavy deps) are reserved for level-ups, integrity-tier changes (US-1912), season completions, and first-ever events — each with a one-tap share of a badge/level card
Respects reduced-motion and accessibility (WCAG AA per VPAT posture); celebration frequency is capped so FlipDesk power users bulk-processing hundreds of items are never spammed
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][UI] React 19 + Tailwind v4 + shadcn; toasts via sonner (project rule); animations CSS-only, honor prefers-reduced-motion. Widget on dashboard.tsx; full page new route. Badge/level share cards reuse the renderer. jsx-a11y build-blocking (accessibility memory). Refined 2026-07-09: celebrations tiered — confetti-on-everything erodes the professional credibility the Verified brand depends on; big moments only.

userStories.title: Rewards: economics guardrails, budget caps & anti-abuse
userStories.description: As GradeThread, I want tangible rewards strictly capped and fraud-gated so that gamification drives growth without eroding margins or being farmed.
acceptanceCriteria: A global + per-user tangible-reward budget (free grades + discounts) with an ai_budgets-style ceiling and an admin kill-switch; cosmetic rewards are exempt (zero marginal cost)
Tangible payout respects unit-economics guardrails (grades cost real AI $; keep tiers above the 40% margin floor / AI-action caps) and is reconciled against grade_credit_transactions + Stripe
Abuse detection: dedupe on all grants, velocity limits, self-referral/self-click blocking, and a fraud review queue (reuse admin-fraud/admin-safety); admin dashboard of reward spend vs signups (ROI)
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][OPS][BILLING] Reuse ai_budgets pattern for a reward_budget + kill-switch (feature_flags). Ties project_subscription_unit_economics (Pro 750 / Business 2000 caps, 40% floor). Fraud via admin-fraud.ts + rate_limit_counters + step-up-audited grants (admin-growth pattern). ROI dashboard = reward spend vs attributed signups.

userStories.title: Rewards: re-engagement nudges (streaks, near-miss, quests)
userStories.description: As a lapsing user, I want timely nudges so that I keep my streak, finish quests, and come back to grade and share.
acceptanceCriteria: Opt-in notifications: streak-at-risk reminders, 'you're 1 grade from the {badge}' near-miss nudges, new-quest and challenge announcements, and reward-available alerts
Delivered via the existing notifications/drip/journey engine, frequency-capped and honoring notification preferences + suppressions
Nudges are attributed so we can measure re-engagement lift
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][GROWTH] Reuse notifications.ts + drip.ts + journeys + admin-suppressions. Frequency caps + preference/consent (ties legal geo-consent + branded auth email pipeline). Attribution via campaign-tracking.

userStories.title: Seller Grade Integrity score — buyer confirmations become seller reputation
userStories.description: As a verified seller, I want a Grade Integrity score built from real post-sale outcomes (buyer arrival confirmations, dispute rate, coverage, tenure) so that my proven accuracy — not just my activity volume — is my standing; and as GradeThread we want a reputation asset no listing-tool competitor can replicate without first building a grading-quality scanner and a buyer confirmation base.
acceptanceCriteria: An integrity aggregate per seller (confirmed-accurate rate from US-1812 outcomes, upheld-dispute rate, avg photo-coverage %, graded volume, tenure) computed into named tiers with transparent, explainable rules the seller can view

Score is anti-gameable: minimum confirmed-outcome volume before a tier displays (below the floor shows 'building history', never a bad score), self-purchases/linked-account confirmations excluded (reuse referral self-click blocking), and dispute outcomes only count after human-review resolution
Integrity tier surfaces on the public verified profile and certificate pages (read path via the existing public-cert/verified RLS carve-outs, PII-safe)
Tier changes emit reward_events (US-1849) and a tier-up is a celebration moment (US-1857); a tier-down notifies the seller privately with the specific driver, never publicly announced
Migration triple satisfied; aggregate recompute is idempotent and tenant-scoped
userStories.notes:
[P2][GAME][TRUST][NEW] Added 2026-07-09 (gamification refinement session). THE connective story: US-1810..1814 buyer confirmations currently feed only model accuracy — this makes them feed seller reputation too, closing the two-sided loop. Inputs: grade_outcomes (1812), human_reviews, coverage scoring (US-1276+ epic), verified profile (00057+). Load grading-engine + tenant-isolation skills. Distinct from buyer Trust Score (1815-1818): this scores SELLERS. | FOUNDATION 2026-07-12 (passes:false): pure sellerIntegrityTier() added to buyer-grade-confirmation.ts (next to existing computeSellerIntegrityScore + recomputeSellerGradeIntegrity + seller_grade_integrity cache) — named tiers building/verified/reliable/trusted/elite with a transparent TIER_LADDER (score+confirmed-volume+coverage+tenure+graded-volume gates, coverage/tenure gated only when known), AC2 anti-gaming confirmed-volume floor (MIN_CONFIRMED_FOR_TIER=10 → non-displayable building history, never a bad public score), explainable reasons + nextTierGaps; 7 deno tests. REMAINING: recompute must apply AC2 self/linked-account exclusion + human-review-resolved-disputes-only filtering and store tier+coverage/tenure inputs (migration for tier fields on seller_grade_integrity); AC3 surface tier on public cert/verified-profile (RLS carve-outs, PII-safe); AC4 emit reward_events + tier-up celebration BLOCKED on US-1849 (Rewards engine / reputation_events ledger decision), tier-down private notify. grading-engine/tenant-isolation apply to the impure recompute+surfacing, not this pure fn. 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (agent loop, NO migration → pushable). AC2 anti-gaming advanced: added pure countableSellerOutcomes(rows, {sellerUserId, linkedUserIds, requireResolvedDispute}) in buyer-grade-confirmation.ts — drops self-purchase + linked-account confirmations (a seller can no longer inflate their integrity via their own/colluding accounts; reuses the referral self-click-blocking idea) AND counts a dispute only after human-review resolution (an unresolved dispute is excluded entirely — not bad, not total — so a frivolous dispute can't dent a score before an expert rules). Wired into recomputeSellerGradeIntegrity: select now includes buyer_user_id + human_review_flagged; self/linked exclusion is ACTIVE; a review-flagged (material) dispute is treated as PENDING (uncounted, benefit-of-the-doubt) until resolved, a minor never-reviewed dispute counts immediately. 7 deno tests (self-exclusion, linked-exclusion, unresolved-dispute-excluded, resolved-material-counts-double, requireResolvedDispute:false, self-dispute-excluded, null-buyer-kept); full edge suite green, deno check/lint clean. REMAINING (unchanged blockers): the resolved-dispute RE-count once a flagged dispute's human review RESOLVES still needs the grade_reports/human_reviews join (approximated here via human_review_flagged); AC2 tier/coverage/tenure STORAGE needs a migration; AC3 surface tier on public cert/verified profile (RLS carve-outs); AC4 emit reward_events + tier-up celebration remains BLOCKED on US-1849 (Rewards-engine/reputation_events decision). Story stays passes:false — AC4 is the hard blocker.

userStories.title: External status: level + integrity tier on embedded badges, certificates & public profile
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want my GradeThread level and Grade Integrity tier to render on the badges buyers actually see — my eBay-embedded seller badge, per-listing cert badges, certificates, and my public verified profile — so that status earned in GradeThread converts directly into buyer trust and sales; for a business user, external legibility is what makes gamification worth engaging with (and every leveled-up badge is an ad).
acceptanceCriteria: Badge Studio embed renders (verified-seller badge /badge/verified/:handle, cert badge /badge/cert/:id) gain level/integrity-tier variants (e.g. 'Gold Verified · 1,200 grades · 98% confirmed accurate') — opt-in per embed, seller chooses plain vs status format
Certificate page + public verified profile show the seller's integrity tier and level flair (frames from US-1851 cosmetics) with a tooltip explaining the basis
Embedded badge images reflect tier changes without the seller re-pasting HTML (badges are edge-rendered per request, so the same URL serves the current tier); stale-tier caching bounded to <=24h
Numbers on external badges are defensible: only display integrity claims above the US-1912 minimum-volume floor; no placeholder/aspirational stats (mirrors the no-fake-JSON-LD rule)
Share-source attribution (?s=embed) preserved so status-badge click-throughs are measurable against plain-badge click-throughs
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][GROWTH][NEW] Added 2026-07-09 (gamification refinement session). Converts gamification from dashboard dopamine into a selling tool — the retention lever for business users. Builds on badge-studio (US-1759/1761, src/lib/verified.ts, use-badge-studio.ts), edge badge render, US-1851 frames, US-1912 tiers. A/B the click-through delta via existing share-source attribution (US-769).

userStories.title: Loyalty: tenure tiers, anniversary rewards & never-decay standing
userStories.description: As a long-time user, I want my loyalty recognized with standing that never decays — member-since tenure tiers, anniversary rewards, and escalating milestone-credit multipliers — so that being a loyal customer is rewarded independently of how active I am this month; activity and loyalty are different things and only activity should be time-windowed.
acceptanceCriteria: Tenure tiers derived from account age + lifetime paid engagement (e.g. 1yr/2yr/veteran) that only ever ascend — no decay, no reset; displayed as 'member since' flair on profile and rewards page

Anniversary moments: on each account anniversary, an automatic milestone grant (via the US-1853 catalog) + a celebration/share card; delivered through the existing notifications/drip engine, preference-honoring
Tenure tier applies a multiplier to milestone-granted credits (US-1853) so loyal users earn tangibly more per milestone; multiplier config lives in the admin catalog and respects US-1858 budget caps

Returning-after-a-gap users are welcomed, never shamed: no 'you lost your streak' messaging anywhere in the system; re-engagement nudges (US-1859) for lapsed users lead with what's new + their preserved standing
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][RETENTION][NEW] Added 2026-07-09 (gamification refinement session). Split from US-1851: seasons handle ACTIVITY, this handles LOYALTY — decay mechanics punish exactly the loyal-but-bursty reseller. Tenure from profiles.created_at + subscription/credit history. Multiplier hooks the US-1853 grant path. Anniversary via drip/journey engine (drip-tick cron — note edge-cron curl gotcha memory).

userStories.title: Rewards: north-star metrics, per-mechanic attribution & retention instrumentation
userStories.description: As the operator, I want every gamification mechanic instrumented against explicit north-star metrics (week-4 retention, grades/user/month, share-loop K-factor) so that we can tell dopamine from retention and kill mechanics that don't move the business — before quests/seasons/leaderboards scale spend.
acceptanceCriteria: North-star metric definitions codified (week-4 retention by cohort, grades/user/month, K-factor from share-to-earn, milestone-grant cost per retained user) and computed from existing event data (reward_events, referral_events, affiliate_clicks, grade_credit_transactions)

Every reward grant, celebration, nudge, and external-badge click carries a mechanic-attribution tag (which mechanic caused it) so lift is measurable per mechanic, not just in aggregate — extends the US-1859 nudge-attribution pattern to ALL mechanics

Admin rewards-analytics surface: per-mechanic engagement lift, reward spend vs retention (extends the US-1858 spend-vs-signups ROI view), cohort retention curves gamified-vs-not, and a per-mechanic kill-switch honoring the US-1858 pattern
PostHog events for the key loop steps (grant, celebration shown, share, verified click-through, milestone claim) consistent with existing analytics conventions
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][ANALYTICS][NEW] Added 2026-07-09 (gamification refinement session). The epic had no measurement story — US-1858 covers spend/abuse ROI, US-1859 attributes nudges only; this makes every mechanic accountable. Ship the definitions WITH the engine (1849), not after: retro-instrumenting cohorts is impossible. Admin surface can live beside admin/growth/dashboard.tsx.

userStories.title: EPIC: Thrift Radar — crowdsourced store-level sourcing intelligence ('Waze for thrifting')
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want to know which local stores are currently producing high-value finds for my brands — before I drive there — so I spend my sourcing hours in the right places. Every Prospect scan already carries the raw signal (location, brand, estimated grade, buy/pass verdict); aggregated across opted-in users it becomes a live map of secondhand supply that no listing-tool competitor can replicate without first building a grading-quality scanner and a fleet of users pointing it at store racks.
acceptanceCriteria: This is the umbrella/epic story — it does not ship code itself; child stories US-1861..US-1867 implement it.

Privacy stance (non-negotiable): contribution is strictly OPT-IN (default off); contributions are anonymized and aggregated at store/venue granularity only; no precise user coordinates retained after venue resolution; network aggregates are displayed only above a k-anonymity floor of distinct contributors.
The personal layer (US-1864) must be independently useful at n=1 with zero network data — that is the cold-start answer.
Monetization: network layers (map hotness, venue detail, route planner) are plan-gated Pro+; the personal history layer is free on all plans.
Viewing Radar and contributing to Radar are separate consents — using the map never silently enrolls you as a contributor.
userStories.notes: [EPIC][P2 Growth][FlipDesk][Scout] Parent of US-1861..US-1867. Origin: founder ideation session 2026-07-09 ('the Waze of secondhand sourcing'). Builds on the existing Prospect/Scout scan path (flipdesk-scout.ts, scout.tsx, iOS Prospect module). Distinct from US-1064 (per-user insights) — this is the cross-user network intelligence layer; distinct from US-1829 demand board (buyer demand, not store supply). Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: opt-in scan telemetry + consent & privacy model
userStories.description: As a privacy-conscious user, I want Radar contribution to be explicitly opt-in, anonymized, and clearly explained, so sharing where I source never exposes me or my spots to identification.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds radar_scan_events: rotating anonymized contributor key (no readable user_id in the analytical path), venue_id (or geohash cell while unresolved), brand, category, estimated grade band, buy/pass verdict, timestamp. Raw scan coordinates are NOT retained after venue resolution. Deny-all RLS, service-role writes only; register in rls-guard_test.ts.
Settings toggle 'Contribute to Thrift Radar' (web + iOS), DEFAULT OFF; Prospect scans emit Radar events only when it is on.

Consent copy states exactly what is shared and at what granularity; privacy policy gains a Radar section; iOS App Privacy declarations updated for location use consistent with the US-1214 opt-in posture.
Contribution is fire-and-forget: a Radar-event failure never degrades or slows the Prospect scan result itself.
New/changed edge routes carry tenant-isolation_test.ts cases (tenant-isolation skill); migration follows the US-1108 triple (migrations skill).
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar][Privacy] Child of US-1860. The consent boundary is the whole story — get this wrong and the feature is a liability. Emit from the existing prospect scan handler behind the flag. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: store venue resolution + registry
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need to resolve raw scan coordinates into named, deduplicated store venues (Goodwill on Main St, Savers on Route 9), so intelligence accrues to places rather than coordinate soup.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds radar_venues: display name, centroid (lat/lng), geohash, chain tag (goodwill / savers / salvation_army / value_village / other), status (candidate / confirmed).
Resolver maps scan coordinates to the nearest known venue within a distance threshold; unresolved scans create a candidate venue (or bin to a geohash cell) that later scans converge onto.
Chain normalization: 'Goodwill Store #123' and 'Goodwill Industries' resolve to the same chain tag; per-venue identity stays distinct.
Dedupe merge path for near-duplicate candidate venues; unit tests cover threshold resolution, candidate creation, and merge.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar] Child of US-1860. Keep it dependency-free: no external Places API required for v1 (chain inference from scan density + optional user naming); design the schema so a Places enrichment can be added later without rework. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: aggregation engine + k-anonymity floor
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need scheduled aggregation that turns anonymized scan events into venue-level intelligence (brand density, grade quality, freshness) that is only ever served above an anonymity floor.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduled aggregation job (durable-jobs conventions: claim/heartbeat/reclaim, cron_runs visibility) computes venue x brand x time-window stats: scan count, distinct-contributor count, average estimated grade, buy-verdict rate, last-activity freshness.

K-ANONYMITY FLOOR: aggregates for a venue x window are served only when distinct contributors >= K (configurable, default 3). Below the floor the venue shows no network data — enforced server-side, with a test proving a below-floor venue returns nothing.
Raw radar_scan_events older than the retention window are rolled up and pruned; retention is configurable.
Read-only edge endpoint serves aggregates (venue list by bounding box + venue detail); responses contain no per-user or per-contributor data.
deno tests cover the aggregation math, k-floor enforcement, and retention pruning; migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar] Child of US-1860. Load the durable-jobs skill for the job pattern and the migrations skill for the rollup tables. The k-floor is a hard privacy guarantee, not a display preference. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: personal sourcing history layer ('your best stores')
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want my OWN sourcing history per store — items found, spend, realized profit, best brands, last visit — so Radar is valuable to me on day one even before any network data exists near me.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-venue personal stats computed from the user's own scans and sourced items (sources + inventory_items + sales outcomes): items sourced, total spend, realized + expected profit, top brands, last-visit date.
Works with zero network data and does NOT require the Radar contribution opt-in (it is the user's own data).
Surfaced as a 'My stores' list in the FlipDesk Scout area, sortable by personal ROI.
All queries tenant-scoped per US-268 (tenant-isolation skill test cases).
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar][LHF] Child of US-1860. This is the cold-start answer and the free tier of Radar. Links personal scans to venues via the US-1862 resolver. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: web map + venue detail UI
userStories.description: As a reseller planning where to source, I want a map of nearby stores showing which are hot for my brands right now, with per-venue detail, so I can pick my next stop with data instead of habit.
acceptanceCriteria: Radar surface in FlipDesk (route or Scout tab): map of nearby venues with hotness coloring (recent scan density weighted toward the user's top brands from their pipeline history), freshness indicator, and the personal layer (US-1864) overlaid on the same map.

Venue detail panel: brand mix, estimated-grade distribution, activity-by-day pattern — each section hidden below the k-floor with an honest 'Not enough data here yet — contributions unlock this' state.
Network layers plan-gated Pro+ with an upgrade prompt; personal layer visible on all plans.
Cold-start/empty states designed for zero-data regions (personal layer + contribution pitch, never a blank map).
Map implementation must not violate the no-external-request constraints of any prerendered/public surface — this is an authed dashboard page; use a lightweight map lib consistent with bundle budgets.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar][UX] Child of US-1860. Depends on US-1863 (aggregates endpoint) + US-1864 (personal layer). Brand weighting comes from the user's existing pipeline history — no new AI spend. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: iOS surface (nearby hot stores in Prospect)
userStories.description: As an iOS user standing in (or driving past) a thrift store, I want the Prospect module to show nearby venues ranked by hotness for my brands, so the phone in my hand answers 'is this store worth walking into?'
acceptanceCriteria: Prospect module gains a Nearby/Radar view: nearby venues sorted by network hotness for the user's brands, blended with the personal layer; venue detail parity with web (same k-floor hiding).
Location permission requested only for the Radar view flow; viewing Radar does NOT enroll the user as a contributor (separate consent per US-1861); App Privacy declarations stay consistent.
Plan-gate parity with web: Pro+ network layers; 402 routes to the paywall/upgrade flow per the US-1213 pattern, never a dead-end.
Offline/sparse-data states degrade gracefully to the personal layer.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar][iOS] Child of US-1860. Reuses the US-1863 read endpoint; no on-device aggregation. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: sourcing route planner ('plan my circuit')
userStories.description: As a reseller planning a sourcing day, I want an ordered multi-stop route ranked by expected value per hour for MY brands, so a Saturday circuit is optimized instead of guessed.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Plan my circuit': user picks day + time budget + start point; planner returns an ordered stop list ranked by expected $/hour blending network hotness (US-1863) and personal per-venue ROI (US-1864), with travel time between stops considered.
Each stop shows its ranking rationale in plain language ('strong Lululemon density this week; you average $34 profit/visit here').
One tap opens the ordered route in Apple/Google Maps (no in-app turn-by-turn).
Degrades gracefully with sparse data: falls back to personal-only ranking, and says so.
Pro+ gated consistent with the Radar network tier.
userStories.notes: [P3][Radar] Child of US-1860 — build LAST, after US-1863/1864/1865 prove out data density. Simple greedy/nearest-value ordering is fine for v1; no route-optimization service dependency. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: EPIC: Inventory Equity — graded-inventory valuation (GradeThread Capital, Phase 1 ONLY)
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want to see the estimated liquidation value of my graded inventory — the capital sitting on my racks — so I understand what my stock is actually worth at current market prices and how much of it is unvalued because it is ungraded. Strategic context: this is Phase 1 of the 'GradeThread Capital' concept. It is display-only analytics built entirely from data we already have (grades, sold comps, Value Index condition curves, personal sell-through). It also creates the strongest organic grading incentive in the product: the more you grade, the more of your inventory is valued.
acceptanceCriteria: This is the umbrella/epic story — it does not ship code itself; child stories US-1869..US-1871 implement it.

SCOPE FENCE (founder decision 2026-07-09): Phase 1 is DISPLAY-ONLY valuation. Phase 2 — working-capital advances / lending against inventory (e.g. via the Stripe Capital platform program) — is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED due to legal and financial-responsibility concerns. Do NOT build any lending, credit-offer, advance, underwriting, or 'get funded' functionality, UI hints included, without a new explicit founder green-light. No Phase 2 child stories exist by design; do not create them.
All valuation output is clearly labeled an ESTIMATE for informational purposes — never presented as an appraisal, offer, or financial product, and no copy may imply borrowing capacity.
No new AI spend: valuation composes existing grade data, cached comps, and Value Index curves within existing comp-refresh quotas (US-1749 guardrails).
userStories.notes: [EPIC][P2][FlipDesk][Finance] Parent of US-1869..US-1871. Origin: founder ideation session 2026-07-09 ('Shopify Capital for resellers' — Phase 1 approved, Phase 2 deferred: DO NOT BUILD lending without explicit founder approval; revisit only post-launch with legal counsel). Distinct from US-1824 Wardrobe Portfolio (buyer closet valuation) — this is seller/FlipDesk inventory-side. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Inventory Equity: iOS Money tab card
userStories.description: As an iOS user, I want my inventory equity on the Money tab next to my other financials, so the value tied up in stock is visible where I already track money.
acceptanceCriteria: Money tab gains an Inventory Equity card: total equity, trend sparkline from snapshots, and valued-coverage % (valued items / total items); tapping opens a breakdown list (category / brand / grade band).
Reuses the US-1869 edge endpoint; numbers match web exactly (route money math through Money/MoneyMath per US-1002).
Estimate disclaimer parity with web; no borrowing-capacity language (US-1868 scope fence).
Graceful states for zero graded items (coverage CTA) and endpoint failure.
userStories.notes: [P3][Equity][iOS] Child of US-1868, depends on US-1869/1870. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: EPIC: Unified GradeThread extension — one install, role- and subscription-aware (buyer research for everyone, seller tools on top)
userStories.description: As a GradeThread user, I want ONE browser extension that gives every user the buyer-research surface (AI condition read on eBay/Poshmark/Grailed/Mercari/Depop/Vinted listings) and additionally unlocks the seller cross-posting Lister tools when I'm signed in as a seller, so I don't manage two installs — and sellers doing sourcing/comping get the same buyer research in the same session. Founder decision 2026-07-09: this supersedes the deliberate two-extension split (extension/ US-716 vs extension-condition/ US-1755/1756). Features gate on the signed-in GradeThread account's role and subscription tier.
acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella/epic story — child stories US-1873..US-1885 implement it; it ships no code itself

Target architecture: a single extension folder (merge extension/ + extension-condition/) with one manifest carrying both permission sets (marketplace host_permissions + gradethread.com), a shared background service worker, and a feature registry that exposes: condition-read overlay = always on (anonymous allowed, quota-capped), Lister cross-post/delist = only when authenticated with seller entitlements

Auth/entitlements reuse the signed extension token planned in US-1838 (buyer-subscription gating), extended to carry seller role + FlipDesk plan so one token answers both 'can this install cross-post' and 'what buyer quota applies'

Privacy posture is re-documented for the merged permission set (the old 'not host-permitted on gradethread.com' Lister claim no longer holds once merged — the privacy story becomes 'no cookies permission, no marketplace credential access, marketplace automation stays on-device') and store listing copy/privacy policy are rewritten accordingly (feeds US-1757)
The two legacy folders are removed once the unified extension reaches parity; READMEs updated; US-1757 (store distribution) targets the unified extension only
userStories.notes: Origin: 2026-07-09 extension deep-dive (3-agent audit of extension/, extension-condition/, and server integration). Related open stories NOT duplicated here: US-1833..1846 (buyer confidence suite + gating + legal), US-1757 (store distribution), US-1808 (extension-fed ingestion). Audit found the Lister privacy-by-manifest posture genuinely enforced today — the merge deliberately trades that isolation for one-install UX, so the privacy copy rewrite is mandatory, not cosmetic. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC4's STORE-KIT half done. userStories.title: Research surface: verify the five unverified adapters, fix the dead Poshmark upgrade rule, close intl host gaps, add selector-failure ping

Unknown/failed adapters keep degrading to the honest 'couldn't read the photos' state
