userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Trigger + per-listing results now live in the app. Placement is deliberate: the button sits IN the amber "this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its title/price/description/photos" banner on the item canvas — the exact place the seller hits the wall — rather than on a settings page they would have to know to look for. useMigrateEbayListings() reports eBay reasons PER LISTING rather than collapsing to one "done" (a multi-variation rejection is actionable, "failed" is not), capped at 3 toasts so a large batch cannot bury the screen. ⚠ FOUND AND FIXED A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE LOOK BROKEN: item-canvas computed lockedByEbay via deriveListingOrigin() but its listings query never SELECTED listing_origin — and that persisted column is exactly what migration writes, and what deriveListingOrigin lets WIN over the provenance signals. So post-migration the row still had a platform_listing_id, no batch_id and no synced_to_ebay_at, the canvas would have re-derived "ebay", and the seller would have seen the locked banner and the migrate button still sitting there after a SUCCESSFUL migration. Added listing_origin to the select + the two type literals, and invalidated the item_ebay_sync query in the mutation (it backs that banner; without it the UI would not refetch at all). Pinned with a NEW test file src/lib/__tests__/listing-origin.test.ts — deriveListingOrigin gates revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote and the locked-fields banner across the app and had ZERO test coverage before this; 5 tests now cover persisted-marker-wins (both directions), unrecognized-marker fallback, batch/sync signals, draft-with-no-listing-id, and non-eBay platforms. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. STILL passes:false — the only thing left is a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it), which cannot be done from the sandbox. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. Post-deploy smoke checks run the same day: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 (auth enforced) rather than a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which is the specific failure that would indicate 00477 had not landed; a real certificate off sitemap-certs.xml still returns 200, so the grading/cert path is unbroken; and gradethread.com now serves Permissions-Policy camera=(self) (a first check showed the old camera=() from a cached response — the cache-busted request confirmed the fix is live, worth noting because that cached read looked exactly like a failed deploy). | 2026-07-19 RE-VERIFIED LIVE. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' — auth enforced, route mounted, and specifically NOT a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which remains the exact signature that would mean 00477 (listings.inventory_sku) had not landed. So the feature is still healthy in prod. The ONLY remaining item is unchanged and unreachable from a sandbox: a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it) needs a live seller account with legacy listings. TWO INCIDENTAL SIGNALS FROM THE SAME PROBE, worth recording for whoever runs the next deploy: /health/ready still reports schema {expected:00478, applied:00479} — so the DEPLOYED edge predates the 00480-00485 stack, and the phantom 00479 is still there; and features{} has NO 'alerting' key while observability reads 'ok'. Both are artefacts of the deployed build predating today's work: US-2003 adds the alerting group and US-2001 makes observability report DEGRADED until GIT_SHA is a real SHA. Expect both to change on the next deploy — 'alerting' will appear as degraded (no channel configured) and 'observability' will flip from ok to degraded until the build arg is wired. Neither is a regression; they are the new checks becoming visible.

userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX.

userStories.title: US-1891 backwards title sync never shipped server-side — the edge title-sync module has zero callers
userStories.description: As a seller, when I correct an item's Brand/size/color/style/department from ANY surface, I want the listing title to update — not just from the web item canvas. US-1891 (P1, archived passes:true) required the substitution on 'the edge item update path AND web item-canvas save' (its AC2). Only the web half shipped. src/lib/title-sync.ts is wired into item-canvas.tsx persist(); its declared lockstep mirror services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts is imported by NOTHING — verified 2026-07-18, every export has zero production references. So an edit made through the edge item-update API, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit or CSV import still corrects the brand and leaves the OLD brand in listing_title: exactly the bug US-1891 exists to fix, on every surface except one. Both suites are green because each calls its own copy directly, so nothing signals the gap.
acceptanceCriteria: Item edits from EVERY non-canvas write path apply the same substitution the web canvas does, under the same conditions (GT-origin non-ebay listings only; both title_variants; hand-edited-vs-ai_generated_snapshot sets needs_review; live listings queue the revise-in-place prompt, never end/relist). NOTE: there is no generic edge item-update endpoint — see the 2026-07-18 scope correction; the concrete surfaces are web bulk-edit (brand/size/color/style, nearest gap), identification-verify, and iOS
It cannot DOUBLE-APPLY against the frontend path — decide one owner per surface, or make the substitution provably idempotent for the web canvas case that already ran it

iOS is the ONLY remaining surface (audited 2026-07-18): AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style and iOS never writes listing_title. identification-verify only annotates provenance, and CSV import is fill-only so a blank old value makes the substitution a provable no-op — neither needs wiring. Needs a macOS session; test the Swift port against src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json so it cannot drift from the two JS copies

A BEHAVIOURAL parity fixture shared by both suites: one table of (title, field changes) -> expected output asserted by the deno test AND the vitest test, so the two copies cannot drift. They currently differ by ~80 lines and nothing pins them — the frontend inlines the trim because it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects, which is legitimate, but that is exactly why source-diffing cannot be the guard
The ⚠ block at the top of the edge title-sync.ts is removed once it has real callers
userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. This is the more serious of the two: US-1994 is a contract divergence with no known live bug, whereas this is a P1 feature that measurably does not run on most surfaces. US-1891's own notes describe the web wiring in detail ('Wired into item-canvas persist()') and never claim the edge half — the AC asked for both, and the story was marked done anyway. Worth asking what else in the archive has the same shape: a 'lockstep mirror' is a strong smell, since only one copy usually gets a caller. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). Each needs verifying by hand: superseded, pending, and half-wired all look identical to the tool. NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. Anyone picking this up would have started by hunting for an endpoint that was never built. WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES ITEM FIELDS (verified 2026-07-18): (1) web item-canvas.tsx — a DIRECT supabase write, no edge round-trip, and the ONLY surface that runs title-sync; (2) web autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:872 — also a direct supabase .update(), and it patches brand/size/color/style, i.e. FOUR OF THE FIVE SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELDS, with NO title sync at all; (3) edge lib/ai-listing.ts:1793 and lib/grading-pipeline.ts:657 — but US-1891's notes state the AI-apply path REGENERATES titles wholesale so it deliberately needs no sync; (4) edge lib/identification-verify.ts:245 (attributes); (5) iOS. SO THE HEADLINE CHANGES: the nearest, cheapest gap is NOT iOS or the edge — it is WEB BULK EDIT, in the same codebase, with src/lib/title-sync.ts already sitting there importable. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. Do not start coding before that is settled. The AC list above still stands EXCEPT AC1's 'edge item update path' phrasing, which should be read as 'every non-canvas write path'. | SIZING THE BULK-EDIT GAP (same pass): it is smaller than it looks. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx ALREADY selects listing_title AND ai_generated_snapshot from listings (line ~190) — which are exactly the two inputs title-sync needs, ai_generated_snapshot being the hand-edited-vs-AI check that decides whether to set needs_review — and it ALREADY writes back to listings (line ~707). It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free). The sizing is recorded so whoever makes the call knows the per-surface option is cheap, not so the decision gets skipped. | 2026-07-18 ARCHITECTURE DECIDED + AC4 DONE. THE DECISION: per-surface mirrors with a shared BEHAVIOURAL fixture — NOT a DB trigger. I had earlier offered the trigger as my pick and then argued myself out of it: applyTitleSubstitution is 100+ lines of token-boundary, case-transfer, multi-word-brand and size-pattern string handling, so porting it to plpgsql would create a THIRD implementation in the language with the worst string handling of the three. That is a bigger version of the disease, not a cure. Funnelling every item write through one edge endpoint was also rejected for now: item writes are direct supabase calls from multiple clients (web canvas, web bulk-edit, iOS), so that is a large migration of its own and does not have to be paid before fixing the actual bug. AC4 SHIPPED: src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json — 13 cases (10 syncTitle + 3 changesFromItemDiff) read by BOTH suites, services/edge-functions/src/tests/title-sync_test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/title-sync.test.ts. A source diff could never have been the guard: the two files legitimately differ by ~80 lines because the web copy inlines the trim (it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects). Behaviour is the only thing that can be compared. FINDING: the two copies currently AGREE on all 13 cases — I ran the fixture against each implementation before wiring it in, so a disagreement would have surfaced as data rather than as a red test I then rationalised. So they had not behaviourally drifted; the risk was that nothing would have caught it if they did. Negative-verified: breaking case-transfer in the web copy alone turns 3 web tests red naming the exact fixture case, and the edge suite stays green (which is the point — the failing side identifies itself). Verified: edge 4129 passed / 0 failed, web 2164 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. STILL OPEN: the actual gap. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx patches brand/size/color/style with no title sync, and it already loads listing_title + ai_generated_snapshot and already writes to listings — so with the fixture now guarding the copies, wiring that call site is the next step and is safe to take. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BULK-EDIT GAP IS CLOSED. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx now syncs the listing title when its reverse-projection writes brand/size/color/style back onto the item — so a seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts no longer gets 40 titles still naming the old one. I did NOT inline item-canvas's ~30 lines of orchestration, which would have been a FOURTH copy — of the orchestration this time, the substitution already being shared. Extracted it instead to src/lib/title-sync-patch.ts: buildTitleSyncPatch is pure (inputs -> listings patch, no IO) and owns the decisions wrapped around syncTitle — refuse ebay-origin listings (the sync-precedence guard), move BOTH A/B variants, and flag needs_review when the title was hand-edited away from ai_generated_snapshot or the listing is live. 9 unit tests. That extraction is the actual fix for this story's root cause: the pure helper was shared and the ORCHESTRATION was not, which is why only one surface ever ran it. NOTE the guard is explicit, not inherited: this page filters batch_id + listing_status='draft', which implies GradeThread origin via deriveListingOrigin, but relying on that implicit invariant is how these contracts rot — listing_origin is now selected and checked directly (the column has existed since 00232, far below prod's >=00474, so unlike quality_score it is safe to read). TYPESCRIPT CAUGHT A REAL BUG MID-WIRING: I threaded the new columns onto DraftRow but the save loop iterates EditRow, a different shape — tsc flagged four property errors rather than letting it fail at runtime on undefined. Fixed by carrying listingOrigin/titleVariants through the EditRow mapping. Verified: web suite 2173 passed (was 2164), tsc clean, lint exit 0. REMAINING for passes: the OTHER non-canvas surfaces — identification-verify (edge) and iOS — plus confirming CSV import routes through a covered path. Those are separate surfaces, not this one; buildTitleSyncPatch is deliberately pure so the edge and a future iOS port can consume the same decisions rather than re-deriving them. item-canvas.tsx should also be refactored onto it (it still has the longhand version) — mechanical, but it touches a large working component so it wants its own change. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) item-canvas.tsx REFACTORED onto buildTitleSyncPatch, so the orchestration now exists ONCE in the web app. I had created a second copy in the previous commit by extracting the helper for bulk-edit while leaving the canvas's longhand in place — which is the same duplication this story exists to remove, so leaving it would have been incoherent. ~30 lines of inline logic replaced by one Object.assign; tsc then flagged syncTitle and trimTitleToLimit as unused imports in that file, which is the tidy confirmation that the longhand path is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. PROVED BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BEFORE COMMITTING, not asserted: transcribed the OLD inline block verbatim into a throwaway test and compared it against buildTitleSyncPatch across the full input matrix — locked/unlocked x 4 change-sets x 4 titles (incl. empty, over-long-so-pure-retrim, and a token-boundary near-miss) x 3 variant shapes (incl. null entries) x 4 snapshot states x live/not = 768 combinations, 0 mismatches. Same standard as the 2048-subset proof used for US-1994's route swap. The throwaway was deleted after it passed; the durable coverage is title-sync-patch.test.ts (9 cases) plus the shared edge<->web fixture. Verified: web suite 2173 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. | 2026-07-18 REMAINING SURFACES AUDITED — three of the four need NO work, and the scope is now exactly ONE surface (iOS). Evidence per surface rather than assumption: (1) identification-verify.ts (edge) — NOT APPLICABLE. It updates only { attributes, ai_field_sources }, and the attributes it writes spread the existing map and add just identification_verified + market_title_keywords. Neither is a SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELD, so it never changes a value a title could contain; it annotates provenance/confidence, it does not re-identify the garment. (2) CSV import (src/pages/flipdesk/import.tsx) — NOT APPLICABLE, for a subtler reason worth writing down. It is FILL-ONLY (isBlank(existing[field]) && !isBlank(incoming)), so it can only populate a brand that was previously blank. A blank old value means there is nothing in the title to substitute: syncTitle with a blank `from` is a deliberate no-op, pinned by the shared fixture case 'blank from/to is ignored rather than blanking the title'. Filling a blank brand cannot fix a title that never named one, so wiring sync here would add a call that provably does nothing. Its own comment also confirms 'Listings/sales are left untouched on re-import'. (3) iOS — GENUINE REMAINING GAP, and the only one. ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style to inventory_items via a sparse FieldUpdate, and it is NOT fill-only: it keeps a Snapshot of pre-fill values expressly so an undo can restore them, which only matters if the write can overwrite a populated column. A repo-wide grep shows iOS NEVER writes listing_title anywhere. So an AI-fill on iOS that corrects a brand updates the item column and leaves the listing title naming the old one — the original US-1891 bug, surviving on exactly one surface. CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only (CLAUDE.md), so this needs a macOS session. The port is small and the decisions are already made for it — buildTitleSyncPatch is pure precisely so a Swift equivalent can mirror the same rules (refuse ebay-origin, move both variants, flag needs_review on hand-edited/live), and src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json is the behavioural contract a Swift copy should be tested against so it cannot drift from the two JS copies. | 2026-07-19 THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSIONS WERE NEVER WRITTEN BACK INTO THE CODE OR THE NOTE — fixed. The per-surface audit recorded above settled that there is NO edge item-update endpoint and that bulk-edit was the real gap (since closed), leaving iOS as the only remaining surface. But both durable artifacts still told the old story: services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts opened with '⚠ NOTHING IN THE EDGE SERVICE IMPORTS THIS MODULE' and named 'the edge item update path, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit, CSV import' as the affected surfaces, and vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md filed it under 'Accidentally dead' repeating the same list. THREE OF THOSE FIVE SURFACES ARE NOW WRONG: the edge endpoint does not exist, bulk edit is wired, CSV import is a provable no-op. So the two places a future reader would actually look were both directing them to wire an edge route that was never built — which is precisely the wasted session this story's own scope-correction warned about. Rewrote the module header as a per-surface table with the verdict for each, and an explicit DO NOT WIRE THIS instruction explaining that audit-unwired-exports.mjs will keep reporting it and that the report is correct. Moved the vault entry out of 'Accidentally dead' into a new 'Uncalled by design' section, since leaving a section titled accidental containing an entry titled by-design is its own small lie. NOT DELETED, deliberately: the edge copy is the reference the Swift port mirrors AND one half of the behavioural parity fixture asserted by both suites, so deleting it would remove one side of the only guard keeping the implementations honest. THIS IS THE SAME-COMMIT RULE BEING PAID LATE — the audit happened in a prd note and the artifacts it invalidated were left standing, which is exactly how the original US-1891 'lockstep mirror' claim survived being false. Story stays passes:false: iOS AIItemFieldWriter.swift is untouched and needs a macOS session. Verified: 16 edge + 19 web title-sync tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean.

userStories.title: Backlog integrity: archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED — starting with US-1770's unenforced authenticity safety gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want passes:true to mean the behaviour runs. Three archived stories say DEFERRED in their own notes and are marked passing anyway, and the unwired-export audit confirms at least one of them never shipped. The severe case is US-1770 (authenticity golden-set eval gate): its notes read '[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration' — it was deferred BY the held-migration rule and then closed. runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. The unmet ACs are the safety ones: AC1 requires a candidate prompt to clear an accuracy gate BEFORE activation and AC3 requires per-brand regressions to BLOCK activation — neither is enforced by anything, AC2's human-review routing, by contrast, IS implemented and tested (authenticityNeedsReview, wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054) — an earlier draft of this story claimed otherwise and was wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: US-1770 is reopened (or a successor story filed) and its authenticity eval gate is actually wired: no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate, and a per-brand regression blocks activation

userStories.title: Edge builds ship with release="dev" — every prod edge error is unattributable to a commit (frontend is correct)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to know which build produced a production error. The frontend does: https://gradethread.com serves a bundle tagged release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814", a real commit SHA, so Cloudflare Pages is wiring VITE_RELEASE_SHA correctly. The EDGE does not: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"dev"}, measured 2026-07-18. Root cause is exact — services/edge-functions/Dockerfile:12 declares ARG GIT_SHA=dev and line 13 sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA}; its own comment (lines 9-11) says the builder must pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT, and the Coolify build is not doing so, so the literal default ships. lib/observability.ts:52 releaseSha() therefore returns "dev" and tags every Sentry event, structured log and trace with it. This is an ASYMMETRY between the two halves of the system, and the half that is blind is the one handling grading, payments, eBay writes and webhooks.
acceptanceCriteria: The Coolify build passes the commit into the image (GIT_SHA build arg = $SOURCE_COMMIT or the platform equivalent), so RELEASE_SHA is a real SHA in production.
GET /health on production returns a release that matches the deployed commit — verify by measuring the endpoint after a deploy, not by reading the config.
Sentry edge events carry that release, so an error can be attributed to a deploy and "did the fix ship?" is answerable. Confirm a real event is tagged.

A guard so this cannot silently regress: the edge should REFUSE to report healthy-and-production while release is the literal default "dev"/"unknown" — or at minimum surface it as a degraded feature in /health/ready features{} alongside the existing observability entry, which currently reports "ok" while the release is meaningless.
Document the build-arg requirement in COOLIFY.md next to the other deploy settings, since the Dockerfile comment alone did not survive contact with the actual deploy.
userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/Observability][Measured] Found 2026-07-18 during the cross-platform production-readiness deep dive, by querying prod rather than reading config. EVIDENCE, all live: /health -> {"status":"ok","service":"gradethread-edge-functions","env":"production","release":"dev","errorTracking":"enabled"}; the frontend bundle /assets/index-CIbHzx5V.js contains release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814" (which is also proof Pages auto-deployed that commit). WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC TAG: with every edge event tagged "dev" you cannot (a) attribute a production error to a build, (b) tell whether a deployed fix actually shipped, (c) see a regression appear at a release boundary, or (d) make a rollback decision on evidence — and ROLLBACK.md assumes you can identify the bad build. Note errorTracking reports "enabled" and /health/ready features.observability reports "ok", so the health surface actively says observability is fine while the release dimension of it is inert; that is why AC4 asks for a guard rather than just a config fix. The fix itself is small (one build arg); the reason it survived this long is that nothing measured it. | 2026-07-19 AC1/AC4/AC5 DONE; AC2/AC3 need a deploy to confirm. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A MISSING BUILD ARG, and the fix is DECLARATIVE rather than another instruction: docker-compose.coolify.yml now carries build.args GIT_SHA: dev. That placement is the whole point — the Dockerfile has carried a comment telling the builder to pass GIT_SHA since it was written, and per this story's own evidence that comment did not survive contact with the actual deploy. A build arg in compose is APPLIED BY THE PLATFORM instead of remembered by a person, so documenting it harder would have reproduced the same failure. The :-dev fallback keeps a plain local docker compose build working. AC4 DONE and it is the anti-regression half: the observability feature group now requires SENTRY_DSN *and* a real RELEASE_SHA, so /health/ready reports observability DEGRADED while the release is a placeholder — previously it reported 'ok' in the exact prod state this story measured (errorTracking enabled, release 'dev'), which is the false confidence that let it sit unnoticed. isRealReleaseSha is deliberately permissive on FORM: it rejects the placeholder set (dev/unknown/local/none/latest/empty) but accepts short SHAs and tags, because the measured failure was the literal ARG default surviving the build, not a malformed SHA — requiring 40 hex chars would break tag-based deploys for no benefit. 4 tests, including the exact prod state as a case. AC5 DONE in COOLIFY.md with a MEASURE-DO-NOT-READ verification step (curl /health | jq .release), plus the warning that deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant needs the same args block. ⚠ REMAINING AND GENUINELY UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: AC2 (measure /health after a deploy) and AC3 (confirm a real Sentry event carries the release). Both require the deploy to actually happen. What HAS changed is that a regression now announces itself on /health/ready instead of waiting for someone to think to curl. [2026-07-19 AC4+AC5 DONE, AC1-AC3 NEED THE COOLIFY BUILD + A PROD MEASUREMENT] AC4: /health/ready now carries features.release, degraded whenever the release is unattributable (dev / unknown / empty / whitespace, case-insensitive). Deliberately a SEPARATE key from features.observability: that group reports ok whenever a Sentry DSN is present, which stays true and stays misleading while every event it ships is tagged dev. Also deliberately does NOT flip the service to not_ready — the AC allowed either, and refusing readiness on an untagged build would pull grading, payments and webhooks out of rotation to protect observability. health.ts already argues this exact principle for the schema probe (a probe that can fail a container over a diagnostic is a worse bug than the blind spot it fixes). A test asserts ready stays true. releaseReadiness() is pure; 5 new tests. AC5 FINDING: COOLIFY.md already had a US-2001 build-args section from an earlier pass, and it CLAIMED /health/ready reports features.observability as degraded on a placeholder release. That was FALSE — nothing implemented it. The documentation described a guard that did not exist, which is a plausible reason nobody built one; same defect class as US-2035 (comment asserting a property the code lacks) and US-2123 (copy advertising an ungranted entitlement). Doc now names the real key, shows the curl, and records the correction rather than quietly overwriting it. STILL OPEN (all need the deploy, not code): AC1 the Coolify build must actually pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT — docker-compose.coolify.yml declares it but prod measured release=dev on 2026-07-18, so either the deploy uses docker-compose.yml or the Build Args field is unset. AC2 verify by curling /health after a deploy. AC3 confirm a real Sentry event carries the SHA. The new features.release entry makes AC2 checkable without remembering the curl.

userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Alerting][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. userStories.title: GDPR erasure misses an entire class of email-keyed PII, including full rendered email bodies
userStories.description: As a data subject, when I delete my account I want my personal data actually erased. Both the erasure endpoint (routes/account.ts:310-496) and the RPC (00043_delete_account_rpc.sql:33-36) rely EXCLUSIVELY on the ON DELETE CASCADE chain rooted at auth.users, which reaches only tables with an FK to users. These tables hold real PII keyed by EMAIL and are untouched: email_deliveries (recipient, subject, and html — the full rendered body of every critical email, 00095:9-13), email_consent_audit (email, ip, 00296:36), email_subscribers, marketing_send_log, waitlist_entries, newsletter_issue_recipients (no FK at all), email_journey_step_sends, guarantee_claims (third-party buyer PII). The ON DELETE SET NULL cases are sharpest: they sever the link while PRESERVING the email address — the exact identifier a subject would cite in an erasure complaint. account.ts:306-307 asserts the cascade 'wipes every public table keyed to it', which is true and precisely the wrong invariant, because these are keyed to an email.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an explicit email-keyed purge before auth.admin.deleteUser: delete from email_deliveries / marketing_send_log / email_journey_step_sends / newsletter_issue_recipients by the user email; anonymize email_consent_audit / waitlist_entries / email_subscribers.
email_suppressions is a DELIBERATE exception — a suppression list must survive erasure or the user starts receiving mail again. Hash the address there rather than deleting it, and document why.
Add a test asserting that after deletion NO row in any table matches the deleted address. That assertion is the only durable guard, since the bug class is 'a new table keyed by email'.
Re-word the comment at account.ts:306-307 so the next reader is not reassured by an invariant that does not cover email-keyed tables.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/GDPR] Found 2026-07-18 by the data-integrity deep dive. Severity comes precisely from the endpoint SUCCEEDING: it returns {deleted:true} and sends a confirmation email while the address and the full HTML of every payment-failed and grade-ready message remain queryable forever. The surrounding compliance work is genuinely good — account.ts export, a deletion log that does not block erasure on logging failure (:439-442), data-retention keeping the non-PII grade while purging PII — which is what makes this gap easy to miss: everything around it is correct. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). AC1 DONE: account.ts step 3c purges email-keyed PII BEFORE auth.admin.deleteUser (ordering is load-bearing — after the cascade users.email is gone and there is nothing left to key the purge on). ⚠ I CORRECTED THE STORY'S OWN PRESCRIPTION while implementing it: the AC said to ANONYMIZE waitlist_entries and email_subscribers, but both declare email as NOT NULL (and UNIQUE), so nulling would simply fail and leave the PII sitting there — an 'anonymize' that silently no-ops is worse than no attempt, because the code reads as handled. Those two are hard-DELETEd instead (a deleted account has no waitlist position to hold and no subscription to keep; unsubscribe protection does NOT depend on them — that is email_suppressions). Hard-delete: email_deliveries (the one carrying full rendered html bodies), marketing_send_log, email_journey_step_sends, newsletter_issue_recipients, waitlist_entries, email_subscribers. Anonymize: email_consent_audit (email + ip nulled) because both columns ARE nullable and the row proves WHEN a consent action happened — a record that outlives the subject once identifiers are gone. Every column name was VERIFIED against the migrations rather than assumed; these tables disagree on whether the column is `recipient` or `email`, and a wrong name would look exactly like a successful purge (we log the 42703 and continue). AC2 DONE: email_suppressions deliberately preserved + a test that fails if anyone starts deleting it, because forgetting a bounced/complained address makes it start receiving mail again — harming the very person erasure protects. AC4 DONE: the endpoint header comment claimed the cascade 'wipes every public table keyed to it', which was reassuring in exactly the wrong way; it now states that the cascade covers user_id-keyed tables ONLY and points at step 3c. NEW TEST account-email-purge_test.ts (4 cases). The durable one is an INVENTORY GUARD that rediscovers candidates from the migration corpus — any table declaring an email/recipient/claimant_email text column, not cascade-deleted from users, and not handled by the route, fails the build with an explicit EXEMPT escape hatch. That matters because the bug class is ADDITIVE ('someone adds a table that stores an email'), so a hand-maintained list would decay the same way the original gap formed. ⚠ IT ALSO CAUGHT A FLAW IN MY OWN TEST: the first version used substring matching, and since the route's COMMENTS name these tables, a guard could have passed on prose alone — a guard satisfied by a comment describing the fix is worse than no guard because it reads as proof. Now keyed on a QUOTED occurrence, which only code produces. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: removing email_deliveries from the purge fails BOTH the explicit-list test and the inventory guard independently; restoring it passes. Guard is not vacuous — it identifies 9 email-bearing tables across 201 parsed, of which 7 are handled and 2 exempt. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4159 edge tests pass. STILL passes:false on AC3 — a behavioural 'after deletion NO row anywhere matches the address' test needs a live DB (the endpoint is a Hono handler over the service-role client with no injection seam), so it belongs in the db lane. Also un-run: the actual backfill question of what to do about addresses ALREADY retained for users deleted before this fix — that is a prod data task and arguably its own story.

userStories.title: The data-retention PII sweep cannot advance past its first batch — GDPR retention silently unenforced
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want expired submission images actually purged. lib/data-retention.ts:36-50 selects submissions past the cutoff with NO filter for whether images remain and NO ORDER BY, despite the comment claiming 'still have images to purge'. It takes 200 arbitrary expired submissions, looks up their images (:53-56), and returns early when there are none (:63-65). So after the first run purges those 200, every subsequent nightly run re-selects the same already-purged rows, finds zero images, and returns {objects_deleted: 0} — newer expired submissions are NEVER reached. The cron stays perpetually green while enforcement stopped at run two.
acceptanceCriteria: Filter to submissions that still HAVE images and order deterministically, e.g. .select('id, submission_images!inner(id)').lt('created_at', cutoff).order('created_at', {ascending:true}).limit(BATCH_LIMIT).
Add a regression test asserting a SECOND sweep over a fresh dataset still returns objects_deleted > 0 — the single assertion that distinguishes this bug from correct behaviour.
Backfill: quantify how much past-retention imagery accumulated while the sweep was stalled, and drain it.
Emit an ops event when a sweep finds nothing across N consecutive runs while past-cutoff rows exist.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/GDPR] Found 2026-07-18 by the data-integrity deep dive. Compounds two other findings: the purged originals are EXIF/GPS-bearing (account.ts:377-379), and enforcement also depends on a hand-registered Coolify cron that nothing monitors (see the cron-stall story). A perpetually-green cron doing nothing is the pattern this whole session keeps finding — a check that reports success is indistinguishable from one that works, unless something asserts the work happened. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). The scan now drives off submission_images joined to submissions!inner(created_at), filtered on submissions.created_at < cutoff, ordered created_at ASC, limited to BATCH_LIMIT. That choice is deliberate and structural rather than cosmetic: the sweep can no longer stall BY CONSTRUCTION, because the query only ever returns rows that still exist and deleting them is precisely what this function does, so every run strictly advances. (The alternative — keeping the submissions-first scan but adding an images-exist filter — would have worked too, but it leaves the two-step shape that made the stall possible in the first place.) ORDER BY added so 'the next 200' is a well-defined set instead of Postgres row order. submissions_processed is now the distinct submission count within the batch, so the reported metric keeps its meaning. NEW TEST src/tests/data-retention_test.ts (3 cases) — and I want to be honest about what it is: a STRUCTURAL guard, not a behavioural one. purgeExpiredGradingPii talks to the service-role client with no injection seam, so two sweeps over a fixture would need a live DB (that belongs in the db lane). But the defect IS a property of query shape, so shape is the right thing to pin. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: I checked out the original buggy version and all three assertions failed, then restored the fix and all three passed — the guard demonstrably catches the real historical bug rather than merely describing it. STILL OPEN: AC3 (quantify + drain the backlog of past-retention imagery that accumulated while the sweep was stalled — needs prod DB access) and AC4 (ops event when a sweep repeatedly finds nothing while past-cutoff rows exist). | 2026-07-19 AC4 DONE. The sweep now NOTICES when it stops advancing. AC1 and AC2 shipped previously (query shape fixed, structural guard added and negative-verified against the original buggy version); this is the RUNTIME counterpart, and the distinction is the point: the shape guard proves the code is right TODAY, while this proves the BEHAVIOUR is right in production — which is the thing that actually failed. A stall can return in a form no source assertion would catch: a bad cutoff, an RLS change, a storage outage, a permissions regression. THE SIGNAL IS DELIBERATELY A CONJUNCTION — zero objects deleted AND past-cutoff rows still remaining. Zero-deleted ALONE is the normal steady state once the backlog is drained, so alerting on it would fire every night forever, which is exactly how a channel becomes noise and stops being read (the same reasoning behind the cron-fleet suppression window in US-2004). Escalation is by CONSECUTIVE RUNS rather than elapsed time, because the failure is 'the sweep is not advancing' and runs are the unit in which that is true: one odd run is a warning, three consecutive is critical. The streak is carried on the ops event payload and read back next run, mirroring the loadLastAlert pattern already used by jobs-cron-fleet rather than inventing a second mechanism. decideRetentionStall is pure with 5 tests; the whole check is best-effort in a try/catch for the same stated reason as the prunes beside it — the stall DETECTOR must never be the reason the purge itself reports failure. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by weakening the conjunction to a bare zero-check (the tempting simplification): the 'nothing left to do is NOT a stall' test goes red, which is the assertion standing between this alert and nightly noise. Also aligned the severity vocabulary to ops-events' 'warning' rather than casting my own 'warn' through — a cast would have compiled and produced an event severity nothing downstream ranks. Verified: edge 4278 passed, deno check + lint clean. STILL OPEN: AC3 alone — quantify and drain the backlog of past-retention imagery that accumulated while the sweep was stalled. That needs prod DB access, and note the new alert will now TELL you the size of that backlog on the next run (past_cutoff_remaining in the event payload), so AC3 gets its number for free once this deploys.

userStories.title: Migration tracking is a max-watermark, so a skipped mid-sequence migration is undetectable — this already happened
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to know EVERY migration applied, not just the highest-numbered one. latest_schema_migration() (00254:63-79) returns GREATEST(max(cli), max(self)); apply-prod-migrations.sh:29-31 skips any file whose prefix is <= current; schema-version.ts:41 compares a single number. A gap in the MIDDLE of the range is structurally invisible — the watermark only moves forward and a file below it is never re-applied. 00254:108-111 even seeds 00252/00253 on the assumption that reaching 00254 means 00250..00253 ran. NOT THEORETICAL: 00322_api_keys_webhook_url_idempotent.sql:1-16 documents the realized incident — 00005's non-idempotent ADD COLUMN webhook_url never landed in prod, the watermark advanced anyway, and EVERY finalized grade silently no-op'd its developer webhook delivery with 42703 for an unknown duration.
acceptanceCriteria: Change the boot guard from a watermark comparison to a COMPLETENESS check: ship the expected version set as a manifest in the edge image and fail on any missing version, not just on max.

Run a one-time prod-vs-migrations COLUMN-LEVEL diff (information_schema.columns against the parsed corpus). No such check exists today, and it is the only thing that would have caught webhook_url. The ~253 pre-00254 files carry no self-record footer, so any could have partially failed the same way.
Note post-00254 hygiene is already excellent — all 224 files >= 00254 carry the footer, zero exceptions — so this is about the historical tail, not new work.
userStories.notes: [P2][DB/Ops] Found 2026-07-18 by the data-integrity deep dive, dovetailing with a measurement made the same day: /health/ready reports schema {expected:00476, applied:00476, status:match}, which proves the MAX is current and proves nothing about intermediate versions. That is exactly the residual risk here. Re-running the tail via apply-prod-migrations.sh is idempotent and remains the cheap mitigation; the manifest check is the durable one. | 2026-07-19 AC1 DONE; AC2 needs prod DB access. The boot guard is no longer a watermark comparison. scripts/gen-migration-manifest.mjs generates lib/migration-manifest.ts (231 footer-era versions) into the edge image, and checkSchemaCompleteness() reads the WHOLE applied set and reports two opposite findings: MISSING (in the manifest, never applied — the mid-sequence gap a max comparison structurally cannot see, since the watermark only moves forward and apply-prod-migrations.sh skips anything at or below it) and UNEXPECTED (recorded in applied_migrations with no migration file in this build). MANIFEST STARTS AT 00254 DELIBERATELY: the self-recording footer was introduced by that migration, so the ~253 files below it legitimately do not self-record and their absence carries no signal. Including them would emit ~253 permanent false 'missing' reports, and a check that always fires is a check nobody reads. THE UNEXPECTED DIRECTION IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IS WHY I BUILT IT THIS WAY: measured live this session, /health/ready reports applied=00479 while NO 00479 file has ever existed in this repo. That is the exact phantom this half detects, and it is the reason 00480-00485 were numbered around it — reusing 00479 would have satisfied the boot guard off a stale row even if the SQL never ran, which is the precise failure the guard exists to prevent. On the next edge deploy the container log will NAME the phantom, which answers PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's open question 1 without a psql session; I noted that there. DELIBERATELY NON-FATAL, unlike the behind-max check, and this is the judgement to review: it is a brand-new assertion over 231 historical migrations that has NEVER run against prod. If any one of them failed to self-record years ago, making it fatal would refuse to boot the whole service on the first deploy containing this code — converting an unknown into an outage, which is the same trap I avoided in US-2003 (declined to fail at boot on a missing alert channel). It logs at ERROR instead. PROMOTE IT TO FATAL once prod is observed clean; that is a deliberate follow-up, not an oversight. Fails CLOSED in the sense that matters: a read error returns checked:false, which must never render as 'clean'. 6 tests including the mid-sequence gap where the MAX still matches (the case the old guard could not see) and the 00479 phantom as a literal case, plus a drift guard asserting the generated manifest matches supabase/migrations on disk — otherwise adding a migration without regenerating would silently shrink what the guard checks. AC2 (one-time prod-vs-migrations COLUMN-LEVEL diff against information_schema) still needs DB access and remains the only thing that would catch a migration that applied PARTIALLY. Verified: edge 4272 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Single edge replica with no graceful shutdown — every deploy strands in-flight work for 6-15 minutes
userStories.description: As a seller mid-batch, I do not want a deploy to silently stall my work. SCALING.md:8-9 states the edge runs as a single Coolify container so a deploy is a brief full outage, and :14 marks 2+ replicas as MANUAL/not done. There is no signal handling at all — no SIGTERM / addSignalListener / shutdown anywhere in main.ts (1638 lines) — so in-flight requests are KILLED, not drained. Recovery is by sweep rather than drain: flipdesk-autolister.ts:114 JOB_STALE_MS = 6min, :117 BATCH_STALE_MS = 15min, reclaim crons at */5. The ~30s outage documented at SCALING.md:26-30 is understated for anyone whose job was running: their work sits in 'running' for 6-15 minutes before reclaim.
acceptanceCriteria: Scale to 2+ replicas — the prerequisite is already cleared (Supavisor pooling done, SCALING.md:22).
Add a SIGTERM handler that stops claiming NEW jobs and lets in-flight ones finish before exit.
Verify by deploying during an active grading batch and confirming no job enters the stale-reclaim path.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Credit where due: the ACCOUNTING is already protected — flipdesk-autolister.ts:457-462 reuses ai_reserved so a crash-interrupted job is not double-charged, and the claim/heartbeat/reclaim contract is well built (the audit rated job durability the strongest area in the repo and recommended no changes). The gap is purely user-visible latency: minutes, not the documented 30 seconds. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE; AC1/AC3 need Coolify + a deploy. New lib/lifecycle.ts installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that stop claiming NEW work immediately and drain in-flight requests before exit (SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS, default 8s — deliberately INSIDE Docker's 10s SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL grace, since a drain deadline longer than the grace period is a drain that gets killed halfway having already stopped claiming). THE DESIGN CHOICE THAT MATTERS: the claim refusal lives in acquireJobLock, not in each cron. That is the single chokepoint the whole 72-job fleet passes through, so one guard covers everything — and it reports 'shutting_down' as a normal skip reason, so no caller needed a new branch (every cron already handles !acquired). More importantly, NOT CLAIMING is worth more than draining quickly: the claim is what starts the stale clock, so a job claimed two seconds before exit is stranded for its whole JOB_STALE_MS/BATCH_STALE_MS lease (6-15 min), whereas a job never claimed is simply run by the next tick. Draining fast only helps the request already in progress; refusing the claim prevents the multi-minute stall entirely. 10 tests. ⚠ MY FIRST NEGATIVE VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND I CAUGHT IT — recording because the failure mode is subtle and will recur: I removed the guard with a multi-line node string replace, the test still passed, and I nearly accepted that. The file is CRLF (enforced by .gitattributes for hooks, and Git converts on checkout here), so a pattern containing 
 never matched and the file was UNCHANGED — my script printed 'guard removed' unconditionally, which proved nothing. Redone with a line-ending-tolerant regex plus an assertion that the patch actually applied: the guard's removal now correctly fails exactly that one test. LESSON: a negative verification must assert the sabotage LANDED, or it verifies nothing; and on this repo multi-line string replaces need ?
. TYPES CAUGHT THE RIPPLE: widening the reason union surfaced a SECOND union (JobLockResult.skipped) that would otherwise have silently diverged. Also corrected vault/10-ops/scaling.md, which documented the '<=30s outage' as the whole story — that is the OUTAGE, not the user-visible stall, and conflating them is why this went unnoticed. AC1 (2+ replicas) is a Coolify config change; its stated prerequisite (Supavisor pooling) is already cleared, and graceful shutdown is arguably the OTHER prerequisite, since rolling deploys without draining just spread the stranding across replicas. AC3 needs a deploy during an active batch. NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE SWEEPS, and the note says so: SIGKILL/OOM/host loss bypass all of this, so the reclaim crons remain the correctness backstop; this only improves the orderly case, which is every routine deploy. Verified: edge 4254 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/Payments] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Smallest fix-to-impact ratio in the audit: one line converts silent revenue loss into a page. Blocked in practice on the alert-channel story (setting the webhook secrets), since the fan-out currently has nowhere to go. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). recordWebhookDeadLetter now emits a CRITICAL ops event alongside the existing captureException, so a dropped webhook reaches the on-call fan-out instead of only Sentry (whose routing is separately unverified — US-2003). userStories.notes: [P2][Security/Testing] Found 2026-07-18 by the security deep dive. CRITICAL CONTEXT so this is not misread as a breach: the audit traced all 740 .from() call sites on multi-tenant tables, taint-traced request-supplied ids into filters, and machine-diffed every mounted route against the middleware tables — and could NOT confirm a single cross-tenant data hole. Every unscoped-LOOKING query hand-verified as parent-verified (inventory_items!inner(user_id), loadListingOwned, loadReconcilePair, or a locally-minted id). The US-268 discipline is genuinely being followed. This story closes the TEST gap and inverts a default that currently makes unauthenticated exposure a silent one-line mistake. | 2026-07-18 THREE OF FOUR ACs (agent loop). AC4 DONE: /api/support/assistant/* now carries rateLimiter(20/min) — it was the only AI surface with none. Not an open faucet before (support-assistant.ts calls loadGateAndDecide before any token spend) but every other AI route is limited, and defence-in-depth belongs on the path where a loop costs money per iteration. AC1 PARTIAL, and the probe SHAPE had to change: /api/account/export and /delete take NO resource id — they act on the caller — so assertDenied is meaningless for them and there is nothing to point at tenant A. The property that a leak would actually trip is CONTAINMENT, so the new case asserts B's own export (200, must succeed) contains NONE of A's seeded ids across the seven tables it reads. Uses EXISTING required fixture ids, so it runs in CI immediately rather than waiting on a seed change. Also added an env-gated remove-bg probe (that route writes to the PUBLIC item-photos bucket, so a cross-tenant call would publish another seller's photo) — deliberately NOT added to REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS, because a case that hard-fails CI before the seed script provides TEST_USER_A_PHOTO_ID would simply get muted, which is worse than skipping loudly. Plus an unauthenticated-read probe on equity. ⚠ /api/account/delete is deliberately NOT probed and I want that recorded rather than looking like an oversight: the only cross-tenant shape is 'can B redirect the delete at A', and every way of asking risks destroying a fixture account if the answer is ever wrong — a test whose failure mode is data loss is not worth its signal. The route reads only c.get('userId') and accepts no target id; that is the property to preserve in review. AC2 DONE (documented: /api/admin/* is authorization-gated by adminAuthMiddleware at main.ts:730-731, so it is lower priority by design, not by neglect). AC3 — I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO WHAT THE AC ASKED, and this is the judgement call to review. The AC says invert to app.use('/api/flipdesk/ebay/*', authMiddleware) + skip-list. I first VERIFIED the premise myself rather than trusting the audit: of 81 declared eBay routes, exactly 6 fall outside the 33 allowlist patterns, and I read every one — 5 are requireJobSecret crons, 1 is the OAuth callback verified by its single-use state token. So there is NO live gap, confirming the audit independently. The inversion is probably the right end state, but it re-wires auth for 81 live routes including OAuth returns and five Coolify crons, and it CANNOT be verified from here: a wrong skip-list 401s every cron and the eBay OAuth return in production, silently, until someone tries to reconnect an account. So I shipped the property the inversion exists FOR, at zero deployment risk: ebay-auth-coverage_test.ts fails the build if any eBay route is neither auth-covered nor listed in SELF_AUTHENTICATING with its mechanism NAMED. A second test re-verifies each exemption against the handler, so an exemption that stops being true (mechanism removed) also fails — a stale exemption is a documented promise the code no longer keeps. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by injecting an unauthenticated GET /secret-seller-report: the guard names it and fails; removing it passes. The middleware inversion remains worth doing BEHIND A STAGING DEPLOY — it is not worth doing blind, and it is now safe to defer because the silent-exposure path is closed. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4169 edge tests pass. STILL passes:false: the new tenant cases only prove themselves when the tenant-isolation workflow runs with its two-tenant fixture (they skip locally by design), and AC3's inversion is deferred rather than done.

userStories.title: Android is a plumbing skeleton, but its README and 19 passing stories claim near-parity
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the Android backlog to reflect reality. Android has genuinely good infrastructure — auth, a Room sync engine, mutation queue, delete reconciliation, telemetry, app-lock, CameraX capture, ~70 Kotlin files. It has no product: every navigation destination except one is a literal placeholder (ui/shell/AppShell.kt:162-175 — Home, Inventory, Money, Marketplaces, Settings, Details intake, AutoLister all render SectionPlaceholder; only capture/photos is real). Corroborating: Android calls exactly ONE edge endpoint in the entire codebase (/api/flipdesk/photo-profiles) versus iOS's 77 and web's ~530 — no grading submit, no inventory read, no eBay, no payments. Two documentation problems compound it: android/README.md:31-39 presents a package map for grading / inventory / marketplaces / money / billing whose directories contain ZERO .kt files, and :3 calls it 'at iOS parity'. And 19 stories are marked passes:true with no implementing code — verified: US-1380 Glance widgets (zero 'glance' references anywhere, no AppWidgetProvider in the manifest), US-1378 FCM push (no FirebaseMessaging reference), US-1383 Settings (routes to a placeholder), US-1384/1385/1387/1388/1389, US-1393 localization (no values-* locale dirs). The pattern is clean: US-1300-1328 (infrastructure) are genuinely done; US-1378-1396 is a contiguous block marked done without code.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-open the falsely-passing Android stories (start with the verified list: US-1380, US-1378, US-1383, US-1384, US-1385, US-1387, US-1388, US-1389, US-1393) and audit the rest of the US-1378-1396 block the same way.
Correct android/README.md — remove the 'at iOS parity' claim and the package map for directories that contain no code. This is the first document a new engineer or a diligence reviewer reads.
Re-baseline the Android estimate: real completion is closer to 29/98 than the 48/98 the backlog implies, and ALL remaining work is the expensive UI/feature half rather than a polish pass.
Decide explicitly whether Android is on the launch plan. If it is, the remaining work is essentially the whole app.
userStories.notes: [P1][Android/Backlog-integrity] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. This is the same class as US-1996 (archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED) but larger and on a platform nobody is looking at. The state is more misleading than a plain stub would be: sophisticated offline-sync infrastructure attached to zero features reads as 'nearly done' to anyone who opens the project and sees the hard parts solved. NOT verified: whether the 50 OPEN Android stories are correctly open — only the passing ones were falsified. | [2026-07-27] AC1 DONE: audited the whole US-1378..1396 block, not just the verified subset — 14 stories re-opened as never-implemented (1378/1379/1380/1381/1382/1384/1385/1386/1387/1388/1389/1390/1392/1393) and 2 re-opened as partial (1391 has no signing config; 1395 has no androidTest/E2E). US-1383 was falsely passing and is now genuinely implemented. AC2 DONE: android/README.md no longer claims iOS parity, the package map lists only packages that contain code, and a Status section names what is and is not built.
