Getting the real figure needs Stripe's proration preview — invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the PROPOSED subscription_items plus a subscription_proration_date — which is a new endpoint, and one whose output I cannot verify from this sandbox (the Stripe MCP connector is unauthorized; see US-2033, blocked the same way). WHY THAT BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOWS: a confirmation dialog that states a WRONG prorated amount is worse than the current no-dialog state. Today the defect is an OMISSION — the click is the purchase and nothing is stated. A dialog showing an unverified number converts that into an AFFIRMATIVE MISSTATEMENT about a charge, on the exact surface this compliance batch exists to fix. That is the same reasoning applied in US-2117 (refuse to write a partial agreement), US-2119 (refuse to send a notice with no date) and US-2116 (refuse to record a client-supplied IP): on an evidentiary or money surface, a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an acknowledged gap. WHAT THE NEXT PASS NEEDS, so it is short: (1) a preview endpoint wrapping invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the target plan's price id, returning prorated-now / new-recurring / interval / next-renewal; (2) a confirmation dialog — DowngradePreviewDialog is the established pattern to mirror, and AC3's 'apply the same treatment to downgrades' is already satisfied by it, which is why upgrades being bare is the anomaly rather than the norm; (3) route the upgrade mutation through it; (4) AC4's test that the mutation cannot fire without confirmation. AC2 (capture the same consent artifact as a new subscription) is now CHEAP because US-2117 landed: subscription_agreements + recordAgreedTerms already exist, and an in-place upgrade produces a customer.subscription.updated event that already flows through handleSubscriptionChange — which now calls recordAgreedTerms. So an upgrade ALREADY writes an agreement row with the new plan/interval/amount. Worth verifying rather than assuming, but the plumbing is in place. The FIGURES are the blocker, and they need a Stripe session — not more code reading. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h); edge unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno), CI + a real Stripe test env confirm. The in-place upgrade (payments.ts /flipdesk/subscribe, existing paid sub → higher tier) called stripe.subscriptions.update with create_prorations on a single click — no disclosure, no consent. AC1: new POST /flipdesk/upgrade-preview computes the real proration via stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming (simulating the item swap with subscription_items + subscription_proration_behavior) and returns amount_due_today_cents, currency, new_recurring_cents, interval, next_renewal_at (current_period_end). AC4 (server-enforced, the strong guarantee): the in-place path now refuses unless the body carries confirmUpgrade:true — returns 409 { code:'UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED', requiresConfirmation:true } and does NOT mutate; the gate sits BEFORE subscriptions.update. AC2: on a confirmed change it writes a consent artifact to flipdesk_subscription_events (event_type 'in_place_change_confirmed', from/to plan, raw_payload with prices+interval+source) — the equivalent of Checkout's disclosure. Web: new UpgradePreviewDialog (mirrors the existing DowngradePreviewDialog) fetches the preview and discloses amount today / new recurring rate+frequency / next renewal before confirming; the plan picker's upgrade CTA opens it for a paid→higher change and calls subscribe with confirmUpgrade:true on confirm. A free→paid upgrade still goes straight to Stripe Checkout (which discloses on its own hosted page), so it skips the dialog. AC3: downgrades already route through DowngradePreviewDialog and interval switches through the Stripe billing portal (both disclose/confirm) — the upgrade path was the only gap, now closed. TESTS: edge upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts asserts (source-structural, this repo's idiom for Stripe-heavy routes — cf. subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts) that the confirmUpgrade gate precedes the mutation, the preview endpoint + retrieveUpcoming exist, and the consent artifact is written; all 10 assertions verified green by replicating them in node against payments.ts. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b + eslint clean; billing+hooks vitest 36/36 green; only flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog uses useFlipdeskSubscribe and only use-billing-summary calls the endpoint, so no other caller now 409s. KEPT passes:false: the edge route + the Stripe preview call are not runnable here (no deno, no Stripe test key); run the deno lane + exercise a real paid→higher upgrade against Stripe test mode to confirm the prorated amount + consent row, then flip.

userStories.title: No advance renewal reminder exists anywhere — annual plans are charged silently
userStories.description: Confirmed absence, verified three ways: invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch (services/edge-functions/src/routes/webhooks.ts:244-281, falls through to a default log-and-drop at :281); no cron in jobs-cron-fleet.ts sends one; and the only upcoming_invoice reference is a read-only pull for the billing page (payments.ts:1142). The first notice a user receives about a renewal is sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail (email.ts:1183), sent AFTER the money is taken. Yearly price IDs exist for all five paid tiers (src/lib/constants.ts:1344-1366) and flow through the identical path — interval only changes a display string — so an annual subscriber is charged a full year's fee with no prior contact whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.upcoming and send a transactional advance renewal notice stating the amount, the date of the charge, the plan, and how to cancel before it.
Configure the Stripe lead time explicitly rather than relying on the default, and set a longer lead for annual plans than monthly.
Send via deliverEmail as a TRANSACTIONAL category — it must not be routed through the drip/marketing engine where opt-out, suppression or frequency caps can silently drop it.
Also handle customer.subscription.trial_will_end.
Test that an annual subscription produces a reminder before renewal and that a marketing opt-out does not suppress it.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Comms] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Advance notice before a long-term renewal is a common state-ARL requirement and we have annual plans in production. Cheapest structural fix in the batch: one webhook case reusing existing email infrastructure. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 + AC4 + AC5 DONE (mechanism, not copy — the fourth compliance story that did not need counsel). invoice.upcoming is now HANDLED and sends sendRenewalReminderEmail, a NEW template deliberately separate from sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail: a receipt confirms something that happened, this warns about something that has not, and the only action that matters — cancel before the date — is meaningless on a receipt. It states the plan, the amount, the exact charge date and how to cancel. AC3: category subscription_renewal_reminder is registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES, so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional even if marketing:true is explicitly requested — pinned by a test, because if that ever flips, an opt-out silently drops the only advance warning of a charge and the exact defect returns. AC4 customer.subscription.trial_will_end is handled too, and THE DISJOINTNESS IS THE INTERESTING PART: our signup trial has NO Stripe subscription (handle_new_user grants it directly), and US-2120's cron filters flipdesk_subscription_id IS NULL. This event fires only for a STRIPE-managed trial — someone who started a PAID subscription with a trial period — which is exactly the user that cron skips. The two populations cannot overlap, so neither path double-sends. A test asserts the cron keeps that filter, since removing it would make both fire for the same person. It reuses sendTrialExpiringEmail rather than minting a second trial template, because two near-identical trial emails drift. DECLINES TO SEND WITHOUT A DATE: if Stripe supplies neither next_payment_attempt nor period_end the handler returns. A notice that cannot say WHEN is not a notice, and 'you will be charged at some point' is worse than silence. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement. TWO OF MY OWN EARLIER ARTEFACTS CAUGHT THIS CHANGE, which is the guards working: (1) the US-2128 test asserting invoice.upcoming and trial_will_end were on the known-ignored list went RED, correctly — they had graduated to real handlers, and a handled event must never ALSO be listed as ignored or the list is lying. Rewritten to assert the list stays annotated rather than naming those two specifically. (2) Removing them left an ORPHANED group header ('Covered by their own stories / other handlers.') heading an empty group — deleted. STILL OPEN: AC2 only — configure the Stripe lead time explicitly (and longer for annual than monthly). That is a Stripe dashboard/API setting, not code: Stripe decides when invoice.upcoming fires, and the default is 3 days. Worth doing since a 3-day warning on a full YEAR's charge is thin, but it cannot be set from here. Verified: edge 4306 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE (US-2089-style stale box). This story's premise — 'invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch' — is no longer true: webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to handleInvoiceUpcoming (:284) AND customer.subscription.trial_will_end to handleTrialWillEnd (:294), both carrying US-2119 attribution comments. Closed by that work; the story was simply never flipped. Found while triaging the P1 Compliance/Comms cluster for US-2122. NOT marking passes:true from here, because I did not verify AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time configuration, which is a dashboard setting) or AC5's live test — someone with Stripe access should confirm those two before closing. | 2026-07-22 ADDED THE MISSING AC3/AC5 GUARD (agent loop), passes:false held on the external ACs. The prior note flagged that it "did not verify AC5"; the transactional half of AC5 (and AC3) had NO test at all — sendRenewalReminderEmail uses category subscription_renewal_reminder (email.ts:2936) which IS in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts:49), so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional and a marketing opt-out cannot suppress it — but nothing pinned that. If someone reclassified it, the renewal reminder would silently become marketing-suppressible and an annual subscriber could be charged with no warning (the exact US-2120 bug class). New services/edge-functions/src/tests/renewal-reminder_test.ts (2 tests, mirrors trial-notice_test.ts): asserts the category is transactional + resolveIsMarketing===false, and structurally that webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to sendRenewalReminderEmail (not the drip). Verified: deno check+lint clean, 2 tests pass. STILL passes:false: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time is a Dashboard billing setting — Settings->Billing->Upcoming renewal reminders — not code) and AC5's live half (an annual sub actually producing a reminder before renewal needs a Stripe run). AC1/AC3/AC4 are done (handleInvoiceUpcoming + handleTrialWillEnd wired, transactional category, now guarded).

userStories.title: iOS paywall advertises 1,000 AI actions for Pro; the server grants 750
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Billing/IAPProduct.swift:88,93 advertises Pro as '1,000 listings · 1,000 AI actions · 30 grades · AutoLister'. Both the server catalog (services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/products.ts:75,80) and web (src/lib/constants.ts:243, aiActionsPerMonth: 750) say 750. iOS buyers are sold 1,000 AI actions and will be plan-gated at 750 — a paid-for entitlement that does not exist. The drift test that should catch this (iap-catalog-drift_test.ts:69-106) compares ids, credits, plan/interval and fallbackPrice but NOT blurb or title, so the guard has a hole exactly where the misleading copy lives.
acceptanceCriteria: Correct the iOS copy to match the entitlement actually granted (or change the entitlement — but the two must agree).
Extend iap-catalog-drift_test.ts to compare user-facing blurb and title against the server catalog, so advertised entitlements cannot drift from granted ones.
Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.

Done: AC1 both Pro blurbs corrected to the granted 750; AC2 iap-catalog-drift_test.ts now parses and compares title + blurb, collecting all drift rather than asserting per-product (a per-product assert stops at the first mismatch, which would have turned AC3 into find-one-and-guess). FOLLOW-UP WORTH FILING: APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md is externally published entitlement copy maintained by hand with no drift guard; it happened to be right this time. | 2026-07-22 FOLLOW-UP GUARD (agent loop): the prior note flagged "APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md is externally published entitlement copy maintained by hand with no drift guard; it happened to be right this time" as worth filing. userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Billing] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Currently latent — no price change has been attempted. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Two divergent cancellation paths — the stale portal route bypasses the reviewed flow
userStories.description: The primary cancellation flow is good and should be preserved: self-serve, ~4 clicks / 2 screens, no email or phone required, period-end timing stated on every screen (cancel-subscription-dialog.tsx:106,178,219), a required acknowledgement checkbox, clearly-labelled escape buttons, and an 'Undo cancel' banner afterwards (billing.tsx:373-395). It has one retention interstitial with two off-ramps ('Pause instead' / 'Switch to cheaper plan'), which is defensible but is the part most worth a second look. The defect is a SECOND path: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker routes to the Stripe billing portal instead (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:393-406), with a stale comment 'until US-216's cancel flow ships' — US-216 has shipped. That path bypasses the reviewed dialog and shows different, portal-native copy.
acceptanceCriteria: Route the Free-tile selection through the reviewed cancellation dialog; remove the stale portal path and its comment.
Audit for any other route to cancellation and ensure all converge on one reviewed flow.
Have the review gate assess the retention interstitial against 'simple mechanism' expectations — in particular whether two deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible.
Confirm cancellation is available in the same medium as signup for every purchase path (web-purchased cancels on web; IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet).
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). California AB 2863 requires cancellation through the same medium used for the original transaction. Web is fine; the divergent path is the risk, not the flow itself. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC2 DONE (no counsel needed — this half is a code defect, not copy). AC1: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker now routes to the REVIEWED cancellation dialog instead of opening the Stripe billing portal. The portal path skipped everything the reviewed flow was designed for: the period-end statement on every screen, the required acknowledgement checkbox, the reason capture, and the undo banner. A divergent second route is how an audited flow stops being the one users actually hit. THE DESIGN POINT: it is a CALLBACK (onRequestCancel), not a self-rendered dialog, because CancelSubscriptionDialog ALREADY opens this picker as its 'switch to a cheaper plan' off-ramp — rendering the cancel dialog inside the picker would have made the two mutually recursive. The parent owns the flow; the picker only reports intent. When the prop is omitted (i.e. the picker was opened FROM the cancel dialog) the Free tile simply closes the picker, returning the user to the cancel flow they are already in rather than stacking a second copy of it. AC2 AUDITED: after the fix, every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation — the plan picker's own non-cancel branch (same-tier interval change) and past-due-banner's 'update payment method'. Using the portal is fine; routing a CANCELLATION through it is not, because cancellation is the flow carrying the review requirements. 4 guard tests pin that distinction explicitly, including one asserting past-due-banner may keep its portal call, so a future reader does not 'fix' it by mistake. The strongest assertion is ordering: the isCancelToFree branch must come BEFORE portal.mutate() AND must return — a guard that merely EXISTS while falling through would leave the bug intact while looking fixed. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by deleting the guard: that test goes red. STILL OPEN: AC3 (have the review gate assess whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations) is explicitly a US-2114 counsel-review item, not an engineering call — the story itself routes it there. AC4 (cancellation available in the same medium as signup) is stated in the story as already satisfied — web-purchased cancels on web, IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet — and I did not re-derive it. Verified: tsc clean, lint 0 errors, web 2293 passed.

userStories.title: Android has no purchase capability but the server will entitle it — build disclosure in before billing ships
userStories.description: There is no billing package, no BillingClient dependency, no paywall, no disclosure copy and no restore path anywhere in android/ (android/README.md:38 lists billing as planned). Meanwhile the entire server side is built and live: lib/google-play/{verify,rtdn,products,expiry-sweep}.ts, routes/google-play.ts, migrations 00321/00353/00354 — so POST /verify (google-play.ts:108) would grant a real entitlement. Separately, decideAppstorePrecedence (lib/appstore/precedence.ts:30-34) treats a user as Stripe-active only when billing_source is null or 'stripe', and appstoreSubscriptionBlocksStripe (:48-55) checks only 'appstore' — Google Play appears in NEITHER guard, so a Play subscriber could stack an App Store or Stripe subscription and be double-charged.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Google Play to the cross-platform precedence matrix on both sides BEFORE any Android billing client ships.
When the Android paywall is built, carry the full disclosure set from the start — model it on PaywallView.swift:303 rather than writing new copy.
Include a restore/entitlement-recovery path and a link to the Play subscription-management screen.
Add an Android equivalent of the iap-catalog-drift test, including blurb/title comparison.
Until the client ships, confirm /verify cannot be exercised by a client that cannot produce a valid purchase token.

userStories.title: Unhandled Stripe subscription webhooks including payment_action_required
userStories.description: The webhook switch (webhooks.ts:244-281) covers the core lifecycle well — subscription created/updated/paused/resumed/deleted, invoice.payment_succeeded/failed, checkout.session.completed, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created/closed — with solid infrastructure (idempotency claims, fail-closed metrics, transient-vs-permanent error split). Everything else hits a default log-and-drop. Unhandled and consequential: invoice.upcoming and customer.subscription.trial_will_end (covered by their own stories), invoice.payment_action_required (SCA/3DS — the user is never told a payment needs authorization and simply fails), invoice.finalized, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/_failed (already flagged in a code comment as a live risk if non-card payment methods are enabled), price.updated, payment_method.attached/detached.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.payment_action_required and notify the user that action is needed, with a link to complete authentication.
Handle the async payment-method events before enabling any non-card payment method.
Review the remaining unhandled events and either handle or explicitly document each as intentionally ignored, so the default branch means 'known-ignored' rather than 'unexamined'.
userStories.notes: [P2][Billing/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. Not a disclosure issue — filed alongside because it is the same webhook surface and a silent SCA failure looks to the user like an unexplained loss of service. Dunning otherwise is genuinely thorough (US-395 grace clock, Smart Retries, fail-closed to Free). | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 DONE; AC2 correctly deferred. AC1: invoice.payment_action_required is now handled and the user is told. That event was the WORST one to be silent about, and the reason is specific — an ordinary failed payment is driven by Stripe's Smart Retries, so it self-heals or escalates on its own, whereas an SCA/3DS challenge waits on a HUMAN who has been told nothing. Same end state to the user (service degrades), completely different remedy (complete a bank challenge, not update a card). New sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail is DELIBERATELY a separate template rather than reusing the payment-failed one: sending 'update your card' here points someone at the wrong fix and leaves the real one undone. It links Stripe's hosted_invoice_url, which is where the challenge is actually completed — an email telling someone their payment needs action with no way to take it would be worse than silence. DELIBERATELY DOES NOT flip subscription_status to past_due: Stripe fires invoice.payment_failed if the authentication is never completed, and THAT event owns the dunning clock. Starting the grace period from two events would make past_due_since depend on delivery ORDER. Mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout (same customer resolution, same US-1799 buyer skip, same event ledger, same safeSendEmail) rather than inventing a parallel one. AC3: the default branch now distinguishes KNOWN-IGNORED from UNEXAMINED. Previously one log line covered both facts, which meant a newly-enabled Stripe feature could start firing a consequential event and read exactly like the routine noise beside it. INTENTIONALLY_IGNORED_EVENTS lists 16 events with the reason each is dropped; anything NOT on it now warns AND records a webhook.unexpected_event metric. Note the two story-owned events (invoice.upcoming, customer.subscription.trial_will_end) are LISTED rather than merely absent — being ignored HERE because another surface owns them is a decision worth recording, not a gap. 5 tests, including the one that catches the likely future mistake: a handled event must never ALSO appear on the ignored list, since that combination would mean someone added a handler without removing the entry and the list would be lying about what happens. AC2 (async payment-method events) NOT done and should not be: those matter only once a non-card payment method is enabled, and pre-writing handlers for a payment method nobody has turned on is speculative work of exactly the kind that produced this codebase's dead modules. The AC itself says 'before enabling any non-card payment method' — that is the trigger, and it has not fired. Verified: edge 4283 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-22 FOLLOW-UP FIX (agent loop): a completeness guard caught that payment_action_required — the SCA/3DS notice AC1 added — was NEVER registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts), even though the note says the handler "mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout" and payment_failed IS in the set. Effect was LATENT not live (sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail passes no marketing flag, so resolveIsMarketing defaulted it transactional), but it lacked the force-classification GUARANTEE the AC6 protection gives every other required billing notice — i.e. if it were ever routed with marketing:true or the identity/unsubscribe logic keyed off membership, the one notice that owns an SCA challenge could be marketing-classified. Added payment_action_required to the set (defense-in-depth + consistency), and added a COMPLETENESS guard in email-transport_test.ts asserting all four required billing notices (trial_expiring, subscription_renewal_reminder, payment_action_required, payment_failed) are members — the prior AC6 test only checked members OF the set, so removing a required one from it passed silently. That guard is what surfaced this. Verified: deno check+lint clean, 13 email-transport tests pass. (US-2128 stays passes:false: AC2 async-payment-method events remain a documented tripwire for when a non-card method is enabled.)

userStories.title: Authenticity prompt activation must fail closed — the eval gate has never run
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-authenticity.ts (530 lines) is LIVE with three callers: the paid grading add-on (grading-pipeline.ts:1239), the buyer credit-metered check (routes/buyer-authenticity.ts:53), and an UNAUTHENTICATED public endpoint (routes/public-grading.ts:998). acceptanceCriteria: Wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path, mirroring how the grading engine gates prompt versions (shadow -> eval gate -> canary).
Activation must FAIL CLOSED: an authenticity prompt version that has not passed the gate cannot be activated, and if no golden set exists yet, activation is blocked rather than defaulted open.
Add the admin route/surface needed to run the eval and view results.
Emit a startup or health warning while any live authenticity prompt version is ungated, so this cannot silently regress again.
Test that activation is refused when the gate has not passed, and that the refusal is visible rather than silent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Safety][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. This is the single most urgent item in the epic: we are already making authenticity claims in production with no accuracy bar, including on an unauthenticated public endpoint. Same risk class as the FTC Section 5 substantiation work (US-2114..2128). Load the grading-engine skill first — it owns the prompt-version lifecycle this must mirror. Related: US-1996 tracks the backlog-integrity side of the same gap. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: shipped authenticityGateStatus + gateStatusFromRun (pure, fail-closed on BOTH no-run and query-error) + assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (the fail-closed guard a future activation path must call) + warnAuthenticityGate wired into main.ts as backgrounded non-throwing boot work (NOT a boot guard — US-778 crash-loop precedent). Model is part of the gate key, mirroring US-2036. Guard test extended: accepts either runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable, and now pins the boot check. 4348 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: (a) no authenticity prompt-ACTIVATION path exists to block — authenticity prompts are code constants, not ai_prompt_versions rows; building that lifecycle needs a migration and was deliberately NOT invented here (see the reasoning in authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, which argues against speculative lifecycles); (b) the gate will report ungated for every version until US-2131 seeds real labeled cases. Next: admin route to RUN the eval. ITER2 2026-07-19: added GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/gate (reports whether each live version has a passing run on the serving model; all_gated headline) and POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/eval (step-up gated — costs one vision call per case; surfaces the empty-golden-set case as a 400 setup state, not a 500). userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.

USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing

A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.
Reconcile the brand-KB 'never auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture.

Check eBay policy exposure: grade-badge.ts is already dead because eBay bans grade overlays on listing imagery, and eBay runs its own Authenticity Guarantee — determine what may be stated on a listing before building listing-facing surfaces.
Confirm the unauthenticated public endpoint should expose verdicts at all.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.

Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.

Authenticity slots (serial/marking/surface/corner/sole) now compress to 3600px, tag/label/detail/defect/interior/certificate to 3000, everything else keeps the unchanged 2400 default -- uploadMaxWidthFor() in src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts, applied at both upload paths (submission photo-upload.tsx and FlipDesk photo-uploader.tsx). AC5 respected literally: the increase is scoped, because the iOS cap was LOWERED to 1600px deliberately for upload speed and that tradeoff is real on mobile data. STATED PLAINLY IN THE CODE, because the number looks like a win it is not: Claude normalizes long edge to ~1568px, so more pixels do NOT change what the model sees today. What changes is what we RETAINED -- the crop-and-zoom pipeline of AC2 cannot recover detail thrown away at capture, so AC1 necessarily lands before AC2 and looks inert until it does. SIZED AGAINST THE CEILING RATHER THAN PICKED: client MAX_FILE_SIZE and edge DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES both cap at 10MB and the server dimension guard at 12,000px; a 3600px WebP at q0.85 runs 1-3MB, while the ~4700px a third-frame crop would need to reach Claude's own ceiling does not fit -- which is why 3600 and not more. The cap table lives beside the US-2136 QUALITY table on purpose and a test pins that every gated slot's cap exceeds its own floor: a slot with a 900px floor and the 2400 default cap would have been nagged for resolution the pipeline was never asked to keep. Both upload paths now resolve the slot photo_type ONCE and feed both the cap and the gate, so they cannot disagree about which slot a photo is. 32 tests total in macro-photo-quality.test.ts. Web has no tag-quality gate at all, and neither platform applies a quality gate to any other macro slot. A blurry or too-distant macro shot currently reaches the model looking exactly like a good one.
acceptanceCriteria: Port the tag-quality gate to web.
Apply a quality gate to every authenticity macro slot, with per-slot thresholds.
Reject or warn in-capture with actionable guidance ('move closer', 'hold steady') rather than failing silently after upload.
Feed the measured quality into authenticity confidence rather than treating accepted/rejected as binary.

The pattern exists and is proven on iOS — this is generalization, not invention. | 2026-07-31 AC1+AC2+AC3 DONE; AC4 recorded as deferred, not half-built. AC4 DEFERRED WITH THE GROUNDWORK IN PLACE: the assessment already carries a continuous 0..1 `score` on both pass and fail precisely so authenticity confidence can read a measure instead of a pass/fail bit, but delivering it to the grading pass means persisting it per photo -- a schema change, and the held-migration rule means a migration commit cannot be pushed without the operator applying the SQL first. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2898 tests pass, build green.

userStories.title: Deepen brand-decoders cross-checks — the strongest deterministic signal we have
userStories.description: brand-decoders.ts is a data-driven regex decoder engine whose crossCheck produces DecodeInconsistency on impossible dates (date_in_future, date_before_brand at :236-245), fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence (ai-authenticity.ts:346-353). This is deterministic contradiction detection — it does not depend on model judgment, cannot be talked out of a finding, and is already built and underused. It is the highest-confidence authenticity signal available today and the one most worth extending. CORRECTION 2026-07-19 (after reading vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md, which the grading-engine skill instructs be read BEFORE adding any decoder): this story as originally filed invites the exact failure that note forbids. Decoders must clear tag-printed AND regular AND BRAND-UNIQUE IN FORMAT, plus a fourth question added 2026-07-19 — WHICH ENTITY does the identifier name? Reebok, PUMA, Chanel/Moncler/Balenciaga serials, the Canada Goose hologram and URBN OB###### are all deliberately decoder-less; they look like coverage gaps and are not. Decoder authority OUTRANKS the AI on conflict, so a false decoder does not merely add a wrong guess — it overrides a correct one. Expanding coverage by submission volume, as originally written, would mint false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat CROSS-CHECKS and DECODERS as different risk classes. A cross-check detects a contradiction (impossible date, mismatched era) and cannot mis-attribute a brand — that is the safe expansion path and where effort should go. A decoder RECOVERS a brand from a code and can override a correct read.
Any new decoder must clear all three bar tests AND the which-entity question, with the reasoning recorded in the vault note alongside the existing table.
Do NOT seed a decoder for any code listed as a deliberate refusal — extend the refusal table instead if a new one is evaluated and rejected.

A parent-wide or shared identifier (URBN OB######, shared RN 66170) can never attribute a sibling brand. Any RN/CA cross-check must handle shared RNs explicitly rather than treating RN -> brand as one-to-one.
Codes that fail the bar get transcribed into tag_eras or authentication_tells, never wired to brand recovery.
A contradiction from a deterministic decoder must dominate model optimism — verify applyVerdictCap composition holds (caps compose as a min and never raise).
Surface which decoders fired in the operator view so a verdict is explainable.

WIRE IT FIRST, and note the plumbing already exists on the consuming side, so this is genuinely small: ai-extract.ts already computes decoderHits: DecodeResult[] (:946,:981) in production. The missing step is running crossCheckDecodeResult over those hits and passing the result as context.crossChecks. BUT IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER, and this is the part worth flagging: this ADDS DYNAMIC PER-ITEM CONTEXT TO AN AUTHENTICITY PROMPT, which the grading-engine skill requires be flag-gated and to SUFFIX prompt_version so accuracy tracking can attribute eras (the same rule that governs +baseline/+fabric/+visual). Shipping it unflagged would silently change verdicts under an unchanged version string and make every before/after accuracy comparison meaningless. AC6 (applyVerdictCap composition) also cannot be verified today, because a contradiction can never currently reach the model to dominate its optimism. userStories.title: Per-brand tell depth is 3 brands and 7 tells, all unverified
userStories.description: CANONICAL_TELLS covers exactly three brands (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) with 7 tells total across categories date_code/stamp/hardware/serial/font — every one marked 'seed:brand-authentication-tells (unverified — review in admin)' at confidence 0.5-0.65, against a taxonomy of 11 categories that includes stitching, construction and material. The separate seeded brand_knowledge.authentication_tells rows are legacy {tell, detail} shape, coerced on read to category 'other' with NO redFlag field (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92), so they contribute almost nothing to the contradiction logic that drives the verdict. admin-brand-knowledge.ts is a working curation surface with validateTellsForWrite and is the right place to do this. EXTENDED 2026-07-19: the KB is also ONE-SIDED. Every field models what a GENUINE example looks like — authentication_tells, tag_eras, country_patterns, registered_numbers — and there is no counterfeit-pattern modelling at all: no known fake markers, no superfake characteristics, no record of a specific counterfeit production tell. authentication_tells is a single column marked 'informational' doing double duty for both directions. acceptanceCriteria: Migrate legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape so they can carry a category and a redFlag and actually affect the verdict.
Expand verified tells to the brands with real submission volume; mark provenance and confidence per tell.
Establish a review workflow so a tell moves from unverified to verified deliberately, with a named source.
Gate: a brand with no verified tells should widen limitations and lower confidence rather than producing a confident verdict from generic reasoning.

Model counterfeit-side knowledge distinctly from genuine-side tells — a known fake marker is a different kind of fact from 'what a real one looks like', and collapsing them into one informational column is why neither drives the verdict.
Reconcile the seeded 'NEVER auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture (see US-2133) rather than leaving the KB and the product in contradiction.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22).

userStories.title: Reviewer tells never flow back into brand knowledge — the loop is half-built
userStories.description:
US-2140 captures tells_relied_on: exactly which tells a human expert used to reach a verdict on a real item. That is the highest-value authenticity data the system can generate, and nothing aggregates it. It flows into the golden set as a single eval case and stops there — it never reaches brand_knowledge.authentication_tells or CANONICAL_TELLS, which are what ground future assessments.

So today a reviewer can identify the same decisive tell fifty times and the model still will not know it. Closing this converts every human review into permanent, reusable brand knowledge instead of one test case.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate tells_relied_on per brand and surface candidates in the admin brand-knowledge curation surface (admin-brand-knowledge.ts already exists with validateTellsForWrite).
PROPOSE, never auto-promote: a tell entering the KB changes future verdicts, so it needs the same deliberate review a seeded tell gets. Frequency is evidence, not authority.
Carry provenance — which reviews supported the tell, and how often it was decisive vs merely noted.
Respect the vault's brand rules before writing anything: read vault/20-domain/brands/ (the decoder bar, the alias refusals, the negative findings) — several absences there are deliberate.

Migrate the legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape as part of this, or aggregated tells will land in a field that contributes nothing to the verdict (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92 coerces them to category 'other' with no redFlag).
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Knowledge][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Cheap and compounding — it wires two systems that already exist. Overlaps US-2139 (tell depth); do them together, since this is the mechanism that makes US-2139 self-sustaining rather than a one-off curation push. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/tell-candidates.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/tell-candidates. Read-only by design — it RANKS what reviewers relied on and drafts a skeleton; an operator writes the real tell through the existing brand-knowledge surface where validateTellsForWrite applies. Nothing auto-promotes: frequency is evidence, not authority, and a tell entering the KB changes every future verdict for that brand. Key design choice is DISCRIMINATION, not raw frequency: a category appearing on both authentic and counterfeit verdicts about equally is something reviewers LOOK AT, not something that separates real from fake, so it is excluded (MIN_DISCRIMINATION 0.7) — seeding it would add noise to every verdict. Inconclusive reviews are ignored entirely (evidence about neither direction, and counting them would dilute the categories that decided something). Unknown categories are DROPPED rather than coerced to other, which is precisely how the legacy {tell,detail} rows ended up contributing nothing. The generated draft says TO WRITE in every prose field and starts at confidence 0.5 — auto-generating confident-sounding claim/check text would manufacture authority the aggregate does not contain. Response splits promotable vs emerging so near-threshold candidates are visible instead of looking like no data. 4384 edge tests pass (+8). STILL OPEN: the legacy {tell,detail} migration into the structured shape (shared with US-2139), and the admin UI. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-19 (self-audit): tells_relied_on was accepted as any string array on write while the aggregator DROPS anything that is not a known AuthTellCategory — so a reviewer could record free-text tells, see a 201, and have the signal silently vanish at aggregation. validateReviewOutcome now rejects unknown categories at write time and names both the offending value and the valid set. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other. | SCOPED 2026-07-30, AC5 NOT ATTEMPTED — deliberately, because the obvious version of it is a regression. Measured the corpus: 179 legacy payload arrays holding 599 individual {tell,detail} entries across the 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql seeds; structured payloads = 0. Two findings that change what AC5 is. (1) A BULK CATEGORIZATION WOULD SILENTLY REMOVE A PAID DISCLOSURE. authenticity-coverage.ts:53 isActionableTell returns true when category !== 'other' OR redFlag is set, so assigning categories alone flips every one of those 179 packs from 'inert' to 'actionable' — which lifts coverageConfidenceCap from COVERAGE_CAP_INERT 0.75 to 1.0 and empties the limitations string the PURCHASED add-on owes its buyer (US-2219 shipped that cap precisely because these rows cannot move a verdict). Not one new verified fact would have been added. That is a user-visible regression on a paid product, dressed as a data migration. (2) MOST OF THE 599 ARE NOT AUTHENTICATION TELLS AT ALL — the column is doing double duty as general brand knowledge. Real examples from the seeds: 'American Eagle runs LARGE', 'Anthropologie also SELLS other brands', 'PINK IS NOT VICTORIA'S SECRET — comp it separately', 'AERIE IS AMERICAN EAGLE — and the tag does not say so'. All 599 are injected into the <<<KNOWN_AUTHENTICATION_TELLS>>> block (ai-authenticity.ts:409-422) under the instruction 'check the item against EACH and report a finding per tell', capped at MAX_TELLS 60 per brand — so sizing and comping rules both generate noise findings and can crowd out real tells. The reshape is therefore a SEPARATION problem first (identification vs authentication knowledge) and a categorization problem second; doing the second without the first is what makes it harmful. AC5 is the SAME work as US-2139 AC1, and authenticity-coverage.ts:20 already names US-2139 as its owner ('Re-shaping the legacy rows is US-2139's job'). Recommend deleting AC5 from this story as a duplicate and carrying it only on US-2139, where the counterfeit-side modelling (US-2139 AC5) that a real redFlag needs also lives. Already guarded, so nobody can do this silently: authenticity-coverage_test.ts:201 asserts structured payloads == 0 and tells the next author to update the floor rather than delete the test. AC1-AC4 remain shipped per the earlier PARTIAL/BUGFIX/UI segments. Nothing changed in code this pass.

userStories.description: As an iOS seller who has used my monthly free Snap-to-Value allowance, I am told what actually happened and how to lift it, instead of being told to try again in a moment.
acceptanceCriteria: EdgeAPIError.from(statusCode:body:) maps any body carrying action:"upgrade" to a new upgrade-required case, keyed on the discriminator rather than the status — mirrors the Android US-1335 fix in EdgeApiError.kt

userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Networking] Found while porting Snap-to-Value for US-1335. Three edge sites emit action:"upgrade" (grade.ts:1020, grade.ts:1038, flipdesk-ai.ts:118) and iOS maps all three by status alone: the 429s become .rateLimited ("You are going a little too fast" — to someone who must wait until next month) and the 403 becomes .unauthorized ("Your session expired. Sign in again" — for a setting that is switched off). The server already writes the correct sentence in every case; only the client discards it. Android now keys on action:"upgrade"; this ports the same mapping so the two clients do not word the same state differently. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h), awaiting iOS CI (macOS) to validate — Swift cannot be compiled in this Linux sandbox. AC1: added EdgeAPIError.upgradeRequired(detail:code:) + WirePayload.action; from() maps any body with action:'upgrade' to it, mirroring Android EdgeApiError.kt (US-1335). AC2: the action check sits AFTER workspace_access_revoked / email_unverified / feature_unavailable/reconnect_required / offer_not_open and BEFORE the status switch (test_from_specificDiscriminator_winsOverUpgradeAction proves a revoked-workspace body that also carries action:upgrade still maps to .workspaceAccessRevoked). AC3: errorDescription returns the server sentence verbatim; the Snap call site (SnapStore.isUpgradePrompt + SnapView.errorCard) now shows an 'Upgrade' button opening PaywallView instead of 'Try again'. Enrichment site: the central mapping fix already surfaces the server's actionable 'AI enrichment is turned off… Enable it in Settings' verbatim (was the misleading 'session expired') and no longer retries — the route is named in the message (enrichment recovery is a Settings toggle, not the paywall); a dedicated button there would need threading isUpgradePrompt through AIExtractStore's .failed phase + AIExtractView (multi-file, uncompilable here) for marginal gain, so it is intentionally scoped out. AC4 (the real bug): the retry loop in EdgeAPI.swift intercepted a 429 by STATUS and threw .rateLimited BEFORE from() ran, so a cap-reached snap was retried twice (burning the per-IP daily ceiling). Restructured so from() runs first and only a genuine .rateLimited gets the Retry-After enrichment; .upgradeRequired is neither transient nor in shouldRetry, so it is not retried (test_snapCap429_action_upgrade_isNotRetried asserts calls.count==1). AC5: EdgeAPITests.swift covers all three live bodies — grade.ts 429 SNAP_LIMIT_REACHED + SNAP_IP_LIMIT_REACHED, flipdesk-ai.ts 403 enrichment-off (no code) — plus description-verbatim, isUpgradePrompt, discriminator-precedence, and the not-retried integration case. Verified in-sandbox: no exhaustive switch over EdgeAPIError lacks a default (checked EbayPublishService/FriendlyErrorCopy/EdgeAPI), so the new case breaks no call site; ios/Scripts/no-ungated-print.py clean. KEPT passes:false until iOS CI (macOS) is green on the branch. | VERIFIED 2026-07-31. iOS CI (macOS) is green on main — the last blocker in the prior note. The code is on origin/main: ios/GradeThread/Networking/EdgeAPIError.swift carries case upgradeRequired(detail:code:) with from() mapping any action:'upgrade' body after the specific discriminators, errorDescription returning the server sentence verbatim, and isUpgradePrompt; EdgeAPI.swift no longer short-circuits 429 by status before from() runs, so a cap-reached snap is not retried. ios/GradeThreadTests/EdgeAPITests.swift covers all five cases (test_from_snapMonthlyCap_mapsToUpgradeRequired_notRateLimited, test_from_snapIpCap_mapsToUpgradeRequired, test_from_enrichmentOff_mapsToUpgradeRequired_notUnauthorized, test_from_specificDiscriminator_winsOverUpgradeAction, test_snapCap429_action_upgrade_isNotRetried).
