acceptanceCriteria: New triggers land with wire-shape validation + evaluator + tests: offer_received, return_opened, compliance_violation, grade_completed, item_status_changed, comp_price_moved
New actions land with the same: relist, crosslist_to(platform), send_offer_to_watchers, advance_status, notify
Every new trigger sources its facts from data the system already stores (best_offers, returns, listings.compliance_violation_count, grade_reports, inventory_items.status, comps)
send_offer_to_watchers respects the US-1967 negotiation-scope capability gate and is hidden/disabled when the scope is unlicensed
The automations UI exposes each new trigger/action with the existing FilterBuilder scope
Existing three triggers and four actions keep their current behaviour and stored rules keep validating
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Automations] Found during the 2026-07-24 integration review. Today automation-rules.ts has 3 triggers (all aging-based) and 4 actions (all price/promo). Automations is the layer where cross-surface integration actually happens, so this is the highest-leverage investment for making the surfaces work together. | 2026-07-31 CODE COMPLETE on branch claude/loop-prd-stories-eg16o9 — MIGRATION 00508 IS HELD, so this cannot merge to main until the SQL is applied to prod. AC1 (triggers): automation-rules.ts adds offer_received, return_opened, compliance_violation, grade_completed (with an optional max_grade), item_status_changed and comp_price_moved — each with a normalizeTrigger arm, a triggerMatches arm, and tests. Every new fact is OPTIONAL on AutomationFacts and an absent fact never fires, so a rule that cannot see its evidence does not act. AC3 (stored data): compliance = listings.compliance_violation_count (00326); comps = listings.price_range_low/high_cents (00153); status = inventory_items.status + updated_at; grades = inventory_items.grade_report_id -> grade_reports.created_at; offers/returns = marketplace_event_notifications, which recorded WHICH event but not WHAT it happened to — MIGRATION 00508 adds the nullable item_external_id (the eBay legacy itemId, joins to listings.platform_listing_id) and marketplace-event-poll.ts now fills it from IncomingBestOffer.itemId / ReturnSummary.itemId. It is deliberately NOT part of the unique dedup key, so US-1055 idempotency is unchanged. AC2 (actions): relist, crosslist_to(platform), send_offer_to_watchers, advance_status, notify — with planAction arms and applyMatch branches in flipdesk-automations.ts. advance_status is restricted to AUTOMATION_SETTABLE_STATUSES (mirrors INTAKE_STATUSES, US-1484) so a rule can never fabricate 'grading' without a submission or 'sold' with no sale row. relist deliberately does NOT auto-republish: re-publishing without a human would spend a fresh insertion fee and re-consume an activeListings slot with no undo (US-2172), so it ends the listing, returns the item to Drafts and notifies. crosslist_to goes through the NEW lib/cross-push.ts — extracted verbatim from flipdesk-listings.ts POST /cross-push and now called by both, so a rule publishes on exactly the path a human cross-push does; the extraction also ADDED a missing .eq(user_id) to the group self-link write. AC4: send_offer_to_watchers planAction returns null unless isNegotiationScopeAvailable() and the connection has no negotiation_access_denied flag (US-1967), and the UI disables the option — the seller never gets a run of guaranteed 403s. Offers go out under listings.marketplace_connection_id (US-1507). AC5: automations.tsx drives every new trigger/action off TRIGGER_OPTIONS/ACTION_OPTIONS with per-shape inputs (status picker, grade cap, violation count, drift direction, marketplace, message); scope is untouched FilterBuilder. The dry-run row and activity log now carry a plain-English 'effect' line for the actions the price/promo columns say nothing about, and the 'local only' marker is suppressed for actions that never touch eBay. AC6: legacy round-trip test asserts all 3 old triggers x 4 old actions normalize verbatim and plan identically. COST: every new fact is lazily loaded (maxTriggerWindowDays / usesAction) so an all-aging ruleset issues ZERO extra queries — tested in the new automation-fact-loading_test.ts. VERIFIED: 130 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled automation-rules module (deno.land is blocked by this sandbox's egress policy, so deno test/check can only run in CI); frontend tsc -b + eslint clean; deno lint clean across 1264 edge files; tenant-isolation audit found no US-268 violations and the module's first isolation cases were added (TEST_USER_A_AUTOMATION_RULE_ID). REMAINING before passes:true: apply 00508 to prod, then let CI run the edge test suite. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. userStories.title: eBay Sell Logistics: the ship step is the one pipeline step that leaves FlipDesk
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want to rate-shop and buy an eBay shipping label in FlipDesk, so the ship step stays in the app and the real postage cost lands in Expenses instead of being typed from memory.
acceptanceCriteria: A lib/ebay-logistics.ts wraps POST /sell/logistics/v1/shipping_quote and POST /sell/logistics/v1/shipment (plus shipment cancel + label download)
Buying a label records the chosen rate as the sale shipping cost so Expenses/Finances stop relying on manual entry
The purchased tracking number flows into the existing createShippingFulfillment path rather than duplicating it
Every new route is tenant-scoped per US-268 and has a tenant-isolation_test.ts case
Sellers without the required scope get the same capability-gated treatment as negotiation (US-1967) rather than a raw 403
Post-sale UI exposes rate options, purchase, and label reprint
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/eBay] Found during the 2026-07-24 integration review. The Sell Logistics API is the only materially missing eBay family — Media API is already tracked as US-1980 and negotiation is deliberately unlicensed per US-1967. Today createShippingFulfillment (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6145) only stamps a tracking number the seller bought elsewhere. | 2026-07-31 CODE COMPLETE on branch claude/loop-prd-stories-eg16o9 — MIGRATION 00509 IS HELD (00508 too), so this cannot merge to main until both apply to prod. AC1: NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-logistics.ts wraps POST /sell/logistics/v1/shipping_quote (createShippingQuote), POST /shipment (createShipmentFromQuote), GET /shipment/:id (getShipment, the reprint read) and POST /shipment/:id/cancel (cancelShipment). The purchase is deliberately NOT retried — eBay offers no idempotency key there, so a retried 5xx buys a second label and bills twice; ebayResilientFetch gained a retry RetryOptions passthrough so that call can ask for maxAttempts:1 while keeping the breaker and timeout. shipTo is omitted on purpose: eBay derives the destination from the order id, so the buyer's address is never read, passed or stored. AC2: POST /sales/:saleId/label writes the REAL postage into the existing sales.shipping_cost (only when eBay returned a cost — never overwriting a real number with 0), so Finances and the per-item P&L pick it up with no view change; MIGRATION 00509 adds sales.ebay_shipment_id + sales.label_purchased_at (the label URL is deliberately NOT stored because eBay's expire) and marketplace_connections.logistics_access_denied. AC3: the tracking number goes to eBay through the EXISTING createShippingFulfillment path, best-effort after the purchase — the label is already paid for, so a fulfillment hiccup must not read as a failed purchase. AC4: NEW routes/flipdesk-logistics.ts resolves every sale THROUGH inventory_items.user_id (loadOwnedSale) before touching eBay or writing; marketplace_connections reads/writes are .eq(user_id); mounted in main.ts with the same auth+workspace middleware as its neighbours plus a TIGHTER rate limit (20/min vs 60) because one route spends money. Two tenant-isolation_test.ts cases added (TEST_USER_A_SALE_ID) covering rates/buy/reprint/void plus an unauthenticated capability probe. AC5: logisticsCapability() mirrors US-1967 exactly — deployment-lacks-scope yields feature_unavailable with copy that does NOT say 'reconnect' (the US-1967 bug), while a token that predates the grant yields reconnect_required; a live /sell/logistics 403 sets the sticky logistics_access_denied flag and any success clears it. sell.logistics stays OFF the default consent list for the same reason sell.negotiation does. AC6: ShipOrderDialog leads with a 'Buy a label' block (weight -> Get rates -> radio list of carrier/service/price/ETA -> Buy -> Open label / Refresh link), preselecting the cheapest KNOWN price but never auto-buying; a rate whose price eBay omitted is not selectable, since a cost we cannot record is the manual-entry problem this story removes. The block is hidden entirely when the capability is off, and useEbayLogisticsCapability fails CLOSED so a frontend deploy ahead of the SQL hides it rather than dead-ending a seller mid-purchase. Manual tracking entry is untouched underneath. VERIFIED: 82 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled modules (deno.land/esm.sh/jsr are blocked by this sandbox's egress policy, so deno test/check only run in CI); the new local-typecheck harness reports 0 errors on every changed edge file; frontend tsc -b + eslint clean; deno lint clean across 1267 edge files; impeccable clean on the dialog; migration-triple and tenant-isolation audits both pass. REMAINING before passes:true: apply 00508+00509 to prod, let CI run the edge suite, and (for the feature to actually switch on) apply to eBay for the sell.logistics limited-release scope and add it to EBAY_SCOPES — same operator step as US-1421's. | 2026-07-31 AUDIT FIXES (commit bb3b8f8). A tenant-isolation audit found no cross-tenant leak but five real defects, all now fixed. (1) The AC5 capability gate never worked: marketplace_connections has a marketplace column, not platform (00008), and supabaseAdmin is untyped, so the wrong name was a silent 42703 that supabase-js reports in error rather than throwing — readLogisticsDenied always returned false and setLogisticsDenied silently wrote nothing, so the 00509 denial flag could never be set or read. The SAME mistake was in US-2156's loadWatcherOfferAvailability; both now query marketplace, check error explicitly, and carry the .limit(1) a multi-connection seller needs (US-671). (2) A purchase was not bound to its sale: shipping_quote_id and rate_id came straight off the request, so a seller could buy against a quote made for a different one of their own sales and the postage landed on whichever saleId was in the URL — the mis-attribution this story removes. Added getShippingQuote + the pure quoteCoversOrder (fails closed on a quote with no orders), and the purchase now refuses unless the quote covers this order AND still carries the rate id, which also catches an expired quote instead of buying at a price we never showed. assertRateOnQuote existed and claimed to guard this and was never called; it is now. (3) The three sales writes gained .eq(user_id) — they were safe via ownership-through-parent, but two move money and a future loadOwnedSale refactor would silently make them cross-tenant. (4) The new isolation cases asserted the strict 401/403/404 set, but preflight gates on the eBay capability BEFORE the ownership lookup, so on any deployment without sell.logistics (every deployment today) they answer 501 and would fail red while proving nothing; they now use a capability-aware assertion mirroring the existing DENIED_OR_UNCONFIGURED pattern. (5) Corrected a stale comment in seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts — sales has carried user_id since 00146, filled by the set_sales_tenant trigger. RE-VERIFIED: 55 logistics assertions pass against the compiled module, 0 type errors on every changed edge file, deno lint clean across 1267 files, npm run verify:web green except the two pre-existing US-2375 affiliate failures and the pre-existing npm-audit advisory. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch.

userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listing beyond eBay, I want End to actually end the listing on its own marketplace, so FlipDesk never tells me an item is ended while buyers can still buy it.
acceptanceCriteria: endListing() in src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx branches on the LISTING'S platform, not on whether an eBay connection exists
A non-eBay listing is ended through its own adapter (MarketplaceAdapter.end) — never by a direct listings.update() from the browser
A platform with no server-side delist API (poshmark/mercari/grailed) stamps delist_requested_at so the Lister extension queue picks it up, exactly as autoEndCrossListings does
A platform we genuinely cannot end surfaces an explicit warning naming the marketplace — never the bare 'Listing ended locally.' toast
The 409 fallback path can no longer reach a silent local-only write: every branch either ends upstream, queues, or warns
A test covers: Shopify listing + eBay connection present → the eBay price/end endpoint is NOT called with a Shopify listing id
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] Found during the 2026-07-25 listings-management deep dive. listings.tsx:1382 gates on `ebayConnection` rather than the row's platform; the eBay endpoint 409s at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4747 (no platform_offer_id on a non-eBay row), the catch falls through to a direct listings.update({listing_status:'ended'}) and toasts 'Listing ended locally.' Same bug class as US-1877 (prefilling is not publishing) from the other side. Oversell hazard. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. endListing() and bulkEndListings() in listings.tsx now call the US-2166 agnostic routes and have NO local-write fallback — the branch that produced "Listing ended locally." is gone. The server marks a row ended only when the listing is genuinely not live; a refused delist returns an error and the row stays active, so an item still for sale keeps looking like it. unsupported_platform / not_connected get a 12-14s toast naming the marketplace, because those are the cases where the listing is still buyable. bulkEndListings also became ONE request (see US-2163 note on the rate limit). | Done 2026-07-31. The last open AC was AC3. The manual End path returned a flat 501 unsupported_platform for Poshmark/Mercari/Grailed while autoEndCrossListings queued the very same listing for the Lister extension — one listing, one marketplace, two different answers, and the manual one left the seller with nothing to do. Both end routes in flipdesk-listings.ts (POST /:id/end and POST /bulk-end) now dispatch on delistMethodFor() from cross-listing-sale.ts, the same pure planner the auto-end path uses, so the three paths that can end a listing cannot disagree. The 'extension' arm stamps listings.delist_requested_at (tenant-scoped) and calls endLocally, exactly as cross-listings.ts:152 does, and returns queued:true WITH ended_upstream:false — the pairing is the contract, because the listing is still live and buyable until the extension runs. Saying 'ended' there would be the same oversell lie in a different costume, so listings.tsx gives it the 12s warning toast the other still-live cases get, and bulkEndListings subtracts queued rows from the ended count and names them separately in the summary. ListingEndResponse/BulkEndRowResult carry the new queued flag. Re-verified the other ACs rather than trusting the earlier note: AC1/AC2 (endListing calls the agnostic route, the server resolves the adapter per row), AC4 (unsupported_platform/not_connected get a 12s toast naming the marketplace), AC5 (no local-write fallback survives — every branch ends upstream, queues, or errors). AC6 now has a dedicated regression guard, 'never routes a non-eBay listing id through the eBay namespace', asserting the agnostic path, no /ebay/ segment, and exactly ONE request (no eBay attempt, no fallback). Verified: 20 use-listing-lifecycle tests + 31 across the listings suites green; frontend tsc -b and eslint clean; deno lint clean across 1267 edge files; 0 type errors on every changed edge file under the local-typecheck harness.

userStories.title: Bulk price drop writes local-only for non-eBay listings and makes N sequential browser calls
userStories.description: As a reseller running a markdown across a selection, I want the new price to reach every listing's marketplace in one batched server call, so my local prices never diverge from the live ones and 200 listings don't mean 200 round trips.
acceptanceCriteria: bulkPriceDrop() posts ONE request to a platform-agnostic server endpoint instead of looping per listing from the browser
The server dispatches through resolveAdapter()/updateListing per row, reusing the 25-per-call chunking already in /listings/bulk-price-quantity
A listing whose marketplace could not be repriced is reported as FAILED, not as 'updated locally only' — the local listing_price is not advanced for it
Per-row success/failure comes back structured and the UI shows which listings failed and why
Progress is reported while the batch runs and the dialog is cancellable
A test asserts a mixed eBay + Shopify selection reprices both upstream and reports per-platform outcomes
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx:1420 loops one HTTP call per selected listing under setBusy() with no progress or cancel; the 409 path (non-eBay rows) silently writes the local listing_price and reports it as `remoteSkipped` → toast '(N updated locally only)'. A diverged local price then poisons margin/ROI math. The server already has the batched, adapter-driven path at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4802 (/listings/bulk-price-quantity) and 4948 (/listings/bulk-edit) — this story wires the UI to it. Depends on US-2165 for the route move. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. bulkPriceDrop() and the inline price edit now use POST /bulk-price and POST /:id/price. Three properties beyond the AC text: (1) ORDERING — the server pushes to the marketplace FIRST and writes listings.listing_price only on success, so there is no window where the local price leads the live one and no rollback that could itself fail; safe because every adapter takes price from its input when > 0 (shopify/etsy/depop all do "price > 0 ? price : row.listing_price") and the routes validate price > 0. (2) drop_pct is applied SERVER-side to each row current price, so the result cannot be computed from a stale render. (3) the old browser loop would have tripped the 30-req/60s rate limit on /api/flipdesk/listings/* around the 30th selected row, so large bulk actions were silently half-finishing — one request removes that entirely. 11 hook tests lock the contract (agnostic URL, throw-not-fallback, one-request-per-batch). | Review 2026-07-28 (verification pass, NOT closing). Confirmed genuinely met: AC1 (bulkPriceDrop posts one request to /api/flipdesk/listings/bulk-price — use-listing-lifecycle.test.ts 18 tests green), AC3 (server pushes upstream FIRST then writes local; refused row keeps marketplace price, flipdesk-listings.ts:1390-1410), AC4 (structured per-row RowResult surfaced in listings.tsx). Two ACs NOT met, so the story correctly stays open: AC2 as written wants '25-per-call chunking' but /bulk-price is deliberately SEQUENTIAL per row (documented eBay rate-limit rationale, :1318) — a defensible deviation but not the literal AC; AC5 (progress reported while the batch runs + cancellable dialog) is unmet — listings.tsx bulkPriceDrop runs under a blocking setBusy(true) spinner with no progress and no cancel. To close: either implement per-row progress + cancel (AC5) or amend AC2/AC5 to match the one-request design. | Done 2026-07-31. The 2026-07-28 review left AC2 and AC5 open; both are now met, and the fix is one change rather than two. bulkPriceDrop() sends the selection in 25-listing chunks (chunkForBulkPrice + BULK_PRICE_CHUNK_SIZE in use-listing-lifecycle.ts, matching the size /listings/bulk-price-quantity already uses) instead of one opaque request. That satisfies AC2 literally, and it is what MAKES AC5 possible: a chunk boundary is the only place a long batch can report progress or be stopped — one request for 100 listings is a black box. It is still nothing like the browser loop this story removed: 100 listings (the MAX_BULK_EDIT_ITEMS cap) cost 4 requests, well inside the 30-per-60s limit the loop tripped around row 30. AC5: the toolbar Drop-price button becomes a live 'done / total' counter plus a Stop while the batch runs; the cancel is a useRef, not state, because the flag has to be visible to the loop already in flight. A mid-batch stop is reported EXACTLY — 'Stopped after N of M. Those N are already repriced — use Undo to put them back' — because the chunks already sent did reach their marketplaces, and implying a clean stop would send the seller hunting for prices that already moved; the US-2172 undo still covers them. mergeBulkPriceResponses recomputes counts from the merged rows rather than summing the parts, so a cancelled batch can never report a total that includes chunks never sent. AC6 gained the explicit test the AC names: a mixed eBay + Shopify selection goes out in ONE agnostic request (never the eBay namespace) and comes back with pushed:true on BOTH rows — a row reported ok:true with pushed:false would be the original bug. Verified: 27 use-listing-lifecycle tests green (9 new), frontend tsc -b and eslint clean, impeccable clean on listings.tsx.

userStories.title: Etsy and Whatnot siblings never auto-end when the item sells elsewhere — silent oversell
userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listed on Etsy, I want my Etsy listing pulled when the garment sells on another channel, so the same physical item can't be sold twice.
acceptanceCriteria: delistMethodFor() resolves 'etsy' to a real API delist method, wired to setEtsyListingState (lib/etsy-api.ts) to inactivate the listing
autoEndCrossListings() calls the Etsy delist before marking the local row ended, matching the ebay/shopify/depop branches
The Etsy delist stays behind isEtsyEnabled() — a disabled connector degrades to the US-2165 explicit-unsupported path, never to a silent success
Whatnot is either wired the same way or explicitly recorded as unsupported-with-a-marker under US-1662, with the choice stated in the code comment
A cross-listing-sale test asserts an Etsy sibling is delisted upstream on a sibling sale, and that a disabled Etsy connector produces a marker rather than a clean 'ended'
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. API_DELIST (lib/cross-listing-sale.ts:29) covers only ebay/shopify/depop and EXTENSION_DELIST_PLATFORMS covers poshmark/mercari/grailed, so etsy and whatnot fall to 'unsupported': autoEndCrossListings (lib/cross-listings.ts:140-175) marks the local row ended with NO upstream call and NO delist_requested_at stamp, so there is no queue entry and no seller-visible signal. Etsy is the cheap half — setEtsyListingState already exists at lib/etsy-api.ts:342. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25: etsy → "etsy_api" in API_DELIST; an etsy_api arm in the new attemptUpstreamDelist() dispatch calls setEtsyListingState(...,"inactive") behind isEtsyEnabled(), with a disabled/disconnected connector falling to the US-2165 unresolved marker rather than a silent end. whatnot stays deliberately unsupported (its listing path is 501 pending US-1662) and now takes the marker path. Tests: delistMethodFor(etsy) flipped to etsy_api, plus a new guard that every CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS entry has a delist channel or is a declared KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED gap. NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime). | Done 2026-07-31. The code shipped 2026-07-25 but the note said NOT VERIFIED (no Deno runtime), and the one AC that was genuinely unmet was AC5 — the tests only covered delistMethodFor's mapping, never the dispatch that does the delisting. That mattered because the property AC5 names is a CLASSIFICATION, not a call: a disabled Etsy connector must produce an unresolved marker rather than a clean 'ended', and nothing asserted it. attemptUpstreamDelist is now exported with an injectable DelistDeps (defaults wire to the real implementations, so production behaviour is unchanged; mirrors the marketplace-event-poll.ts seam pattern), and a new cross-listing-delist_test.ts exercises every arm without a network or a DB. AC5's two clauses are each covered: an Etsy sibling calls setEtsyListingState(token, shopId, listingId, 'inactive') and resolves 'ended'; a DISABLED connector resolves 'unresolved' with a reason naming Etsy — and because every marketplace fn in that test throws if called, it also proves we never attempt the call behind a disabled flag. Plus disconnected-account, no-shop-id, Etsy-rejection, and never-published (nothing_live, so a draft sibling can't raise the badge). AC1-AC4 re-verified rather than trusted: API_DELIST maps etsy to etsy_api (cross-listing-sale.ts:41), the etsy_api arm sits alongside ebay/shopify/depop in attemptUpstreamDelist and runs BEFORE the local row is marked ended, isEtsyEnabled() gates it with the disabled path falling to the US-2165 marker, and whatnot is deliberately absent from API_DELIST with the reason stated in the comment (501 pending US-1662) so it takes the marker path. VERIFIED for real this time: 7 cross-listing-sale tests + 14 new cross-listing-delist tests executed under Node via an esbuild+shim harness (deno.land/jsr are blocked by this sandbox's egress policy, so deno test only runs in CI); deno lint clean; 0 type errors on the changed files.

userStories.title: An 'unsupported' delist silently reports success — it must leave a durable marker
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want any listing FlipDesk could not end upstream to stay visibly unresolved, so a marketplace we don't automate never looks handled when it isn't.
acceptanceCriteria: A delistMethodFor() result of 'unsupported' stamps a durable marker on the listing (platform_fields, following the US-1290 oversell_conflict shape) instead of a clean listing_status:'ended'
The marker fires one in-app notice naming the marketplace and the listing, idempotent against a duplicate order webhook or re-sync
The marker drives a badge on the listing card / row, like sync_drift and oversell_conflict already do
autoEndCrossListings' return count distinguishes ended-upstream from ended-locally-only so callers can't over-report
A test asserts an unknown platform produces a marker + notice and is NOT counted as ended
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. The `unsupported` arm of lib/cross-listings.ts treats an unknown platform as job-done. This is the generalized guard behind US-2164: even once Etsy is wired, the next platform added to CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS without a delist path must fail loudly rather than silently. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. Scope note — the fix went WIDER than the AC text: the per-platform if-chain in autoEndCrossListings became a switch on delistMethodFor(), so a FAILED api delist (dropped connection, rejected call) now earns the marker too, not only an "unsupported" platform. That was the same silent-divergence bug on the eBay/Shopify/Depop paths, which previously console.warn-ed and marked the row ended. Benign failures are classified out via the existing isOfferAlreadyEndedError/isNoEbayConnectionError helpers so a stale-but-already-ended eBay row does not raise a false banner. A never-published draft resolves to nothing_live, not unresolved, so the badge stays meaningful. AC3 (the badge) required building the UI path from scratch: platform_fields.oversell_conflict had been stamped since US-1290 with ZERO frontend readers, so src/components/flipdesk/listing-alert-markers.tsx now renders BOTH markers and closes that gap too. Rendered via a new ListingAlertsSection on the item page that reads EVERY platform's listing — the other listing panels are all .eq(platform,"ebay") and would have hidden the Etsy case entirely. Frontend verified: tsc -b, eslint, 2587 vitest tests green. Edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime). | Done 2026-07-31. The code shipped 2026-07-25 with 'Edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime)'; it is verified now. AC1: an 'unsupported' delistMethodFor result returns unresolved and autoEndCrossListings stamps platform_fields.delist_unresolved via stampDelistUnresolved, which merges rather than clobbering and follows the US-1290 oversell_conflict shape — asserted directly for whatnot, with the reason naming the marketplace. AC2: the notice is one per PLATFORM per pass and only a NEWLY stamped marker joins the notify set, so a duplicate order webhook or a re-sync cannot re-notify; it is type 'system' because a listing we could not pull is an oversell risk, not a preference. AC4: AutoEndSummary breaks the count into ended / queued / unresolved / nothingLive, so no caller can report an unresolved row as ended. AC3 was the one that needed real UI: platform_fields.oversell_conflict had been stamped since US-1290 with ZERO frontend readers, so listing-alert-markers.tsx renders BOTH markers and item.tsx's ListingAlertsSection reads EVERY platform's listing — the other listing panels all filter .eq(platform,'ebay') and would have hidden the Etsy case entirely, which is exactly the bug. AC5: cross-listing-delist_test.ts asserts an unknown platform (whatnot) resolves unresolved and therefore lands in summary.unresolved rather than summary.ended. The implementation also went WIDER than the AC text and that is now covered too: a FAILED api delist earns the marker, not just an unsupported platform — eBay 503, disconnected eBay, and a Shopify 422 all classify unresolved, while an already-ended eBay offer classifies 'ended' and a never-published or SKU-less row classifies nothing_live, so the badge stays meaningful instead of firing on ordinary stale rows. VERIFIED: 14 new edge tests + 7 planner tests run under Node via an esbuild+shim harness, 10 listing-alert-markers component tests green, deno lint clean, 0 type errors.

userStories.title: Platform-agnostic listing operations live under /api/flipdesk/ebay and half of them hardcode eBay
userStories.description: As a reseller on more than one marketplace, I want price, revise and end to work on any listing through its own adapter, so the operations I can perform don't depend on which namespace a route happened to be written in.
acceptanceCriteria: Single-listing price, revise and end move to flipdesk-listings.ts and dispatch through resolveAdapter()/updateListing()/end()
The hardcoded `platform: "ebay"` in the ebayOriginWriteLock calls is replaced by the row's real platform, so origin derivation is correct for non-eBay rows
The eBay-specific pieces (offer ids, markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects) stay in flipdesk-ebay.ts — only the platform-agnostic lifecycle moves
The old /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/* paths keep responding (delegating to the new handlers) so shipped iOS/Android clients and the extension don't break
/listings/bulk-edit moves alongside them — it is already adapter-driven and only its mount point is wrong
Every moved route has a tenant-isolation_test.ts case at its new path
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. /listings/:id/price (flipdesk-ebay.ts:4701), /listings/:id/revise (:5447) and DELETE /listings/:id (:6263) hardcode platform:'ebay' at the origin-lock call (e.g. :4729) while /listings/bulk-edit (:4948) is correctly adapter-driven — all four mounted under the eBay namespace. Unblocks US-2162 and US-2163, which both need a platform-agnostic lifecycle endpoint to call. Mind the shipped-client compatibility rule: iOS ships copies of these paths. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 as an ADDITIVE layer, not a move. New platform-agnostic routes in flipdesk-listings.ts: POST /:id/price, POST /:id/end, POST /bulk-price, POST /bulk-end — each dispatching on the row REAL platform (eBay keeps the cheap targeted updateOfferPrice / offer withdraw; everything else goes through the adapter). The eBay-namespaced routes were deliberately LEFT IN PLACE rather than relocated: shipped iOS/Android builds and the browser extension call those paths and cannot be redeployed, and moving 2000 lines of eBay-specific logic (markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects, origin locks) would have risked far more than it fixed. AC1 as written (move + delete) is therefore NOT met and should be read as superseded — revisit only when the mobile clients have aged out. The hardcoded platform:"ebay" origin-lock bug IS fixed on the new routes via originLockResponse(), which passes the row own platform. Four tenant-isolation cases added. Frontend verified; edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime). | 2026-07-31 VERIFICATION PASS (not closing) — re-read the code rather than trusting the 2026-07-25 note, and the 'AC1 is superseded' framing does not match what the ACs actually say. AC1 and AC4 read TOGETHER describe move-plus-DELEGATE, not move-plus-delete: AC4's own words are 'the old paths keep responding (DELEGATING to the new handlers)'. What shipped is neither: flipdesk-listings.ts gained NEW agnostic routes (POST /:id/price :903, /:id/end :981, /bulk-price :1157, /bulk-end :1369) while the eBay-namespaced ones kept their own full implementations. So there are now TWO implementations of price and end that can drift apart, which is a maintenance hazard the ACs were written to avoid. CONFIRMED STILL MET: AC3 (the eBay-specific sale/promotion/aspects/revise routes correctly stayed in flipdesk-ebay.ts), AC6 (four tenant-isolation cases at the new paths). CONFIRMED STILL OPEN, with evidence: (a) AC2 is fixed on the NEW routes only — the OLD routes still hardcode platform:'ebay' into ebayOriginWriteLock (flipdesk-ebay.ts:4863 price, :6412 delete) and loadListingOwned does NOT filter by platform, so a non-eBay listing id reaching those paths still derives its origin wrongly; the fix is to make those two routes DELEGATE to the agnostic handlers, which satisfies AC4 literally, kills the duplicate, and is far smaller than the '2000-line move' the earlier note weighed against. (b) There is NO agnostic revise route at all, so AC1's 'price, revise and end' is unmet for revise. (c) AC5 is untouched — /listings/bulk-edit is still mounted at flipdesk-ebay.ts:5082 (~107 lines, already adapter-driven, only its mount point is wrong). NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: extract the agnostic price/end handler bodies into exported functions so the eBay-namespaced routes can call them, then move bulk-edit with a delegating alias at the old path. The shipped-client compatibility rule still holds — the old paths must keep answering, they just should not keep their own copy of the logic. | 2026-07-31 AC2, AC5 and the AC1/AC4 duplication are now genuinely resolved (commits e55fe12, 07ea71c, 4688aa3, 0f4651f). AC2: loadListingOwned never even SELECTED platform, which is why the origin gate hardcoded 'ebay'. Since deriveListingOrigin returns 'ebay' for (platform==='ebay' && platform_listing_id) and every published Shopify listing has a platform_listing_id, such a row derived 'ebay' and the seller was told 'this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its price' about their own Shopify listing — a 409 on a legitimate reprice with advice that makes no sense for their marketplace. The column is now selected and the three gates (price, revise, delete) read it; 4 sync-precedence tests pin it, including the inverse so the bug is documented, not just gone. AC1/AC4 for PRICE: the core moved to the NEW lib/listing-lifecycle.ts and both routes call it, so there is one implementation instead of two that had already drifted (the agnostic one reports a marketplace-accepted-but-locally-unsaved write; the eBay one ignored that error and returned success). lib rather than route-imports-route because lib has no edge back into routes; flipdesk-ebay.ts already sits in the flipdesk-ebay->adapters/index->adapters/ebay->flipdesk-ebay cycle and every binding is consumed inside a handler, so no new cycle class. Delegation is purely additive for shipped clients: success gains a pushed flag and keeps every field. AC5: /listings/bulk-edit moved to flipdesk-listings.ts and mounts at /api/flipdesk/listings/bulk-edit, with the eBay path forwarding; tests pin that both answer, that the eBay one forwards rather than re-implements, and that the Pro+ bulkActions gate survived the move. AC6: a tenant-isolation case now covers the agnostic price/end/bulk-edit paths. FOUND AND FIXED EN ROUTE (commit 07ea71c), not in any AC: the eBay adapter's delist checked platformOfferId alone, but a multi-variation eBay listing publishes as an inventory_item_group and has NO offer id — so when US-2162 pointed the listings page at the agnostic end route, every variation listing became un-endable and stayed LIVE on eBay. That is the US-1978 bug reintroduced through a different door, on the path whose whole purpose is to stop telling sellers an item is ended while buyers can still buy it. The adapter now uses the same resolveEndStrategy, and AdapterEndInput carries variations + the item SKU (the group key lives on the ITEM, so the join had to ask for it). STILL OPEN — the ONLY remaining gap: AC1 names 'price, revise and end' and there is still NO platform-agnostic revise. That one is a genuine design question rather than a move: revise on eBay means aspects, categories and markdown overlays, which most marketplaces do not have, so it may be legitimately eBay-shaped rather than an agnostic operation wearing an eBay costume. Recommend deciding that deliberately before building it. VERIFIED: 51 sync-precedence + 14 cross-listing-delist + 7 cross-listing-sale tests run under the Node harness, 48 frontend tests green, deno lint clean across 1269 files, 0 new type errors. | Done 2026-07-31. DECISION (owner's call): revise is the eBay OPERATOR and deliberately does NOT become platform-agnostic. That resolves the one gap left, and it resolves a tension that was inside the ACs from the start — AC1 listed revise beside price and end, while AC3 said the aspects and markdown-overlay pieces stay in flipdesk-ebay.ts. Revise IS those pieces: item aspects, leaf categories, markdown Sale overlays, and the inventory_item-vs-offer field split have no counterpart on the marketplaces the adapter covers, so forcing revise into a shared shape would have produced an operation that is eBay's everywhere except in name. AC1 is therefore read in AC3's favour: the platform-agnostic lifecycle is price and end; revise stays eBay's. The decision is recorded at the revise handler, not just here, so nobody 'fixes' it later. Being the eBay operator also means SAYING SO in code: loadListingOwned does not filter by platform, so a Shopify or Etsy listing id could reach the revise handler and would have gone on to call eBay's inventory/offer APIs with that row's ids — it now refuses with a 409 and code not_an_ebay_listing, naming the marketplace and pointing at the endpoint that does handle it. Two tests pin the refusal and the inverse (no /revise appears on the agnostic router, so a later accidental reversal is caught). FULL AC STATUS: AC1 met as resolved (price + end are agnostic and dispatch through the adapter from lib/listing-lifecycle.ts; revise is eBay's by decision). AC2 met — loadListingOwned never even selected platform, which is why the gate hardcoded 'ebay'; a published Shopify row therefore derived origin 'ebay' and its owner was told eBay owns its price. Fixed on all three gates, 4 tests including the inverse. AC3 met, and strengthened by the revise guard. AC4 met — the eBay-namespaced paths all still answer; price and bulk-edit now FORWARD instead of keeping a second copy, which is what AC4's own wording asked for. AC5 met — bulk-edit moved to flipdesk-listings.ts, eBay path forwards, Pro+ bulkActions gate proven to survive the move. AC6 met — tenant-isolation cases at the agnostic price/end/bulk-edit paths. Also fixed en route and in no AC: the eBay adapter's delist checked platformOfferId alone, so a multi-variation listing (published as an inventory_item_group, no offer id) became un-endable the moment US-2162 pointed the listings page at the agnostic route, and stayed LIVE on eBay — the US-1978 bug through a different door. VERIFIED: 51 sync-precedence + 14 cross-listing-delist + 7 cross-listing-sale tests under the Node harness, 48 frontend tests, npm run verify:web green except the two pre-existing US-2375 failures and the pre-existing npm-audit advisory, deno lint clean across 1269 files, 0 new type errors.

userStories.title: useItemsFull loads the tenant's entire inventory, every column, on 11 surfaces
userStories.description: As a reseller with a real catalog, I want FlipDesk pages to fetch only the rows and columns they render, so the app doesn't slow to a crawl as my inventory grows.
acceptanceCriteria: useItemsFull accepts an explicit column projection and a range/limit; `select("*")` with no bound is gone
Each of the 11 consumers declares the columns it actually reads
Surfaces that render a page of rows request that page server-side; surfaces that aggregate use a server-side aggregate rather than pulling rows to count them
The shared-cache-key hazard called out in the US-419 comment in listings.tsx is preserved: a narrower projection can never win a cache entry a wider consumer depends on
A guard test fails if an unbounded select on items_full is reintroduced
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/hooks/use-items-full.ts:52 is `.select("*").order("created_at")` with no range or limit, consumed by overview, pipeline, prep, grid, listings, item, composer, reconciliation and three components. Overlaps US-2023 (inventory.tsx paginates then loads everything anyway) — fold that story in or sequence them together. STILL OPEN as of 2026-07-25, but its blast radius is now recorded. The listings page's own read already uses a LISTINGS_COLUMNS projection; the unbounded .select("*") is in the SHARED useItemsFull hook, which the other 10 surfaces use. That is what makes this story risky rather than large: each consumer reads a different subset, and a missing column is undefined at runtime rather than a type error, so it fails silently in one column of one view. Do it with the app running, consumer by consumer. The US-2168 guard test (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) has a case that asserts the items_full read is STILL unprojected/unpaged — flip that expectation as part of this story so the gap can't quietly persist. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — four of five ACs are now met; AC3 is half-open and blocked, recorded rather than papered over. Most of this story had already landed under US-2188 (archived): src/lib/item-list-columns.ts owns the projection, use-items-full.ts splits into useItemsList (projected + paged) / useItemFull (one row) / useItemsFull (no consumers), and ItemListRow = Pick<ItemFullRow,…> makes a dropped column a tsc error rather than a blank cell. AC1 MET, AC2 MET, AC4 MET (the US-419 shared-cache hazard is preserved by giving the projected read its OWN key under the same ["items_full"] invalidation prefix). SHIPPED HERE: the ONE items_full read US-2188 did not own — src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx's listingsItemsKey query, which projects its own wider LISTINGS_COLUMNS and issued a single unbounded request. fetchItemsPaged is now EXPORTED from use-items-full.ts and the listings page calls it, so the db-max-rows cap is handled in one loop instead of being remembered in two places. This was a correctness fix, not only a cost one: PostgREST reports truncation only in Content-Range, supabase-js surfaces no error, so an over-cap seller saw a short listings table that looked complete — on the surface where a missed listing costs money. Behaviour is otherwise identical (same key, same newest-first order, same materialized array), so the client-side search/filter/sort/paging below it is untouched. AC5 MET: NEW src/test/items-full-bounded-reads.test.ts guards by ENUMERATION rather than by regex — every ("items_full") call site in src/ must be DECLARED with the bound it carries (use-items-full .range()/.maybeSingle(), grid.tsx .range()+count:exact, reconcile.tsx .limit(200)), and the scan asserts the declared set IS the whole set, so a new read fails until its author states its bound. AC3 STATUS: the aggregate half is MET — tab counts come from useInventoryStatusCounts (server-side grouped count) and flipdesk analytics reads RPC aggregates, so nothing counts by loading rows; grid.tsx already renders a server-side page (count:exact + .range). The OPEN half is the listings table, which still materializes the whole tenant because its search, tab filtering and sort run client-side over the full set and depend on scoreListability, which has no SQL equivalent. That is US-2168 AC3's blocker verbatim, so this story cannot close ahead of it. VERIFIED: 2944 tests pass (231 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green through the 216-route prerender.

userStories.title: The listings table fires six unbounded reads, then filters and paginates client-side

acceptanceCriteria: The cover-photo query stops reading every item_photos row for the tenant — covers come from a server-side per-item lowest-sort_order projection (view, RPC, or a join on the page's item ids)
The four secondary `listings` reads are scoped to the item ids on the current page rather than the whole tenant
Search, tab filtering and sort execute server-side so the client never needs the full set to render a page

Row-count parity is asserted against the current client-side behaviour so the migration can't silently change what a tab shows
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx issues items_full (all rows) + listings ×4 (:708, :749, :786, :853) + item_photos (:817). The item_photos read is the worst: no filter or limit, so it pulls EVERY photo row for the tenant to pick one cover per item — a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transfers ~4,000 rows to render 50 thumbnails. Depends on US-2167. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. DONE: all five per-row detail reads (platform chips, draft metadata, publish issues, cover thumbnails, impressions/CTR) now scope to the rendered page via .in("inventory_item_id", chunk) keyed on pageRowIds, chunked through fetchInChunks (at pageSize 200 a bare .in() puts ~7.4KB of UUIDs in the query string and risks a URL-length rejection at the proxy). The cover read was the worst case — no filter, no limit on item_photos, so a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transferred ~4,000 rows to draw 50 thumbnails; it is now bounded by page size. The five queries had to MOVE below pageRowIds in the component: hook order is now load-bearing, and a 17-case source guard (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) asserts the scope, the key, the chunking and the ordering. Safe to page-scope because all five are consumed only inside the row render — none feeds filtering, sorting, or the tab counts (those come from the server-side grouped count). NOT DONE: AC1's server-side lowest-sort_order projection (the client still picks the cover from the page's ordered photos — correct, and chunking preserves it because chunks are BY ITEM ID so an item's photos never span a chunk), and AC3 — search, tab filtering and sort are still CLIENT-side over the full set, because they depend on the still-tenant-wide items_full read (US-2167) and on scoreListability, which has no SQL equivalent. Those two ACs are blocked on US-2167, not skipped. KNOWN TRADE-OFF: paging now fetches per page, so a first visit to a page shows chips/thumbnails filling in; revisits are cached. That is the normal cost of not downloading the whole account.

userStories.title: No max_rows contract on any FlipDesk read — an over-cap seller could be shown a silently truncated catalog
userStories.description: As a reseller past whatever row cap PostgREST enforces, I want to be told my view is truncated, so I never make pricing or sourcing decisions on a quietly incomplete inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: The self-hosted PostgREST db-max-rows value in prod is established and recorded in vault/10-ops
Reads that could exceed it either paginate explicitly or request one row past their cap and surface a 'showing N of more' state
No FlipDesk surface can silently render a truncated set as if it were complete
The chosen cap is asserted in config so a future infra change can't move it unnoticed
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. Nothing in supabase/config.toml or docker-compose.coolify.yml sets a row cap, so the effective value is whatever the self-hosted PostgREST default is — unverified either way. If a cap IS in force, the unbounded reads in US-2167/US-2168 truncate with no error and no indication. Verify before assuming this is benign; the fix is cheap either way. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — AC2, AC3 and AC4 are MET; AC1 needs one operator step that cannot be done from this host, and the code is deliberately built not to depend on it. FINDING THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the story asked whether a cap is in force. It is not knowable from here (nothing sets db-max-rows in supabase/config.toml, which configures only the throwaway local verify stack, nor in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is the edge service and not Kong/PostgREST), and worse, TWO EXISTING PAGING LOOPS were only correct while the cap was at least their page size — src/hooks/use-items-full.ts and src/pages/flipdesk/bulk-pricing.tsx both advanced by their CHUNK constant and broke on a short page. Below the ceiling every request comes back capped-short, so the loop stops on its FIRST request and the paging written to prevent silent truncation performs it instead. So rather than establish the number and depend on it, the reads no longer need to know it. NEW src/lib/paged-read.ts owns three things: fetchAllPages() advances by the rows ACTUALLY RETURNED and stops only on an EMPTY response (never a short one), so any ceiling costs round trips and nothing else; fetchCapped() asks for limit+1 and drops the probe row so the truncated flag is evidence rather than a guess; and READ_PAGE_SIZE / ASSUMED_DB_MAX_ROWS / CAPPED_READ_LIMIT name the assumption once. AC2 MET: use-items-full.ts and bulk-pricing.tsx now call fetchAllPages; listing-performance.tsx's flat .limit(1000) became a paged read (a cut at 1000 hid exactly the low-view tail the report exists to surface); autolister-drafts.tsx and scheduled-drops.tsx use fetchCapped. Every remaining fixed .limit() in FlipDesk is small enough (25/100/200) that it cannot reach any plausible ceiling. AC3 MET: NEW src/components/flipdesk/truncated-notice.tsx renders 'Showing the first N …. There are more.' on both capped queues. reconcile.tsx's link picker was the worst case and was not truncation at all — it fetched the 200 most-recently-UPDATED items and then filtered client-side to photo_count===0 + linkable status, so a seller whose recent touches were all photographed saw an EMPTY picker while plenty of candidates existed; the cap was silently choosing the WRONG 200 rows. Both predicates now run server-side (.eq(photo_count,0).in(status,…)) so the limit applies to real candidates, and a search that finds nothing against a capped pool now says the pool was capped instead of implying no such item exists. AC4 MET: NEW src/test/row-cap-contract.test.ts (13 cases) asserts CAPPED_READ_LIMIT+1 <= ASSUMED_DB_MAX_ROWS (or the +1 probe stops being answerable and the notice goes silent again), exercises fetchAllPages against a server that clips EVERY response at 137 rows against a 1000-row catalog, and scans src/ for both regression shapes — a hand-rolled short-page-break loop (.length < CHUNK then break) and any for-loop over .range() outside the shared reader. AC1 PARTIAL: vault/10-ops/postgrest-row-cap.md records the contract, the three allowed read shapes, why stop-on-short is wrong, and that the prod value is NOT established — with the operator step named. REMAINING: read db-max-rows off the self-hosted stack and record it in that note. VERIFIED: 2957 tests pass (232 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors (10 pre-existing warnings), build green, vault-lint 107 notes clean, impeccable clean on the new component.

userStories.title: No undo on any bulk listing action — a 200-listing markdown is irreversible
userStories.description: As a reseller who just bulk-dropped prices on the wrong selection, I want to undo the batch, so one mis-click doesn't mean repricing 200 listings by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: A bulk action records the prior value per affected listing and returns an undo handle
Undo is offered in the success toast for a bounded window and re-pushes the restored values upstream through the adapters — not just locally
Undo reports per-row outcomes: a listing that sold or was ended between the action and the undo is skipped and named
Actions that genuinely cannot be undone (a published listing, a withdrawn offer) say so instead of offering a button that silently no-ops
Covers the bulk paths that exist today: price drop, bulk edit, bulk publish, archive, delete
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. CORRECTION (2026-07-25): the original note here said nothing in the codebase implements undo. That was wrong — it came from grepping only for bulkUndo/undo_token/bulk_undo. src/pages/flipdesk/autolister.tsx has a working undo for photo-GROUPING edits (undoLastGroupEdit / undoAutoGroup) using sonner's toast action, and that is the house pattern to follow. What genuinely had no undo is every bulk action on the LISTINGS TABLE: price, edit, publish, archive, delete. US-1348 specified 'multi-select batch + undo'; the batch half shipped and the undo half did not. Depends on US-2163/US-2166 landing the server-side batch path, which is where the prior values can be captured atomically. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 — the PRICE path only. /bulk-price gained a third body shape, `items: [{listing_id, price}]`, because undo needs each row to go back to its OWN former price and no shared price or percentage can express that; the response already returned previous_price per row, so the machinery was half-built by US-2163. The bulk-drop toast now carries an Undo action (15s, matching the autolister pattern). undoableFrom() decides what is reversible and is unit-tested: a row the marketplace REFUSED is excluded (it never changed, so restoring it would push a price nobody asked for), as are rows with no known/positive previous price and no-op rows. Undo is itself a real marketplace push, so it reports its own per-row failures rather than implying a clean revert. NOT DONE: bulk edit, bulk publish, archive and delete (AC5's full list). Publish and delete are arguably NOT undoable at all and per AC4 should say so rather than offer a button — that judgement is still open. Bulk END is the next most valuable: relisting is a real operation, not a field restore, so it needs its own design rather than a mirror of this one. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — AC5's remaining paths are now covered; the story stays open only for bulk END, which needs its own design. AC5 status: price drop (shipped 2026-07-25), bulk EDIT (shipped here), archive/status (shipped here), publish + delete (AC4 treatment, shipped here). SHIPPED HERE, (1) the bulk STATUS change, which was the quiet one: it pushes nothing to a marketplace, so there is no failure to notice — a seller who archives 200 items just finds them in the wrong stage with no record of where each came from. NEW src/lib/bulk-status-undo.ts holds the decisions as pure functions; listings.tsx bulkSetStatus captures a per-row entry only AFTER the write succeeds (a failed row never changed and must not be offered), and the demote path also records the listing half it rewrote (listing_status + is_active via syncListingForDraftStatus) because restoring only the item status would leave the listing half-rewound. is_active is DERIVED from the prior listing_status rather than read, since it is not in LISTINGS_COLUMNS and a guessed boolean is worse than a stated rule. AC3: undoBulkStatus RE-READS current state instead of trusting the cached array the batch ran against — the seconds between the action and the undo click are exactly where a sale lands, and planStatusUndo refuses a row whose status moved since, whose listing went sold or ended, or that is gone, naming each. (2) the bulk EDIT undo, which needed an endpoint change because the reverse of a bulk edit is NOT another bulk edit: every listing goes back to its OWN former price/condition/policy and no shared patch can say that. EDGE: bulk-listing-edit.ts gains normalizeBulkEditItems (parses items: [{listing_id, edit}], last-write-wins on a duplicated id) and processBulkEdit now accepts fieldNames as a FUNCTION as well as an array, so existing callers and tests are untouched; BulkEditItemResult gains previous (present only on ok). The route captures prior values from the SAME snapshot the write is planned against, and its SELECT grew the seven editable columns. Tenant scoping is unchanged: items ids go through the identical .in(id, ids) + .eq(inventory_items.user_id) query, so an id the caller does not own resolves to null and reports Listing not found. (3) AC4 for the two that genuinely cannot be undone: bulk publish now says 'Publishing can't be undone — use End to take one down' and names the real operation instead of leaving the seller hunting for a button; bulk delete repeats its permanence in the toast, where a seller actually looks for Undo. Neither offers an Undo action. VERIFIED: 22 unit cases on the pure planners (including the ones only reachable when the world changes BETWEEN the batch and the undo click); 13-case source guard src/test/bulk-action-undo.test.ts proving each path is wired to its planner and that publish/delete carry no Undo; 11 assertion groups run against the esbuild-compiled bulk-listing-edit module (no deno on this host, so the deno suite runs in CI) plus 7 new Deno.test cases added to bulk-listing-edit_test.ts; frontend 2994 tests pass, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green. The US-2167 items_full guard caught the undo's own read-back and it is now declared with its bound. REMAINING: bulk END. Relisting is a real marketplace operation, not a field restore — it spends a fresh insertion fee and re-consumes an activeListings slot — so it needs its own design rather than a mirror of this one, and is deliberately not bolted on here.

userStories.title: listings.tsx is 3,581 lines in one component — the highest-traffic surface is the hardest to change

acceptanceCriteria: Column definitions, tab predicates, the query layer and the mutation handlers each move to their own module
Every mutation handler becomes a testable unit that does not require rendering the page

userStories.notes: [P3][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx holds LISTINGS_COLUMNS, the TABS predicates, six useQuery blocks, ~10 mutation handlers and the virtualizer in one file. Do this AFTER US-2162/US-2163/US-2168 so the refactor moves already-correct code rather than carrying the bugs across. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — two of AC1's four moves are done plus AC5 in full; AC2 and AC3 remain and are recorded with the reason rather than half-attempted. The page is 3,505 lines, down from 3,844 at the start of this pass (and from 3,581 when the story was written, which had since grown). MOVED OUT, behaviour unchanged: (1) tab predicates — TABS + TO_LIST_STATUSES + DRAFT_LIKE_STATUSES went to the existing sibling src/pages/flipdesk/inventory-tabs.ts under US-2178, and matchesSearch / matchesSoldFilter / payoutState / planListingDemote to NEW listings-filter.ts, all now unit-tested (61 cases). (2) the query layer — NEW src/pages/flipdesk/listings-page-queries.ts exports usePageRowDetails(), holding all five US-2168 page-scoped detail reads (platform chips, draft metadata, publish issues, cover thumbnails, impressions/CTR) plus the US-2170 quality-score read and the PlatformChip / DraftMeta types. (3) column definitions — NEW listings-columns.ts owns LISTINGS_COLUMNS, which is the one thing on this page a projection pass has to change and was previously found by scrolling. AC5 MET AND NOW ENFORCED: a refactor is exactly when a comment gets dropped, and neither of these losses has a symptom a test would otherwise catch — US-419's is a subtle cache bug, US-1489's is a render loop nobody attributes to the deleted line. So the guard now asserts them: US-419's DISTINCT-key rationale must still sit with listingsItemsKey, all three US-1489 effect-dependency notes must survive, US-733's threshold must survive, and the US-2168 page-scoping rationale must have travelled WITH the reads (including the hooks-run-in-order caller constraint, which the module now states because it is the module's to state). AC4: one honest deviation. The behavioural tests pass unmodified, but src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts is a SOURCE SCAN and is file-path-bound, so it had to follow the code it guards — it now reads the query module for the five per-row reads and listings.tsx for the main read and the US-2372 optimistic writes, which stayed. The hook-order case is the interesting one: the constraint moved from 'where the queries sit' to 'where the hook is called', so the assertion moved with it rather than disappearing along with the code it used to check. NOT DONE, deliberately: AC2 (every mutation handler a testable unit) and AC3 (the virtualized table as its own component). The ~10 handlers close over a dozen pieces of component state each, and the table body is the largest single block of JSX in the file with dozens of prop dependencies; both are the kind of move that needs the app driven to confirm, and this host has no runtime. What WAS extractable from the handlers without that — the pure decisions they turn on — is already out and tested: planListingDemote (US-2178) and the two undo planners (US-2172). VERIFIED: 3070 tests pass (237 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green through the 216-route prerender.

userStories.title: listings has grown to ~52 columns across 41 ALTER TABLE migrations
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the listings table's per-platform and per-integration fields organized, so every read of a listing doesn't pay for every feature we ever shipped.
acceptanceCriteria: The columns are inventoried and classified: core lifecycle, eBay-specific, cross-listing, metrics, and dead
Genuinely dead columns are dropped; single-platform fields are assessed for a move into platform_fields
No caller reads a column by `select("*")` on listings after the change
Any migration follows the US-1108 triple
userStories.notes: [P3][FlipDesk/Schema] 2026-07-25 deep dive. 11 base columns in 00002_inventory_financial.sql plus 41 added by ALTER TABLE across the migration set. Not urgent on its own — it is the reason the reads in US-2167/US-2168 are expensive, so measure after those land and only cut what is provably dead. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — AC1 and AC3 are MET; AC2 is ANSWERED rather than deferred, and the answer is that there is nothing to drop, which makes AC4 moot. The story's own note said to measure first and only cut what is provably dead, so this pass is the measurement. NEW scripts/audit-listings-columns.mjs parses every CREATE TABLE and ADD COLUMN touching listings, then counts references across src, edge, functions, ios, android, sdk and the migrations, reporting TWO counts per column on purpose: a loose word-boundary count (the SAFE bias — over-counting only ever prevents a drop) and a strict column-shaped count of quoted names and object keys (the signal — 'views' and 'watchers' are ordinary English and their loose counts are mostly prose, which would read as heavily-used and stop anyone from ever looking). THREE FINDINGS, two of which contradict the story's premise. (1) NINETY-ONE columns, not the ~52 estimated: the estimate counted 11 base plus 41 ALTER TABLE statements, and several statements add more than one column. (2) NOTHING IS PROVABLY DEAD. Exactly one column, search_vec, has zero application references — and it is not dead, it is a tsvector maintained by a trigger and read by a GIN index, so Postgres is its only consumer. Every other column is referenced by name. AC2 therefore has nothing to drop and no migration is warranted; the cost of this table is the WIDTH of its reads, not corpses in it, which is why the actual wins came from US-2167's projection work. (3) NEW: ListingRow in src/types/database.ts is SIXTEEN columns behind the schema, including heavily-used ones (platform_fields, needs_review, quality_score, marketplace_connection_id, inventory_sku) — so code touching them goes through an untyped cast and a rename is invisible to tsc. The script cross-checks type-vs-schema, so re-running it after any listings migration surfaces this. AC3 MET, with one interpretation stated rather than assumed: the rule enforced is 'a LIST read must project; a bounded SINGLE-ROW read may use select(*)', because the cost is width multiplied by rows and one row is one row — the same distinction US-2188 already made when it kept useItemFull unprojected. NEW src/test/listings-select-star.test.ts guards by ENUMERATION: all three existing call sites are declared with the bound they carry, and the declared set must be the whole set, so a fourth fails until its author states why. Negative-verified by appending a bare select(*) to prep.tsx (reddened, reverted). The data export is declared as a deliberate EXEMPTION with its own case, because the obvious 'fix' there is the bug: projecting it would silently omit columns from a record the user is legally entitled to, and the export would still look complete. AC4 N/A — no migration. Vault: NEW vault/20-domain/listings-column-inventory.md carries the classification and the read policy and points at the script for the numbers rather than restating them. REMAINING before passes:true: AC2's second clause, assessing single-platform eBay fields for a move into the existing platform_fields jsonb. Deliberately not done — jsonb costs typing and indexability, the columns are cheap now that reads are projected, and moving them is a schema migration with no measured benefit behind it. That is a product/schema call worth making with numbers from prod, not from this host. VERIFIED: 3076 tests pass (238 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green, vault-lint 108 notes clean.

userStories.title: The 3,581-line listings page has two tests; the actions that can cost a sale have none
userStories.description: As a developer changing the listings surface, I want its behaviour covered by tests, so I find out from CI rather than from a seller that End or a bulk price drop broke.
acceptanceCriteria: End, publish, bulk price drop, archive and delete each have a test asserting which endpoint is called for which platform, and what happens on each failure mode

Tests run in the existing vitest lane with no new harness
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/pages/flipdesk/__tests__/ contains only draft-quality.test.ts and status-param-to-tab.test.ts. The edge side is well covered (538 deno tests, ~40 listings-related), so this gap is frontend-specific — and it is where the US-2162/US-2163 divergence bugs live. Write the failing tests as part of those stories; this story covers the rest. | Done 2026-08-01. AC1: End and bulk price drop were already covered by src/hooks/__tests__/use-listing-lifecycle.test.ts (33 cases, shipped with US-2162/US-2163); publish and hard delete had nothing and now do. NEW src/hooks/__tests__/publish-and-delete.test.ts (10 cases) asserts usePublishToEbay posts to /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/push, sends relist ONLY when asked (a default relist would silently churn item numbers and reset every listing's search standing), composes the 422 blockers array into the thrown message rather than dropping it (on a 200-row bulk publish 'Publish failed.' with no field name sends the seller to open items one at a time), treats a 200 carrying ok:false as a refusal, and names a fallback on an unreadable body; and that useDeleteItem targets /listings/item/:id with the id encoded and carries the 409 guard code onto the error, since that code is how the UI tells a protective refusal apart from a fault. To get there, the predicates and two helpers moved OUT of the 3,886-line page with behaviour unchanged: TABS + TO_LIST_STATUSES + DRAFT_LIKE_STATUSES into the existing sibling src/pages/flipdesk/inventory-tabs.ts, and matchesSearch / matchesSoldFilter / payoutState / planListingDemote into NEW src/pages/flipdesk/listings-filter.ts. matchesSoldFilter takes `now` as a parameter, which is what makes the d7/d30/ytd boundaries assertable at all. Covered: every ItemStatus lands in exactly one stage tab (a status no tab matches is an item that vanishes from the only surface that lists it), All excludes archived, sort key + direction per tab, substring/case/multi-column search and the fields-must-not-run-together case, the fee-discrepancy threshold INCLUDING the exact-20% boundary, window edges, and undated/unparseable sale dates excluded from every date window rather than silently placed in one. The live-offer branch is the one that can cost a sale -- demoting a published listing to draft locally makes FlipDesk show it as unlisted while it is still purchasable, so the seller stops watching a listing that can still sell (the US-2162 failure class). userStories.title: perf: paginate/project useItemsFull to bound FlipDesk reads

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage

acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.

Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.

userStories.description: As a buyer trusting a GradeThread certificate, I want the brand, size, style code and fiber content on it to have been READ off the garment's own label, so that the certificate identifies the item rather than repeating what the seller claimed. Verified today: lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts exists and does exactly this job (a focused vision pass over ONLY the tag photos returning brand/size/fiber_content/style_code/rn_number verbatim with per-field confidence), but its only callers are lib/ai-listing.ts and lib/ai-size-estimate.ts — both FlipDesk AutoLister paths. The grading pipeline never imports it. Grading's own label handling is one line of the per-image prompt (ai-grading.ts:274) that transcribes fiber_content for the fabric-criteria block and nothing else; brand reaches the composite prompt only via ai-grading.ts:1589 as sanitized, fenced, explicitly-untrusted seller text. So the two halves of the same product read the same photograph to completely different depths, and the half that prints a public certificate is the shallow one.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline runs extractTagGroundTruth over the submission's label/label_2 images and persists the result (brand, size, fiber_content, style_code, rn_number, each with its confidence) on the submission or grade report.

Read fields enter the composite prompt as TRUSTED server-generated context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence; the seller's own typed brand/title stays inside the fence, and a test asserts the two channels are never merged.
The composite prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, with a distinct version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the tag-grounded era.
A read below TAG_GROUND_TRUTH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) is discarded rather than shown — an illegible tag must not produce a confident identity.
A read that CONTRADICTS the seller-declared brand or size is surfaced (report field or review flag) rather than silently overwritten in either direction.
Tag-OCR adds a vision call per grade: it is metered through the existing ai-usage/ai-budget path and gated so it cannot run on submissions with no label photo.
Disabled (flag off or no label photo) the composite prompt is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). THE HEADLINE FINDING of the review: the AutoLister reads a garment tag far more carefully than the certificate does. lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts is a finished, tested, metered module (249 lines, ai-tag-ocr_test.ts green) and grading does not call it. Highest value-per-unit-of-work item in the epic because the code already exists — this is wiring plus a prompt-version cycle, not new capability. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (flag-gated OFF, awaiting eval). Commit 5b4ea22. AC1 DONE: processSubmission runs extractTagGroundTruth over label/label_2 photos INSIDE the existing withImageBufferSlot closure, in parallel with the per-image pass, over base64 that is ALREADY RESIDENT — one extra vision call, zero extra downloads, no change to the memory gate that bounds grading concurrency. Persisted to new grade_reports.tag_read (migration 00496, nullable jsonb). AC2 DONE: new lib/tag-ground-truth.ts renders the read as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence alongside baseline/fabric; seller text stays inside; two tests pin it, including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence. AC3 PARTIAL BY DESIGN: the +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are in, but the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR (default OFF) exactly as US-1533 gated baselines — shadow/eval/canary REQUIRE live vision calls and cannot run in this sandbox, so activation stays a deliberate operator step. AC4 DONE (0.4 bar, tested at/below/above). AC5 DONE: a brand disagreement is REPORTED not resolved — neither value overwrites the other; formatting-only differences (Levi's/LEVIS/levi s) are deliberately not mismatches; emits grading.tag_discrepancy + a warn log. AC6 DONE: own recordAiUsage feature row 'tag_ocr' so the added cost is measurable on its own rather than buried in per_image; gated on the flag AND on a label photo existing. AC7 DONE: empty block => composite prompt byte-identical, asserted three ways including a full-string equality on the only-difference-is-the-block property. THREE THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The grade_reports insert uses a CONDITIONAL SPREAD, not tag_read: tagRead — a null-VALUED key still NAMES the column in the PostgREST payload and would 42703 the whole insert, and with it the paid grade, anywhere 00496 has not been applied. That spread is what makes the commit safe to deploy ahead of the SQL; do not 'simplify' it. (2) KNOWN COST EDGE, accepted: the read runs before the image-quality gate (same as the authenticity add-on), so a submission that later abstains on an illegible label has already paid for it. Sequencing the gate first would serialize the hot path on every grade to save a call on the abstaining minority — the same trade fabric-criteria.ts already documents. (3) The escalation path forwards the SAME tag block and does NOT re-read the tag: a verbatim transcription does not get truer on a bigger model. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth now accepts data URIs as well as URLs (tagImageSource), which is what let grading reuse resident bytes; the FlipDesk URL callers are unchanged. tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (content-public.ts CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) — publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity is a product call that waits for eval numbers.
