userStories.notes: [P1][Buyer/Cost] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | Done 2026-08-01. THE REPORT IS A FALSE POSITIVE on AC1 and AC2 — verified directly, and recording that is the point, because the next reader would otherwise "fix" an endpoint that is already correct. AC1 ALREADY MET: routes/buyer-authenticity.ts gates on the authenticityAddon entitlement (403 not_entitled) BEFORE reading the body, then reserves one credit through withBuyerMeter("authenticity_credits", ent.allowances.authenticityCreditsPerMonth) — included allowance → reward credits → upgrade (US-1800/1813) — and the reservation wraps the AI call, so it is refunded automatically if scoring throws. Quota exhaustion returns 402. This shipped with US-1840. AC2 ALREADY MET, in two layers: the per-user cap IS the monthly authenticity_credits allowance, and the global cap is reserveGlobalDailyBudget() called inside the metered block, on top of the process-wide ceiling every non-streaming call already goes through. AC3 WAS THE REAL WORK, and doing it found a genuine gap the story did not name. The sweep: 44 getAnthropicClient() call sites across 33 modules. Every NON-STREAMING call is bounded in ONE place — applyAiLimiter (ai-config.ts) wraps messages.create with the global concurrency cap, daily volume ceiling and retry authority, so a call site cannot opt out by accident. Route-level metering already had a drift guard (this same file, US-1581) with a documented allow-list, and buyer-authenticity.ts is in it with an accurate rationale. So no unmetered ROUTE exists. THE GAP: streaming DELIBERATELY bypasses applyAiLimiter — an SSE flow is a long-lived single call, and wrapping a stream in await/retry would break it. That bypass is correct AND it means a streaming call site is bounded by NOTHING the client provides: no daily ceiling, no concurrency cap. Each must carry its own gate and meter. Both current sites do — content-ai-stream.ts is operator-driven (scheduler/admin, no self-serve surface to meter) and support-assistant.ts gates non-subscribers and locked-out users BEFORE any model call then meters explicitly post-stream via incrementUsage, precisely because create() is bypassed (US-834/US-831). But NOTHING enforced that, so the next streaming feature would have been unbounded with no test to notice — which is exactly the shape of the risk this story was filed about, one layer down from where it looked. SHIPPED: three new Deno cases in ai-metering-coverage_test.ts. Every streaming call site must be DECLARED with the control that replaces the limiter (exact equality, so a new one fails until its author states which control it has — the moment that decision actually gets made — and a removed one fails until dropped); the support assistant's two halves (pre-call gate, post-stream meter) must still be present, since losing either makes an unbounded unbilled model call reachable by any authenticated user; and the non-streaming wrapper must still be applied by the client factory rather than per call site, which is the property that makes the route allow-list safe. VERIFIED: the scan logic executed against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — it finds exactly the two declared sites and the controls are present. It initially reported a THIRD, flipdesk-listings.ts, from `ended_upstream: true` matching a loose `stream:\s*true`; tightened with a word boundary, because a false positive in a guard is how a guard gets deleted. Frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean, test file parses clean. No production code changed — the endpoint was already correct.

userStories.title: Provenance boosts raise confidence above caps set inside compositeGrade
userStories.description: grading-pipeline.ts:2109 seeds the running ceiling from partialSuccess only (`let confidenceCeiling = partialSuccess ? PARTIAL_IMAGE_CONFIDENCE_CAP : 1`). The four caps applied inside compositeGrade — authenticity 0.6, defaulted-factor 0.5, prompt-injection 0.5 (ai-grading.ts:1815-1821), defect-divergence 0.6 (ai-grading.ts:2405) — are already baked into the composite confidence and the ceiling never records them. Three boost sites then raise confidence clamped only to 1: verified capture (:2316), live capture (:2429), verified 360 (:2539). A grade capped at 0.5 for a hallucinated factor can be stored at up to 1.0. The review gate itself holds, but the stored number feeds the public confidence_label bucket and the calibration miner that derives future thresholds. This directly violates the grading-engine skill's 'never raise confidence post-composite' rule.
acceptanceCriteria: compositeGrade returns the ceiling it applied, and the pipeline seeds confidenceCeiling from it.
Every boost site clamps to that ceiling, not to 1.
Regression test per cap: a submission with a defaulted factor plus live capture plus verified 360 stores confidence at or below 0.5.
The grading-engine skill's invariant list is updated to name the mechanism, not just the rule.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Confidence] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Directly contradicts a documented skill invariant. | Done 2026-08-01. RE-VERIFIED FIRST as the note asked, and PART OF THE REPORT IS STALE — worth recording because the stale half would have sent the next reader to the wrong file. The report says the three boost sites clamp "only to 1". They do not: US-1622/C9 already clamps all three (verified capture, live capture, verified 360) to the running confidenceCeiling. AC2 was therefore ALREADY MET before this session. What was genuinely broken is exactly AC1: the ceiling was seeded `partialSuccess ? PARTIAL_IMAGE_CONFIDENCE_CAP : 1` and only ever tightened by post-composite LOWERING events (visual-verification discrepancies, peer-norm), both of which are conditional. The four caps applied INSIDE compositeGrade — authenticity 0.6, defaulted-factor 0.5, prompt-injection 0.5, defect-divergence 0.6 — were baked into the composite confidence and never recorded anywhere the ceiling could see, so on a submission where neither lowering event fired the ceiling stayed at 1 and a provenance boost could lift a grade capped at 0.5 for a hallucinated factor back toward 1.0 and STORE it. AC1 DONE: applyGradingConfidencePolicy now returns confidenceCeiling (the min of whichever caps fired, 1 if none), compositeGrade folds the divergence cap into it and passes it out as CompositeGradeResult.confidence_ceiling, and the pipeline seeds its running ceiling from min(partial-image cap, that value). THE DESIGN POINT, because the obvious alternative is wrong: the ceiling is reported SEPARATELY from finalConfidence, and the pipeline must not seed from the confidence VALUE. Seeding from the value would freeze confidence and disable the provenance boosts entirely, which are a deliberate product feature. Seeding from the CEILING lets an uncapped grade still earn its boost while a capped one can never be lifted past its cap. AC3 DONE: 8 new cases in grading-confidence_test.ts — ceiling 1 when nothing fired, each cap individually, caps COMPOSING by min (an authenticity flag at 0.6 plus a defaulted factor at 0.5 must land on 0.5, not on whichever was checked last), the ceiling never RAISING a grade the model itself scored low (it is a maximum, never a target — reading it as one is the same violation pointing the other way), a 72-combination grid asserting finalConfidence <= confidenceCeiling always, and a source assertion that the pipeline seeds from the composite AND that all three boost sites still clamp to the running ceiling. AC4 DONE: the grading-engine skill's invariant list now names the MECHANISM — a new cap must lower the value AND the reported ceiling, because doing only the first is invisible: the review gate still fires so the grade goes to a human and looks handled, while the next boost lifts the stored number back over the cap. WHY THIS MATTERED DESPITE THE REVIEW GATE HOLDING: the stored number is what the public confidence_label bucket shows a buyer and what the calibration miner reads to derive future thresholds. A wrong-but-confident number there is precisely the failure the contract's never-raise rule exists to prevent, and it lands somewhere nobody is looking. VERIFIED: 72-combination grid plus 12 targeted assertions run against the extracted policy in Node (no deno on this host, so the Deno suite runs in CI); both changed lib files and the test parse clean; confirmed no other site constructs a CompositeGradeResult literal, so the new required field breaks no caller; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. Rounding sites untouched, so the lockstep rule is unaffected.

Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding". DOC CORRECTED (the story's own closing note asked for exactly this): .claude/skills/grading-engine/references/prompt-lifecycle.md read as if a pipeline gate existed. It now opens with what the gate does NOT cover — no CI gate, code defaults with no DB row — while stating clearly that the part which IS real (activation and canary refusing an un-evaled version, via checkPromptServingEligibility, US-2300) applies only to versions that go through a DB row. VERIFIED: 4 alert assertions plus the seeding scan run against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — the scan reports exactly composite_v4 and per_image_v5 as unseeded, matching the declaration; grading-monitor.ts and the test parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm against prod what grading_eval_cases holds and which ai_prompt_versions are active) — operator only, and it should be done BEFORE the rest, as the AC says. AC3 (seed rows for the code defaults) — a migration, push-blocked here. AC2 (eval in CI) — depends on AC1/AC3: a CI eval against an empty golden set would be theatre, and the golden set must grow from REAL human-corrected grades, never fabricated ones, so it cannot be seeded from this host either. AC6 (EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 lets a prompt be a full grade point off on a 1-10 scale and still pass) — a product judgement about acceptable error, with a real cost either way, and it belongs to the owner rather than to a sandbox.

userStories.title: release_job_lock has no holder check, so an over-running job destroys its successor's lock
userStories.description: 00094_job_locks.sql:63-70 defines release_job_lock(p_job) as an unconditional DELETE, and lib/job-lock.ts:71 always passes p_holder: null so a holder check is not even possible today. Scenario: autolister-reclaim has a 300s lease and a */5 schedule — lease equals interval exactly. A run taking 5m30s means tick 2 legitimately steals the expired lock at t=5:00, then run 1's finally block deletes tick 2's live lock at t=5:30, and tick 3 acquires freely and runs concurrently. Mutual exclusion does not degrade, it disappears, and the more loaded the box the more concurrent runs there are. userStories.title: eBay orders sync advances its cursor after swallowing a failure — permanent order loss
userStories.description: flipdesk-ebay.ts:3219-3226 wraps the entire orders pass in a catch that logs and continues, then execution falls through to an unconditional cursor stamp at :3490-3493 setting last_synced_at to now(). Scenario: a seller has 500 orders modified since the last sync, eBay 500s at order 200. Orders 1-199 are committed, 200-500 are never written, and the cursor now says 'now', so the next incremental pull asks eBay only for orders modified since now (ebay-client.ts:3398) and the 301 missing orders are never re-fetched. Sales rows, payouts, net_profit and the inventory_items.status='sold' flip are gone for good. The HTTP response was already 202 {ok:true} and the UI shows 'Synced just now'. The backstop cannot recover it: jobs-ebay-order-backstop.ts:85-100 selects stale owners by that same last_synced_at. Same loss without a throw when ORDERS_PAGE_CEILING is hit (ebay-client.ts:3503-3507) — it only pushes a warning string into errors[] and the cursor still advances. Shopify does this correctly: flipdesk-shopify.ts:357-363 gates the watermark on ingest.ok and lib/shopify-orders.ts:62-68 documents exactly this failure mode.
acceptanceCriteria: last_synced_at is gated on the orders pass completing cleanly, or advanced only to the max lastModifiedDate actually persisted. Mirror lib/shopify-orders.ts.
Hitting the page ceiling is treated as incomplete, not as success.
The sync response and the UI reflect a partial sync rather than reading 'Synced just now'.
flipdesk-ebay.ts:3149-3153 and :3128-3131 destructure away the Supabase error and increment salesNew/salesUpdated anyway — read the error before counting.
Regression test: an injected failure mid-pass leaves the cursor unmoved.
Assume this has already fired. Plan a one-off backfill that re-pulls a wide window for every eBay connection.
userStories.notes:
[P0][FlipDesk/eBay] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-impact marketplace finding — it is silent, permanent, and triggers on any transient eBay error. | [2026-08-01] Fixed. Re-verified the audit claim first and it was right, with corrected line numbers: the orders pass catch is flipdesk-ebay.ts:3312 (logs, pushes to errors[], carries on), the unconditional cursor stamp was at :3581, listRecentOrders is ebay-client.ts:3401 and its ORDERS_PAGE_CEILING truncation only pushed a warning STRING into errors[] at :3520. Confirmed the backstop cannot recover it: jobs-ebay-order-backstop.ts selects stale owners by that same last_synced_at, which the failed run had just refreshed.

Root cause worth naming: last_synced_at does double duty. It is the incremental ORDERS CURSOR (doListingsPull reads it back as `since`) and it is the "the job finished" ping the UI polls. "Log and continue" is right for a listings pass and is data loss for a cursor pass, because a cursor is a promise that everything before it was persisted.

AC1 + AC2 done via a new pure module lib/sync-watermark.ts, planOrdersWatermark():
- fetch incomplete (a throw mid-paging, OR the page ceiling) -> do not advance at all. We do not know what we did not see, so there is no safe value.
- fetch complete but some orders failed to persist -> rewind to the EARLIEST failure. eBay's lastmodifieddate filter is inclusive, so handing back the failed order's own timestamp re-fetches it.
- clean -> now(), unchanged.
Rewinding rather than freezing on per-order failures is deliberate: freezing means one permanently-malformed order pins the cursor forever and the seller re-pulls the whole 90-day window on every sync until a human notices. A failure with no lastModifiedDate has no safe rewind target, so that case freezes (fails closed).

listRecentOrders now returns { orders, complete } instead of RemoteOrder[] - the ceiling had to become readable to the caller making the cursor decision, and a warning string is not. runOrderReport is all-or-nothing (throws unless the whole report parsed), so the Feed path counts as complete.

AC3 done, though not the way the AC imagines. The response is 202 fired detached, so it cannot carry the verdict. What it does instead: the cursor not moving IS the UI signal - marketplaces.tsx detects completion by last_synced_at CHANGING from a pre-sync baseline, so a lost window no longer reads "Synced just now" (it falls to the existing 5-minute "taking longer than expected" path). Plus an explicit "This sync is PARTIAL" line pushed into errors[], which drives recordSyncRun's status:'partial' on the Reconciliation page.

AC4 done. Both writes read their error now and throw: the update discarded it entirely and bumped salesUpdated regardless; the insert destructured only `data`, so a failed insert left insertedSale null - skipping the consignor payout AND the sale notification - while salesNew still counted it as imported. Throwing routes them into the per-order catch, which is what records them as failed orders and rewinds the cursor.

AC5 done. tests/sync-watermark_test.ts: clean/throw/ceiling/rewind/undatable/future-timestamp cases plus source assertions on the route (planOrdersWatermark present, the unconditional now() stamp regex ABSENT, ordersFetchComplete=false in the catch, both write-error strings, the PARTIAL line) and on ebay-client (the {orders, complete} return). Negative-verified the guard regex matches the exact old line.

AC6 done as a plan, not a run - it needs prod. vault/10-ops/ebay-orders-backfill.md: who is affected (treat every eBay connection as affected; there is no stored marker for the failed runs), the recovery (POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/pull?full=true per connection, sequentially, since it ignores last_synced_at and reaches ~23 months), why it must be spaced out, and what it cannot recover (orders older than ~24 months are rejected by eBay errorId 30830 and need a Seller Hub export).

OPERATOR TASK REMAINING: run that backfill for every active eBay connection after this deploys.

Verified: planOrdersWatermark assertions run in Node via esbuild bundle (no Deno on this host), all 8 source assertions pass, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, vitest 239 files / 3079 tests green, vault:index + vault:lint clean. The Deno tests are unverified until a PR runs CI.

userStories.title: The entire Google integration has no fetch timeout — 22 call sites
userStories.description: lib/circuit-breaker.ts:30 provides fetchWithTimeout and every eBay/Etsy/Depop/Shopify/Whatnot client uses it at 20-25s. The Google integration was never migrated. Bare fetch with no AbortSignal at: google-sheets-api.ts:51 (all reads/writes; all four constructors use the default bare fetch), google-service-account.ts:144, flipdesk-google.ts:184/208/311/402/458/615 (OAuth exchange, userinfo, refresh mint, sheet create, access check, revoke), flipdesk-google-photos.ts:106/126/250/382/434/479, flipdesk-sheets.ts:87 (with redirect:'follow'), google-ads-client.ts:99/171/243. Scenario: a Google regional slowdown, the 5-minute sheet-sync cron fans out per user, each hangs on a socket read, and requests pile up in the single Deno container until it stops answering /api/grade/* and /api/payments/* too.
acceptanceCriteria: SheetsClient's default fetchFn becomes fetchWithTimeout (google-sheets-api.ts:34) — that covers the largest block.
The six flipdesk-google.ts fetches and the rest of the table route through fetchWithTimeout.
A lint rule or test flags a bare fetch to an external host in services/edge-functions/src/.

google-sheets-api.ts:62-66 is an UNBOUNDED retry: the comment says 'one retry' but the code self-recurses on 429 with no attempt counter, no growth and no ceiling. Under project-level quota exhaustion this hammers Google every 2 seconds forever, per in-flight request, per replica. Route it through lib/retry.ts.
userStories.notes:
[P0][FlipDesk/Google] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The unbounded 429 retry is a ban risk; the missing timeouts are a whole-container availability risk including grading and payments. | [2026-08-01] Fixed. Re-verified every cited line and the audit was accurate: SheetsClient's fetchFn defaulted to bare fetch (google-sheets-api.ts:34) and ALL FOUR construction sites take the default, so every Sheets call in the codebase ran with no deadline. Confirmed the other 15 sites too (google-service-account.ts:144, flipdesk-google.ts x6, flipdesk-google-photos.ts x6, flipdesk-sheets.ts:87) plus google-ads-client.ts's four `fetchFn: typeof fetch = fetch` defaults.

AC1 + AC2 done via a new lib/google-fetch.ts exporting googleFetch (typeof fetch, 20s via fetchWithTimeout, matching the 20-25s the marketplace clients use). Every Google call site and every injectable fetchFn DEFAULT now points at it. Making it the default rather than something each call site reaches for is the point: the thing that gets forgotten is the thing that must not be optional.

AC4 done, and it was the worse half. The 429 path self-recursed with a flat 2s sleep, no counter, no growth, no ceiling. The comment said "one retry" and was true of the case the author had in mind - a quota BLIP does clear in 2s. Project-level quota exhaustion does not, and then it hammers Google every 2 seconds forever, per in-flight request, per replica. Now routed through lib/retry.ts: maxAttempts 3, baseDelayMs 2000, exponential with jitter, and Google's own Retry-After honored (converted seconds->ms onto the error, which is the shape retryAfterMs() reads) and capped at 30s. The throttle sits INSIDE the retried body on purpose - a retry is another request against the same per-minute quota and must take a slot.

AC3 done as tests/no-bare-fetch_test.ts, an ENUMERATION not a regex ban. 33 bare fetch sites remain in 27 files this story does not touch, so a blanket ban would mean either a red build or a suppression, and a suppressed guard is a deleted guard. Instead each remaining file is declared with its COUNT: a new bare fetch in an undeclared file fails, a new one in a declared file fails because the count moves, and fixing a file fails until its entry is deleted. The list can only shrink. Note circuit-breaker.ts's single call IS fetchWithTimeout's own implementation and is permanent.

THAT LIST IS THE REAL FINDING: 33 undeadlined external calls remain outside Google - agent-tools, apns, fcm, ebay-trading (3), gsc-client (2), keyword-research (2), content-webhook (2), openai-images, webhook-delivery, cloudflare-purge and more. Same container-exhaustion risk, different upstream. Worth its own story.

Also added tests/sheets-retry_test.ts - behavioural, not source assertions, because the COUNT is the fix and asserting "imports withRetry" would not catch a maxAttempts of Infinity. Covers: a permanent 429 stops at 3 attempts, the backoff grows and no single wait exceeds 30s, a 429 that clears still succeeds (bounding a retry is worthless if it stops retrying), a 404 is NOT retried (widening from 429-only must not start retrying permanent answers), and an uncapped Retry-After: 3600 is honored but clamped to 30s.

Verified: all 5 sheets-retry cases run in Node via esbuild bundle + a Deno.env shim (no Deno on this host); the enumeration guard simulated in Node against the real tree - undeclared/stale/mismatch all empty; the bare-fetch regex negative-verified on 9 cases (fetchWithTimeout(, googleFetch(, this.fetchFn(, deps.fetch(, prefetch(, commented-out forms all correctly excluded, `fetch (url)` correctly caught). tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, vitest 239 files / 3079 tests green. The Deno tests are unverified until a PR runs CI.

userStories.title: Concurrent token refresh disconnects sellers on providers that rotate refresh tokens
userStories.description: No advisory lock, mutex or single-flight guard exists in any token path (no pg_advisory, no FOR UPDATE, no in-flight promise map). The read-modify-write is check expiry, refresh, persist. Four connectors do this and all four persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, which proves rotation is expected: etsy-client.ts:392-396, whatnot-client.ts:347-350, depop-client.ts, flipdesk-google.ts:353-355. Scenario (Etsy, 1-hour tokens): a user opens the Marketplaces page while the sync cron fires; both see expiresAt - now < 60s (etsy-client.ts:368) and POST the same refresh token; Etsy rotates and invalidates the old one on first use; the second call gets 400 invalid_grant; isPermanentEtsyAuthFailure classifies 400 as PERMANENT (:243) so the handler sets is_active:false and stores a reconnect message (:410-416). The user is force-disconnected by a race, not a revocation. eBay is not exposed (its refresh token is not rotated).
acceptanceCriteria: A per-connection advisory lock (keyed on connection id) around refresh, so concurrent callers wait rather than racing.
invalid_grant immediately after a successful sibling refresh is treated as transient (re-read the row and retry once) rather than permanent.

refreshExpiringEtsyConnections (etsy-client.ts:467) scans on a 24-hour horizon but delegates to getEtsyAccessToken which only refreshes inside a 60-second window, so the cron decrypts every active connection every run and proactively refreshes nothing. Fix or delete it.
Confirm whether Etsy/Depop/Google actually invalidate the old token on rotation — that sets the real severity.
Audit prod for connections deactivated with an invalid_grant refresh_error and offer affected sellers a reconnect.

userStories.title: Etsy and Depop syncs discard every per-record error and report success
userStories.description: flipdesk-etsy.ts:274-278 and flipdesk-depop.ts:269-273 (plus the adapter copies at marketplace-adapters/etsy.ts:371-381 and depop.ts:329-339) loop over receipts calling handleEtsyReceiptEvent, which never throws and instead collects failures into res.errors (etsy-orders.ts:192,225; depop-orders.ts:167,200). res.errors is read nowhere. Every failed receipt is invisible and the sync returns ok:true. Neither loop has a per-record try/catch, so a throw at receipt 200 aborts 201-500, and since every retry restarts at offset=0 it hits the same poison record forever — a permanently stuck sync. Mitigating: neither uses a real fetch cursor so the next run replays the window and self-heals, but Etsy's window is capped at 20 pages x 50 = 1000 receipts (etsy-api.ts:525) so anything aging out before the retry is lost.
acceptanceCriteria: res.errors is propagated into the sync result and surfaced to the seller.
Per-record try/catch so one bad receipt cannot block the tail.
A record that fails repeatedly is quarantined rather than retried forever at the head of the queue.

etsy-api.ts:68-76, depop-api.ts:69-78 and whatnot-api.ts:53-60 have no 429 handling at all — fetch then throw on !ok, with no Retry-After, no backoff and no 429-vs-4xx distinction. Route them through lib/retry.ts. Shopify (shopify-graphql.ts:98-220) is the model to copy.

userStories.title: Marketplace webhooks have no freshness window and one debug flag disables all four
userStories.description: Verification itself is correct everywhere — all four receivers read the raw body, verify before any DB write, fail closed when the secret is missing, and use constant-time comparison (or asymmetric verify for eBay). Three residual gaps. (A) isDebugAllowed('WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG') is checked at flipdesk-webhooks.ts:123, :201, :493, :1229 and skips the whole verify block when true; lib/env.ts:82-85 returns false in production and edgeEnv() defaults to 'production' when unset, so a bare container fails closed — but any staging or preview with EDGE_ENV non-production and the flag on accepts unsigned requests on the account-deletion path (mass seller disconnect) and logs headers plus 2KB of body verbatim. (B) No replay or freshness check anywhere. All four rely on event-id dedupe which is skipped when the provider's id header is absent (:756, :389, :512) and FAILS OPEN on a DB error (:770, :400, :595, :1290). eBay's notification.publishDate is declared in the type at :744-745 and never read; Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At is never read. (C) fetchPublicKeyMaterial (ebay-notification-verify.ts:135-154) does getAppAccessToken plus a call to eBay's public_key/{kid} for any attacker-supplied kid, with no timeout and no negative cache (keyCache at :92 stores only successes), bounded only by the 600/60s limiter at main.ts:1025 — so an attacker can drive 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica and burn the app's API quota.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod. If it does, this is live.
A timestamp freshness window (+/- 5 min) on the eBay and Shopify receivers using the headers already sent.
Dedupe fails CLOSED on a DB error rather than open.
Negative cache plus a timeout on the eBay public-key fetch.

Depop's header names (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256 at :495-496, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id at :512) are unconfirmed guesses. The signature failure mode is safe (401) but the dedupe failure mode is SILENT — if Depop uses neither header, every delivery is reprocessed with no error. Confirm and narrow, including the hex-or-base64 hedge at depop-api.ts:488-491.

userStories.title: Admin SPA writes ai_prompt_versions straight to Postgres, bypassing scope, step-up and the edge audit
userStories.description: 00003_admin_tables.sql:143-161 grants any is_admin() caller full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on ai_prompt_versions via RLS, and no later migration through 00480 tightens it. The admin SPA uses that grant directly: src/pages/admin/ai-models.tsx:559-563 INSERT, :666-669 DELETE, :708-711 UPDATE prompt_text, :629-632 UPDATE is_active:false. So an admin whose grading:review scope was deliberately revoked can still open /admin/ai-models and rewrite the prompt_text of the LIVE active grading prompt — biasing every grade the platform issues — or delete the version row. The edge guard (admin-grading.ts:150), the step-up on activate (:518-520) and the whole shadow/eval/canary lifecycle are all routed around. This falsifies the premise stated in lib/admin-scope-map.ts:11-13 that revoking a scope closes the surface.
acceptanceCriteria: The RLS write policies on ai_prompt_versions are narrowed to service_role, so the table is only mutable through the edge.
The admin SPA's four direct writes go through the existing edge routes, which already carry the scope and step-up checks.
Sweep every other admin SPA surface for direct-to-Postgres writes on tables the edge also guards, and close the same way.
A test asserts no admin page mutates a scope-guarded table through the browser client.
userStories.notes:
[P0][Admin/Security] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Admin-class, not user-class: no path was found where a normal user can do anything admin. The role model itself is sound. | [2026-08-01] Fixed. Re-verified every claim and the audit was accurate: 00003_admin_tables.sql:143-161 grants any is_admin() caller SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on ai_prompt_versions, and none of the nine later migrations touching that table narrows it. The SPA used the grant directly at ai-models.tsx:560 (insert), :630 (is_active:false), :667 (delete) and :709 (prompt_text). The router scope guard is admin-grading.ts:150 and the step-up is on activate only, so all four were routed around.

AC1 done: migration 00510_prompt_versions_service_role_writes.sql drops the three write policies and creates NO replacement. With RLS on and no permissive policy for a command, that command is denied for every non-service role; the edge's service-role client bypasses RLS, which is how writes still work. The SELECT policy is deliberately KEPT - the admin UI still lists prompts directly and there is no reason to break that. EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00510 in the same commit, self-record footer present, PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md entry added.

MIGRATION ORDER IS UNUSUAL AND MATTERS: this one removes a capability the frontend uses, so the safe sequence is frontend deploy -> edge redeploy -> SQL, the OPPOSITE of the normal order. Applying the SQL against an old frontend build breaks prompt create/edit/delete with an RLS error; deploying the frontend before the edge makes the new edit/delete buttons 404 until PATCH and DELETE /prompts/:id exist. Written up in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md.

AC2 done. Two new edge routes were needed - the existing router had create, activate and deactivate but nothing for edit or delete. PATCH /prompts/:id and DELETE /prompts/:id, both under the same grading:review guard, both auditing. They also enforce what a direct write never could: an ACTIVE version's prompt_text is IMMUTABLE (409, deactivate or make a new version) and an ACTIVE version cannot be deleted (409 - deleting it silently reverts grading to the code default with nothing in the change log explaining why the numbers moved). All four SPA writes now go through a small promptsApi() helper.

Two side findings while repointing: the old create never sent a `stage`, so every prompt made in this UI silently became 'composite' (the column default) whatever it was written for - the dialog now has a stage selector because the edge route requires one. And the old deactivate skipped invalidatePromptCache(), so every replica kept serving the prompt the admin had just turned off until its cache expired.

AC3 done as a sweep, and it found three more. Declared in the new guard with reasons rather than silently fixed or silently ignored:
- users.plan written directly from user-detail.tsx - an admin granting entitlement with NO billing:write scope check and NO step-up. The nearest edge route (POST /admin/billing/users/:id/change-plan) is not equivalent: it drives flipdesk_plan through Stripe and lets the webhook write the row, and nothing server-side writes users.plan at all. Needs a new route. FILED AS US-2376 [P1] with submissions.status.
- submissions.status written directly from submissions.tsx - no edge equivalent exists. Same story.
- admin_audit_log inserted directly from three admin pages - that is US-2349's whole subject (the log is forgeable), not a side effect of this one.

AC4 done as src/test/admin-direct-write-guard.test.ts - an ENUMERATION, not a ban, because direct READS are fine and direct writes to tables the edge does not guard are fine, so a blanket rule would be wrong as often as right. Each remaining direct write is declared with its reason; a new one fails until declared, a closed one fails until its entry is deleted. Plus a named assertion that ai_prompt_versions specifically has zero browser writes, and one that the migration drops exactly the three write policies and NOT the read policy.

Verified: negative-verified the guard by reintroducing a direct ai_prompt_versions update - 2 of 5 tests went red, then reverted. tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, vitest 240 files / 3084 tests green, npm run build + prerender clean. The Deno-side edge routes are unverified until a PR runs CI.

userStories.title: Impersonation is unbounded, unmarked, non-revocable, and allows account deletion as the user
userStories.description: admin-impersonation.ts:43-132 gets the entry right: super_admin only (:44), users:role scope (:38), fresh step-up (:49), self and privileged targets refused (:54, :68-73), start audited (:116). Everything after the token is minted is open. No time limit — generateLink type magiclink (:90) yields a normal Supabase session for the target, access token plus long-lived refresh token, in the admin's browser, with no cap anywhere. No revocation on stop — src/lib/impersonation.ts:126-129 only redeems the resume token and never calls auth.admin.signOut(targetId), so a copied refresh token outlives the session. No marker — there is no impersonated_by claim and no server-side active-impersonation row, so every request made while impersonating is indistinguishable from the real user's. And destructive actions are fully available: POST /api/account/delete's only server-side control is the confirm string (account.ts:390); the password re-auth at :625-631 is client-side only. A super_admin can impersonate a disputing customer, cancel their subscription and delete their account, and every downstream record shows the customer did it.
acceptanceCriteria: A hard maximum impersonation duration, enforced server-side.
Stopping impersonation revokes the target's sessions.

userStories.title: High-impact admin routes have no step-up: feature flags, money, grade voiding, agent execution
userStories.description: Step-up coverage is inconsistent in a way that inverts the risk ordering. PUT /api/admin/flags (admin-flags.ts:68) toggles ANY feature flag with only the router-wide ops:write, while the far less impactful PUT /:key/rule (:210) requires both super_admin and step-up; a second unguarded write into the same table exists at admin-waitlist.ts:235. POST /claims/:id/resolve (admin-guarantee-pool.ts:89) draws the pool and grants reward credit with no step-up and no super_admin, the only money-moving route in the service without step-up. POST /:id/approve (admin-claims.ts:473) refunds the grading fee and grants a free re-grade with no step-up, and sits under grading:review, so revoking billing:write does not stop an admin paying claims. POST /regrade (admin-bulk.ts:380) supersedes up to 200 issued grade reports with no step-up while its siblings /credits:260 and /suspend:316 both have it. POST /retry with kind grading (admin-jobs.ts:387) voids grades under ops:write without ever holding grading:review. The guard now carries an 11-case --self-test that runs on EVERY invocation (not behind a flag - an opt-in test for a guard is back where it started), proving each rule fires and each exemption stays quiet. DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT OF SCOPE with the reason recorded in the file: consignment/ConsignorPicker.kt (splitHint) and marketplaces/ListingCard.kt (quantityText, contentDescription) build sentences in plain non-composable functions that unit tests assert on by exact wording; their Compose literals ARE converted, but scoping them would mean the guard called a file clean while shipped English sat one call deeper. Kotlin could not be compiled here (the Android Gradle plugin does not resolve in this container) - Android CI is the gate. | Progress 2026-07-31 third pass - AC1 and AC2 are now MET; AC3 (a second language) is the only thing outstanding. SCOPE is 91 of 91 Compose files under app/src/main, up from 39 at the start of the session; ~180 more literals moved to res/values/strings.xml across seven commits. AC2 held throughout: SyncStatusBar, ConsignmentReportScreen, PayoutReconciliationScreen, DisputeSheet, SalesScreen, CompsSection and ListingPerformanceScreen all hand-rolled plurals as \${if (n == 1) \"\" else \"s\"} and are now <plurals>; ListingPerformanceScreen needed three of them (views / watchers / impressions each agree independently) so its metrics line is assembled in a small @Composable helper rather than inside buildString. THE GUARD WAS REWRITTEN, not extended again. Four positional rules had each lost to ordinary Kotlin in turn - Text(\"x\"), then ktlint's wrapped form, then if/else, then the same conditional on one line - and Text(band.days?.let { \"Last \$it days\" } ?: \"Any time\") would have been the fifth. It now finds the sink's argument list, reads to its close, and judges each LITERAL rather than its position: copy needs internal whitespace, or an initial capital, or a template hole with words around it and no path punctuation. That excludes separators, routes, when-keys, MIME types, animation labels and character counters; the documented false negative is lowercase one-word copy with no hole. Seven live strings fell out of the rewrite in files already marked converted, which is the point. Also added: a declared escape hatch (// no-bare-strings: <reason>) for a wire value in a default argument, @Preview bodies exempt by region, per-line dedupe, Badge/SectionLabel/SectionPlaceholder as sinks, and a 24-case --self-test that runs on EVERY invocation rather than behind a flag. They return the DECISION now (a sealed SplitHint, a @StringRes id) with @Composable wrappers resolving it, so the tests assert the choice and its numbers instead of English. Under run-sdk.mjs's descending sort the Android epic would never be picked at all; under ascending, nothing positive ever would. Only one can be right and the backlog currently encodes both. Raised with the user four times across loop iterations without an answer; recorded here so it stops being conversational and starts being a decision with an owner. userStories.title: Listings-page inline edits write their optimistic update to a cache the page never reads
userStories.description: src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx runs its own query under ["items_full","listings",user.id] (:695 — deliberately distinct, because it projects a narrower LISTINGS_COLUMNS subset). All four inline-edit paths — updateTracking (:1316), markDelivered (:1345), updateListingPrice (:1397) and patchItemColumn (:1430) — write their optimistic patch to ["items_full",user.id] instead. That is a different cache entry, so the optimistic UI never appears on the page doing the editing. Two of the four (updateTracking, updateListingPrice) also have NO success invalidation, so the edited value stays stale on screen behind a success toast until the query goes stale on its own — 15 minutes off the Active tab. The rollback halves are wrong in the same way and worse in kind: they capture prev = items (the listings-projected array) and write it into the FULL cache key, so before US-2188 a failed edit here replaced the shared full-row cache with narrower rows for pipeline/overview/prep. patchItemColumn is commented as 'mirrored optimistically into the items_full cache', which is the intent — the key is simply wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: All four optimistic writes and all four rollbacks target the page own query key, not the bare ["items_full", user.id]
The key is derived from one shared definition rather than re-spelled at nine call sites, so it cannot drift again
updateTracking and updateListingPrice invalidate on success like the other two, so the row reconciles with the server rather than relying on the optimistic value
A guard test fails if a setQueryData in listings.tsx targets a key the page does not read
userStories.notes: Found 2026-07-31 while auditing items_full readers for US-2188. The optimistic-write half has been user-visible the whole time. | DONE 2026-07-31, same session it was found. AC1+AC2: one definition — const listingsItemsKey = ["items_full","listings",user?.id] — now backs the page query and all EIGHT setQueryData calls (4 optimistic writes + 4 rollbacks) that previously hand-spelled the bare full-row key. AC3: updateTracking and updateListingPrice now invalidate ["items_full"] on success like markDelivered and patchItemColumn already did; without it an optimistic value the server had rejected kept reading as saved until the query went stale, up to 15 minutes off the Active tab, and for updateListingPrice that value is a price. userStories.title: iOS AutoLister bulk flow: no import progress, a 90s upload cap that big batches always blow, and grouping the seller cannot drive
userStories.description: The iOS AutoLister batch flow breaks down at exactly the size it exists for. (1) Import ran one photo per await (loadImage -> compress -> dHash, strictly serial) behind a single isImporting flag, and the skeleton only rendered when the batch was EMPTY — so adding to an existing batch showed nothing at all, and a 200-photo import was minutes of frozen screen with no count and no way to stop. (2) PHPickerResult.loadImage() returns a UIImage, which carries no EXIF, and the picker is deliberately configured without a photoLibrary (US-1013) so assetIdentifier — and therefore the PHAsset creation-date lookup — is always nil. Every imported photo was stamped .now: capture-time clustering had nothing to work with, the Date-taken sort was meaningless, and auto-group was guessing from filenames alone. (3) importPicks called ingest, which called regroupAll, so the app auto-grouped the whole batch before the seller saw a single photo; the only way to fix a wrong boundary was a per-photo context menu, one photo at a time. The web (src/pages/flipdesk/autolister.tsx) has had selection-driven grouping since US-1550 — photos land ungrouped, you select and hit New group from selected — and iOS never got it. (4) AutoListerGenerator.waitForUploads used a flat 90s wall-clock deadline for the WHOLE batch while uploads run one at a time at roughly a second each, so any batch past ~90 photos ran out the clock while uploading perfectly well and landed on the Uploads still finishing screen, with only item-level progress (which sits unmoved for minutes) to show for it.
acceptanceCriteria: Import publishes per-photo progress (N of M) with a Stop that keeps everything already imported, both full-screen for the first import and inline when adding to a batch
Import decodes/compresses/hashes with bounded concurrency while preserving pick order, and reports capped, failed and stopped picks in one notice instead of an all-or-nothing error
Imported photos carry their real capture time, read from the file EXIF, with no extra photo-library permission
Imported photos land ungrouped; nothing is grouped until the seller acts

The ungrouped pool is a selection grid sorted by file name, date taken, shooting order or import order: tap to select, select-through-here for a range, Group makes those photos one item and drops them from the grid
Auto-group, Group every N and AI group act on the ungrouped pool only and leave hand-made items alone; Regroup everything (destructive) is behind a menu
Any item can be ungrouped back to the grid without discarding photos
Generate warns when photos are still ungrouped, because ungrouped photos are not listed
The upload wait is bounded by a no-progress stall, not by total batch time, and shows photo-level progress
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS/AutoLister] Reported 2026-07-31 as "bulk upload is clunky and/or broken and the auto group is horrendous". | DONE 2026-07-31. AC1+AC2: AutoListerReviewModel.importPicks now walks the picks in slices of importConcurrency=3 through a task group, re-orders each slice by pick position (import order is the .upload sort and every other sort tiebreaker), publishes ImportProgress(done,total) per slice, ingests each slice as it lands so the grid fills live, and honours cancelImport() between slices; importNotice() folds capped/failed/stopped counts into one banner. AC3: new ImageCaptureDate reads DateTimeOriginal (then DateTimeDigitized, then TIFF DateTime, honouring OffsetTime) out of the raw bytes via PHPickerResult.loadImageWithCaptureDate(), which loads a data representation instead of a UIImage — no library permission, EXIF intact. AC4+AC5: ingest() no longer regroups; new AutoListerSelectionGrid renders the pool as a LazyVGrid with toggleSelection/selectRange/selectAllUngrouped and a bottom bar that swaps to Group N photos as one item while a selection is live. Group order follows the grid, not tap order. AC6: autoGroupUngrouped() clusters only the pool and appends, regroupAll() is the destructive one and moved behind the toolbar More menu. AC7: ungroupGroup() returns photos to the pool in import order. AC8: the generate bar warns on ungrouped photos. AC9: AutoListerGenerator.waitForUploads switched from a 90s batch deadline to a 90s no-progress stall window and publishes UploadProgress (photos + items), which AutoListerQueueView shows as a determinate bar. ungroupedSorted is now cached on (mode, pool, photoRevision) because the grid recomputes it on every selection tap and the provenance compare parses filenames with a regex. iOS cannot be built on this box (Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only) — iOS CI is the gate.

userStories.title: AutoLister has no phone → desktop handoff: a batch shot on mobile can only be finished on mobile
userStories.description: The desktop AutoLister keeps its whole working session — staged photos plus grouping — in the BROWSER (IndexedDB via src/lib/autolister-session-idb.ts, localStorage fallback, autolister.tsx:566-916). Nothing about a session exists server-side, so there was no shelf for one device to leave work on for another. On iOS the batch was even more local: photos live in AutoListerReviewModel memory and reach the server only when Generate runs the create-items → upload → classify → generate pipeline. The result: the phone, which is where the camera is, could not be used as a capture device. You either finished the entire job — grouping, review, AI spend — on a 6-inch screen, or you re-shot the batch on the desktop. Generated drafts DO already cross over (iOS Generate writes listings rows with a batch_id, which is exactly what the desktop autolister-drafts cockpit reads), but that is after the AI has run and the money is spent; the pre-generation review state had no path at all.
acceptanceCriteria: A server-side handoff record holds a batch pre-generation: the staged photo list and the grouping, owned by one tenant
The phone can upload a whole batch to the shared staging folder and park it without running any AI or creating any inventory rows
Ungrouped photos travel with the handoff, not just the grouped ones — the desktop grid is where the job gets finished
A fabricated capture time never travels; only a real EXIF time does, so desktop auto-grouping does not read a burst that never happened
The desktop AutoLister shows what is waiting, loads it into the current session by APPENDING (never replacing what is on screen), and claims it so it stops being offered
Discarding a handoff on the desktop also deletes its staged objects
Every handoff route is tenant-scoped and every storage path is checked against the caller's own _staging prefix, with tenant-isolation cases proving it
After a successful send the phone offers to clear the batch, so the same photos cannot be generated twice
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS+Web/AutoLister] Asked for 2026-07-31: "upload from mobile then continue on desktop in the autolister draft area". userStories.title: npm run verify is not CI parity: two affiliate tests fail locally and pass in CI on an env var only CI sets
userStories.description: CLAUDE.md sells 'npm run verify' as mirroring GitHub Actions, and it does not. .github/workflows/ci.yml declares a workflow-level env block (VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://api.gradethread.com, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, VITE_EDGE_API_URL=https://functions.gradethread.com). Nothing supplies those locally. vitest.config.ts injects only VITE_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321 and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, and 'localhost' does not start with 'api.', so edge-api.ts deriveFromSupabase() returns null and edgeApiUrl() throws. postClickPing swallows that throw by design, so no fetch goes out and src/test/cert-ssr-attribution-capture.test.ts 'the parked click ping' loses two cases: 'is flushed by the first SPA load' and 'sends once, even if the visitor keeps browsing'. CI is green on the same commit because its env block happens to satisfy the derivation. A developer following the documented workflow sees a red suite on a commit CI calls clean, which trains people to push --no-verify - and --no-verify is exactly what CI's own comments (US-2038) say already let a red scripts/ suite sit on main for 15 commits.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run verify and GitHub Actions agree on the same commit: no test passes in one and fails in the other because of ambient VITE_* config
The VITE_* values CI declares have a single source both CI and local verify read, rather than being restated in ci.yml only
A test that needs a resolvable edge API URL states that itself (stub or per-file env) instead of depending on what the runner happens to export
A guard fails if ci.yml's env block and the local source drift apart again
userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/CI] Found 2026-07-31 while running npm run verify for US-2371. Reproduced both ways: locally 'npx vitest run src/test/cert-ssr-attribution-capture.test.ts' gives 2 failed | 13 passed, and the same commit (1ac16d5, the base of this branch) is a green CI run. Root cause chain: ci.yml env block sets VITE_EDGE_API_URL -> src/lib/edge-api.ts RAW is truthy -> edgeApiUrl() returns; locally RAW is unset and deriveFromSupabase() sees hostname 'localhost' which fails the url.hostname.startsWith('api.') test -> edgeApiUrl() throws the 'Edge API URL is not configured' error -> src/lib/affiliate.ts postClickPing catches it and returns without calling fetch -> the two assertions on fetchSpy.toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) fail. NOT a product bug: the shipped code is correct in both environments, and nothing about affiliate click attribution is broken in prod. It is a parity bug in the harness, and the cheapest fix is probably to move the three VITE_* values into vitest.config.ts's test.env (which already exists and already sets two of them) so both runners read one source, with a small assertion that ci.yml's env block matches it. Same defect class as the US-2038 note in ci.yml. | Done 2026-08-01. AC2: NEW scripts/lib/ci-env.ts exports CI_VITE_ENV (the three placeholder VITE_* values) + CI_ENV_WORKFLOWS; vitest.config.ts's test.env is now `{ ...CI_VITE_ENV }` instead of its own localhost:54321 pair, so both runners read one object. The workflow env: blocks stay literal (Actions can't import a module for a workflow-level env), but all three now carry a comment naming the source file. AC1: the two src/test/cert-ssr-attribution-capture.test.ts 'parked click ping' cases pass locally — full suite 2917 passed / 0 failed where the same tree at HEAD~ gives 2 failed, reproduced twice each way. AC4: NEW src/test/ci-env-parity.test.ts asserts each of ci.yml / indexnow.yml / lighthouse.yml declares EXACTLY CI_VITE_ENV (equality both ways, so an extra key is drift too), that import.meta.env carries the same values at runtime, that VITE_SUPABASE_URL still satisfies edge-api.ts's api.->functions. derivation (the property that actually broke, not the string), and that no value has JWT shape. Proven to fail: flipping VITE_EDGE_API_URL in ci.yml turns the guard red. AC3: the cert-ssr test now vi.mock's @/lib/edge-api to a fixed URL, so it states its own dependency rather than inheriting the runner's — postClickPing swallows an unresolvable URL by design, so that inheritance failed silently. FOUND AND FIXED WHILE HERE (a latent flake, not the reported bug): once the new test file changed worker packing, the real web-vitals library's onCLS/onINP timers began outliving jsdom teardown and crashing the run with 'ReferenceError: self is not defined', blamed on whichever unrelated file was executing (analytics.test.ts and autolister-telemetry.test.ts on different runs). userStories.title: Admin SPA writes users.plan straight to Postgres, with no billing scope and no step-up
userStories.description: Found by the US-2348 sweep. src/pages/admin/user-detail.tsx handlePlanChange does supabase.from("users").update({ plan }) directly from the browser. RLS lets any is_admin() caller do it, so an admin whose billing:write scope was deliberately revoked can still grant any account any plan, and no MFA step-up is asked for. The nearest edge route, POST /api/admin/billing/users/:id/change-plan, is NOT an equivalent: it drives flipdesk_plan through Stripe and lets the webhook write the row. Nothing server-side writes users.plan at all, so this needs a new route rather than a repointed call. Same sweep also found src/pages/admin/submissions.tsx marking a submission failed with a direct update and no edge equivalent. Both are declared in src/test/admin-direct-write-guard.test.ts DECLARED with their reasons; closing them means deleting those entries.
acceptanceCriteria: A new edge route owns the users.plan change, carrying the billing:write scope, an MFA step-up and an audit row — matching change-plan's posture.
user-detail.tsx calls it instead of writing the row, and its DECLARED entry in admin-direct-write-guard.test.ts is deleted.
The same for submissions.tsx marking a submission failed.
The RLS write grants on users.plan and submissions.status are narrowed so the browser client cannot write them at all — the SPA fix alone is cosmetic while the grant stands.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-08-01. PREMISE CORRECTION FIRST, because it changes what the bug was: the story says "RLS lets any is_admin() caller do it". It does not. 00006 grants admins SELECT on public.users only, and there is no admin UPDATE policy on public.users or public.submissions at all. So both browser writes matched ZERO rows, PostgREST returned no error for a zero-row update, and the SPA toasted success and wrote an admin_audit_log row claiming a change that never happened. The defect was worse than described: not an over-broad grant, but two admin controls that silently did nothing while reporting success and forging their own audit trail. AC1: new POST /api/admin/users/:id/plan in routes/admin-users.ts, carrying requireScope("billing:write") (granting a plan is granting entitlement, so it belongs to the same scope as the Stripe path), requireStepUp as the first statement in the handler before any lookup, an ASSIGNABLE_PLANS allowlist pinned to the public.user_plan enum (an unlisted value would be a 500 from Postgres instead of a 400 from us), and a writeAuditLog with before/after — the prior plan is what makes the row reviewable. It deliberately does NOT touch Stripe; details.stripe_synced=false records that this is a manual grant so a later reconciliation can find it. No path collision with admin-billing's /users/:id/change-plan. AC2: user-detail.tsx calls the route, handles 403 + code STEP_UP_REQUIRED by opening MfaStepUpDialog and retrying, and no longer writes admin_audit_log from the browser. AC3: new POST /api/admin/grading/submissions/:id/mark-failed. Found while writing it: the browser version did 1 of the 3 steps the grading pipeline's own failure path does — it flipped status and stopped, leaving the customer CHARGED for a grade they never got and the FlipDesk link stuck. Rather than re-implement, the fail+refund was extracted from the poison-orphan sweep into lib/stuck-submissions.ts failUngradedSubmission(), and defaultStuckStore.failAndRefund now delegates to it, so the admin button and the sweep are literally the same code (same shape as lib/cross-push.ts in US-2156). The UPDATE re-asserts status='processing' as its concurrency claim: a grade that lands in the race window fails the match and no charge is reversed. Route 409s on any non-processing status so a completed grade can't be destroyed. AC4: split. users.plan needed no migration — there was never a grant to narrow. submissions.status did, so 00511_submissions_protected_columns_guard.sql adds a BEFORE UPDATE trigger freezing 13 lifecycle/billing columns (status, payment_status, service_tier, authenticity_addon, refunded_at, flagged, flag_reason, moderation_status, grading_started_at, grading_lease_until, grading_attempts, superseded_at, superseded_by_submission_id) against auth.role()='authenticated', with a short-circuit so the service role and the trigger-less paths are untouched. HELD, not pushed. Deleted 4 DECLARED entries from src/test/admin-direct-write-guard.test.ts (both table writes plus both admin_audit_log inserts) and added 5 new cases pinning the replacements. GOTCHA worth keeping: my own explanatory comment quoting the old supabase.from("users").update({ plan }) call re-tripped the scanner — the guard is textual, so prose that looks like the write reads as the write. Verification: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, deno lint/check clean, 41 Deno tests pass (incl. a new admin-plan-and-mark-failed_test.ts), 1574 vitest pass. 00511 was applied to a THROWAWAY local stack from zero and exercised column by column with request.jwt.claims role switching. The load-bearing proof against the 00076 class (a guard trigger naming a column that does not exist raises 42703 on EVERY update of the table, at runtime, and 00076 broke all user writes that way until 00331): a title-only UPDATE SUCCEEDED, which forces the whole OR-chain to evaluate, proving all 13 NEW.<field> references resolve. Owner updates to each frozen column raised; a service-role update to status='failed' succeeded. Two of the checks looked like false passes until I noticed IS DISTINCT FROM was correctly false because the values already matched the defaults — re-seeded the row and they raised. No web, iOS or Android client writes public.submissions directly, so nothing breaks. ALSO FOUND, filed as US-2377: adminBillingRoutes.use("*", requireScope("billing:write")) mounted at the bare /api/admin prefix becomes a plain ALL /api/admin/* on the parent router under hono 4.3.7, so it gates the ENTIRE admin surface. Masked today only because both admin roles hold the scope by default.

userStories.title: admin-billing's use("*") scope guard leaks onto the whole /api/admin surface
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-01 while adding the US-2376 plan route. services/edge-functions/src/routes/admin-billing.ts calls adminBillingRoutes.use("*", requireScope("billing:write")). main.ts:1186 mounts that router at the BARE /api/admin prefix (not /api/admin/billing), and under hono 4.3.7 app.route() rewrites a sub-app's use("*") into a plain wildcard on the PARENT router — so it registers as ALL /api/admin/* and runs before every other admin router, not just the billing ones. An admin whose billing:write scope was deliberately revoked would get 403 on the entire admin surface: users, grading, moderation, everything. This is masked today only because admin and super_admin both hold billing:write by default, so nobody has ever hit it — which is exactly why it will surface the first time a narrower admin role is created, and it will look like a broken login rather than a scope bug. Proven with real hono 4.3.7 route-table output, not inferred from the docs.
acceptanceCriteria: requireScope("billing:write") applies to the admin-billing routes only; a request to another admin router is unaffected by it.
The URLs do not change — the fix is where the guard is attached, not what the paths are.
A test asserts the isolation directly, so a future use("*") on any router mounted at a shared prefix fails rather than silently widening.
Every other router mounted at a shared prefix is checked for the same pattern.
userStories.notes: [P1][Edge/RBAC] Least-risk fix that preserves URLs: drop the use("*") and pass requireScope("billing:write") as a per-route middleware argument on each adminBillingRoutes registration — the same shape admin-users.ts already uses. Do NOT 'fix' it by changing the mount prefix to /api/admin/billing; the billing routes' own paths already include their segments, so that would move every URL. Related: US-2376 added the first per-route requireScope on admin-users. | Done 2026-08-01. Reproduced on the real hono 4.3.7 before touching anything: a sub-app with use("*") mounted at /api/admin and a sibling mounted at /api/admin/users, and GET /api/admin/users/abc came back 403 from the sub-app's middleware. The route table shows why — app.route() copies the sub-app's entries onto the PARENT with the prefix prepended, so "*" becomes ALL /api/admin/*, which is a sibling matcher, not a scoping one. AC1+AC2: adminBillingRoutes.use("*", requireScope("billing:write")) is gone; all 21 billing routes now pass requireScope("billing:write") as a per-route argument. No path changed. AC4 turned up two more, both of which I fixed here rather than leaving the pattern half-cleaned: /api/admin/compliance is the parent mount of /api/admin/compliance/legal, so adminComplianceRoutes' moderation:write wildcard was ALSO being required of the legal routes, which ask for content:publish — anyone holding content:publish but not moderation:write was locked out of legal. 7 routes fixed. And /api/admin/marketplace is the parent of /api/admin/marketplace/pipeline; that leak was harmless (pipeline asks for the same marketplace:write) but it is the same pattern, so 9 routes fixed too. Every OTHER use("*") router — 40 of them — is mounted at a leaf prefix and is safe; they are deliberately left alone. AC3: new src/tests/router-mount-isolation_test.ts, three tests. The first pins hono's behavior itself with a live mini-app, so a version bump that changes it says so instead of leaving a rule nobody can justify. The second is the drift guard: it parses main.ts's mount table, computes which mounts are strict parents of another mount, resolves each parent router back to its routes/ file through the import, and fails if that file registers use("*"). Verified it actually fails — re-adding the billing wildcard produces "mounted at /api/admin, which is the parent of 54 other mount(s)". The third asserts all 21 billing routes still carry the scope, so "fixing" the leak can't quietly drop the guard. admin-scope-map.ts's mode "router" is redefined from "guarded with use(\"*\")" to "every route carries the scope" — the guarantee was always the point, the wildcard was just how it was written — and admin-scope-coverage_test.ts now accepts either shape (new allRoutesGuarded() helper) so the three fixed routers still satisfy their declared mode. Not a live outage today: only admin and super_admin reach /api/admin at all, and both hold billing:write in the seed. It would have surfaced the first time an operator narrowed a role in the scope editor, and it would have looked like a broken admin login rather than a scope change. ALSO FIXED here because it blocked verification: deno check src/main.ts was FAILING on main (TS7006 implicit any at webhooks.ts:1761, landed the same day in US-2293). clawbackApiOverage was hand-remapping charge.refunds.data before calling resolveRefundClawback; Stripe.Charge already satisfies that function's structural parameter — the credit-pack caller at :1579 passes it straight in — so the remap is deleted. Since deno test type-checks first, the ENTIRE edge suite had been unable to start. Also added the currency field (US-2292) to 6 ShopifyOrder fixtures in shopify-orders_test.ts, which was 6 more type errors. With those cleared the suite runs: 4988 passed, 9 pre-existing failures in 6 files, filed as US-2378. Confirmed those 9 are untouched by this change — identical 9 with the work stashed and unstashed.

userStories.title: The edge test suite is red on main: 6 type errors hid 9 failing drift-guards
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-01 while verifying US-2377. `deno check src/main.ts` and `deno test` (the two gates verify:edge and security.yml's deno-check job run) both failed on main. deno test type-checks before it runs anything, so the whole edge suite has been unable to START — a green-looking lane that executed zero tests. US-2377 cleared the 6 type errors (webhooks.ts:1761 implicit any from US-2293, and 6 ShopifyOrder fixtures in shopify-orders_test.ts missing the currency field US-2292 added). Underneath them the suite runs 4988 tests with 9 failures in 6 files: ebay-cleanup_test.ts x2 (US-2166 — the owned-listing load no longer selects listings.variations, and the platform guard is no longer inside the revise handler), plan-gate-coverage_test.ts (flipdesk-automations.ts puts an item live without gating the activeListings cap), sizing-chart-parity_test.ts x2 (00498 and 00499 are stale against their generators), tenant-isolation_test.ts (TEST_USER_A_AUTOMATION_RULE_ID gates a cross-tenant case but is neither seeded nor in KNOWN_UNSEEDED, so that case SKIPS in CI while the suite reports green), authenticity-references_test.ts (US-2218 bucket assertion), and no-bare-fetch_test.ts x2 which is a WINDOWS-ONLY test bug, not a product one: it builds a filesystem path from a URL and gets '/C:/Users/...', so it passes in CI and fails locally. Each failure is a different owner; they are grouped here because the type errors hid all of them at once.
acceptanceCriteria: `deno check src/main.ts` and `deno test` both pass in services/edge-functions, and npm run verify:edge is green.
Each of the 9 failures is resolved on its merits — the guard is right and the code is fixed, or the guard is wrong and is corrected with a written reason. None are deleted or skipped to go green.
no-bare-fetch_test.ts resolves its file paths platform-independently so it gives the same answer on Windows and Linux.
A red edge lane can no longer look green: a type error in the suite must fail loudly rather than silently preventing every test from running.
userStories.notes: [P1][Edge/CI] The tenant-isolation one is the worst of the nine and should be read first: it is the failure mode that guard was written to catch (a case that skips while the suite reports green), firing about itself. The two sizing-chart ones each name their own fix in the assertion message (deno run --allow-read --allow-write scripts/gen-sizing-chart-seed.mjs and scripts/gen-size-systems-migration.mjs) — but regenerating 00498/00499 rewrites APPLIED migrations, so check what actually drifted before regenerating; the answer may be to write a new migration instead. See US-2377 for how the type errors were cleared. | Done 2026-08-01. services/edge-functions now runs 5002 tests, 0 failures — deno lint, deno check and deno test all green, and npm run verify --edge passes all four checks. The nine split three ways once each was actually read. FIVE were Windows-only test bugs that pass in CI and fail on a developer's machine, which is the shape that trains people to push --no-verify: no-bare-fetch_test.ts x2 built a filesystem path from url.pathname and got "/C:/Users/..." (fixed by keeping URLs end to end — Deno.readDir and Deno.readTextFile both take a URL, and href arithmetic gives the same relative path either way); sizing-chart-parity x2 and authenticity-references x1 compared a generator's "\n" output against a .sql file git checks out with native line endings, so the whole file read as drifted (fixed by normalizing both sides — the guard is about the SQL, not about newlines). A SIXTH of the same family surfaced only once the suite could run at all: brand-style-coverage_test.ts died in scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs on the same url.pathname bug, now fileURLToPath. TWO were guards that had gone stale against refactors, where the product code was right: ebay-cleanup's owned-listing check still read flipdesk-listings.ts after loadOwnedListing moved into lib/listing-lifecycle.ts (repointed), and its revise-guard check sliced a fixed 4000 characters to mean "inside the handler" — the guard sat at 4024 because someone wrote a paragraph of comment above it, so the test called a present guard missing (now slices to the next route registration instead of a magic number). ONE was a real, correctly-diagnosed gap: plan-gate-coverage flagged flipdesk-automations.ts for calling markItemListed with no activeListings gate. Checked the claim rather than allow-listing on the code's say-so: loadOwnerListings selects .eq("platform","ebay").eq("listing_status","active"), so every listing a rule can touch is ALREADY live and already holds its slot, and the cap counts live ITEMS not listing rows. The markItemListed call is accounting repair for the eBay-active-but-status-drifted case; gating it would refuse to FIX the count for a seller sitting at their cap. Allow-listed with that written out, which is what the guard's own failure message asks for. ONE was the guard firing about itself, and it was right: TEST_USER_A_AUTOMATION_RULE_ID gated two cross-tenant cases but was never seeded, so both SKIPPED in CI while the suite reported green — exactly the failure that guard exists to catch. flipdesk_automation_rules is a plain row, so it is now SEEDED rather than classified as unseeded (seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts), with is_active false on purpose: an active fixture rule would be picked up by the hourly fan-out and start acting on the fixture inventory. AC4: deno check now covers src/tests/ as well as src/main.ts, in both scripts/verify.mjs and security.yml's deno-check job. deno test type-checks before it runs anything, so one bad type in a test file means zero of the ~5,000 assertions execute; checking the tree in the job whose purpose is types names the broken file instead of letting it read as a test failure. Costs ~8s. NOTHING was deleted or skipped to go green. The two sizing-chart assertions each named 'regenerate 00498/00499' as the fix — did NOT do that: those are APPLIED migrations, and regenerating them rewrites history to fix what turned out to be a line-ending artifact. See US-2377 for the six type errors that hid all of this.
